वैदान्तिक-व्याकरणम्

विचारसागरः — चतुर्थतरङ्गः · श्रीवासुदेवब्रह्मेन्द्रसरस्वती

उत्तमाधिकारिण उपदेशनिरूपणम्
विषयानुक्रमः · contents३२ विभागाः · क्लिक् → विस्तारः
शुभसन्ततेः राज्ञः, तत्त्वदृष्टिरिति, अदृष्टिरिति, तर्कदृष्टिरिति समाख्यातानां तत्पुत्राणां च कथा॥ १२२–१२५ ॥ज्ञानोपदेशः॥ १२८–१६८ ॥अत्राक्षेपसमाधानानि॥ १२९–१६८ ॥सुखविषयकाक्षेपसमाधानानि॥ १२९–१३२ ॥दुःखविषयकप्रश्नप्रत्युक्तयः॥ १३३–१६८ ॥शिष्यः स्वप्रश्नस्याशयं वर्णयति॥ १३८–१४३ ॥अन्यथाख्यातिः॥ १४१–१४२ ॥अख्यातिमतखण्डनम्॥ १४४–१४५ ॥सिद्धान्तिनोऽनिर्वचनीयख्यातिनिरूपणम्॥ १४६–१४९ ॥अत्राक्षेपसमाधानानि॥ १५०–१५९ ॥सर्पाभावात्सर्पज्ञानस्य कारणे लयरूपनिवृत्तिरिति समाधिः॥ १५३–१५५ ॥पूर्वप्रश्नस्योत्तरम्॥ १६१–१६२ ॥गुरुओरुत्तरम्॥ १६७–१६८ ॥पूर्वोपदिष्टविषये आक्षेपसमाधानानि॥ १६९–२२५ ॥जीवब्रह्मणोरभेदनिरूपणम्॥ १६९–१८८ ॥जीवब्रह्माभेदविषये तत्त्वदृष्टिप्रश्नः॥ १६९–१७१ ॥स्वरूपभेदाज्जीवब्रह्मणोरैक्यासङ्गतिरिति शङ्कायाः॥ १७२–१८५ ॥चतुर्विधाकाशवर्णनम्॥ १७३–१७६ ॥चैतन्यस्य चातुर्विध्यवर्णनम्॥ १७७–१८५ ॥जीवस्वरूपवर्णनम्॥ १७९–१८३ ॥बुद्धिप्रतिबिम्बितचैतन्यं जीवः॥ १७९–१८२ ॥``द्वा सपर्णा'' इति श्रुत्या जीवब्रह्मभेदः॥ १८६–१८८ ॥``अहं ब्रह्म'' इति ज्ञानं कस्येति विचारः॥ १८९–१९८ ॥प्रागुक्तप्रश्नस्योत्तरम्॥ १९०–१९६ ॥आभासस्य सप्तावस्थाः॥ १९०–१९१ ॥कूटस्थाभासयोः ``अहंवृत्तौ'' भानं किं॥ १९९–२१८ ॥पूर्वप्रश्नस्योत्तरम्॥ २००–२१८ ॥प्रमाणप्रसङ्गात्प्रत्यक्षानुमानशब्दोपमानार्थापत्त्यनुपलब्धिप्रमाणानि निरूप्यन्ते॥ २०४–२०९ ॥प्रमातृलक्षणम्॥ २१४–२१७ ॥इन्द्रियसम्बन्धं विना ``अहं ब्रह्म'' इति॥ २१९–२२३ ॥ब्रह्म न ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणां विषयः॥ २२०–२२२ ॥पूर्वोक्तप्रश्नस्योत्तरम्॥ २२४–२२५ ॥

About this edition
TextVicārasāgara — a Hindi Advaita-Vedānta prakaraṇa by Sādhu Niścaladāsa
Sanskrit + ṭippaṇīŚrī Vāsudeva Brahmendra Sarasvatī Svāmī — Sanskrit translation AND the ṭippaṇī (footnotes) are his
EditionFirst Edition, 1964 · Bhāratī Vijayam Press, Madras
Published byŚrī Vāsudeva Brahmendra Sarasvatī Svāmī Library Committee (grantha-koṣālaya-pālaka-samiti), Māyūram
EditorsBrahmaśrī P. Pañcāpageśa Śāstrī and Varahur Kalyāṇasundara Śāstrī
Dedicated toJagadguru Śaṅkarācārya of Śrī Kāñcī Kāmakoṭi Pīṭha — Śrī Candraśekharendra Sarasvatī (the Paramācārya)
By the command (śrīpāda-ādeśa) of the Kāñcī Paramācārya, Śrī Vāsudeva Brahmendra Sarasvatī Svāmī — who lived some twenty-five years continuously at Māyūra-kṣetra teaching dharma and brahma-vidyā and founded a library of Veda-śāstra-itihāsa-purāṇa — rendered Sādhu Niścaladāsa's Hindi Vicārasāgara into very simple Sanskrit and adorned it with his own ṭippaṇī; it was printed and published by his library committee (scan p5).
Dedicatory verse to Śrī Candraśekharendra Sarasvatī, the Kāñcī Paramācārya (editorial front-matter, not the original text)
संचारपूतानि दिगन्तराणि कुर्वन् विवृण्वन्निगमार्थतत्त्वम् ।
संशोधयन्सर्वजनान्तरङ्गं त्वं स्मारयस्यादिजगद्गुरु नः ॥
अविरतं परकार्यकृतां सतां मधुरिमातिशयेन वचोऽमृतम् ।
अपि च मानसमम्बुनिधिर्यशो विमलशारदचन्द्रचन्द्रिका ॥
Hallowing the far quarters of the earth by your travels, unfolding the true essence of the Vedas, and purifying the innermost being of all people — you, O foremost world-teacher (ādi-jagadguru), call [the first Śaṅkara] to our remembrance.
Among the holy who labour unceasingly for others’ good, your speech is nectar by its surpassing sweetness, your mind a fathomless ocean, and your fame the moonlight of the spotless autumn moon.

शुभसन्ततेः राज्ञः, तत्त्वदृष्टिरिति, अदृष्टिरिति, तर्कदृष्टिरिति समाख्यातानां तत्पुत्राणां च कथा॥ १२२–१२५ ॥
122 · शुभसन्ततेस्त्रैलोक्याधिपत्यं
शुभसन्ततिर्नाम कश्चन राजा लोकत्रयमनुशशास ।
A certain king named Śubhasantati ruled over the three worlds.
तस्यासंस्त्रयः पुत्राः - तत्त्वदृष्टिः, अदृष्टिः, तर्कदृष्टिरिति च विख्याताः, चतुःशास्त्रप्रवीणाश्च ।
He had three sons, known respectively as Tattvadṛṣṭi, Adṛṣṭi, and Tarkadṛṣṭi, who were well-versed in the four śāstras.
ते च क्रमेणास्मिन् ग्रन्थे चतुर्थपञ्चमषष्ठतरङ्गेषूत्तममध्यमकनिष्ठाधिकारित्वेन वर्ण्यन्ते ।
And they are described respectively in this treatise in the fourth, fifth, and sixth *taraṅga*s as aspirants of superior, intermediate, and inferior capacity.
राजा तु शुभसन्ततिः शैशवं क्रीडायाम्, यौवनं च स्त्रीभोगे विनियुञ्जानोऽपि स्वभुजबलेन लोकत्रयमपि न्याय्येन मार्गेणापालयत् ।
King Śubhasantati, however, even while spending his childhood in play and his youth in sensual pleasures with women, governed all three worlds righteously by the strength of his own arms.
123 · पुत्रेषु राज्यं समर्प्य शुभसन्ततेः प्रव्रजनं
तस्य राज्ञः कदाचित्स्वपूर्वपुण्यवशात् 1आत्मा अजो नित्यो निरतिशयानन्दस्वरूपश्च; ततोऽन्यत् सर्वं दुःखात्मकम् इति विवेक उदियाय ।
At one time, by the power of his past merits, discrimination arose in that king: 'The *ātman* is unborn, eternal, and of the nature of unsurpassed *ānanda*; everything other than It is of the nature of suffering.'
तदा सोऽचिन्तयत् - अहमात्मविचारं कुर्याम्, त्रयः पुत्रा मम लोकत्रयं पालयन्तु इति ।
Then he thought: 'I shall engage in inquiry into the *ātman*, and my three sons may rule the three worlds.'
ततो मन्त्रिद्वारा पुत्रान् स्वसमीपमानाय्य स्वस्य भोगे वैराग्यमेकान्ते रतिं च तेभ्यो निवेद्य राज्याधिकारमङ्गीकर्तुं तानाज्ञापयन्नेकैकस्मै एकैकं लोकं विभज्यादात् ।
Then, having summoned his sons to his presence through his minister, and having conveyed to them his dispassion for worldly pleasure and his longing for solitude, he commanded them to accept royal authority, and dividing the three worlds, gave one to each.
विभज्य राज्यादाने पुत्राणां मिथः कलहः, तन्मूलकतया प्रजानां दुःखं च भवेदिति मन्वानो राजा स्वयमेव स्वराज्यं पुत्रेभ्यो विभज्यादात् ।
Reflecting that if the kingdom were handed over undivided, there would be mutual dispute among the sons and consequently suffering for the subjects, the king himself partitioned his kingdom and gave it to his sons.
यत्र मानवो मृतः सन् परमेश्वरात्तारकमन्त्रोपदेशं लब्ध्वानायासेन मुक्तिं लभेत, यत्र च सर्वान्तर्यामी विश्वेश्वरः सदा सन्निहितः, यत्र चातिगभीरा गङ्गा उत्तरवाहिनी इति प्रथिता प्रवहति, तत्र काशीनगरे स्थित्वा स्वस्व2
Where a person dying receives the initiation of the liberating *tāraka-mantra* from the Supreme Lord and effortlessly attains liberation; where the inner ruler of all, Lord Viśveśvara, is ever present; and where the very deep Gaṅgā flows, famous as 'flowing northward' — residing there in the city of Kāśī, each...
टिप्पणी
1.
श्रुत्यादिषूपलभ्यमानजनकयाज्ञवल्क्याद्याख्यायिकावदियं गुरुशिष्यसंवादात्मिका कथा पुराणाद्यप्रसिद्धापि स्वबुद्धिमात्रेणापूर्वतया कल्प्यते ।
Just like the narratives of Janaka, Yājñavalkya, and others found in the Śrutis, this story consisting of a dialogue between teacher and disciple, though not famous in the Purāṇas and other works, is newly fashioned by the author's own intellect alone.
2.
काश्यां हि जन्तोः प्राणेषूत्क्रममाणेषु रुद्रस्तारकं ब्रह्म व्याचष्टे, येनासावमृतो भूत्वा मोक्षं लभते ।
For in Kāśī, when a creature's vital breaths are departing, Lord Rudra expounds the liberating Brahman, by which it becomes immortal and attains *mokṣa*.
यत्र कुत्रापि वा काश्यां मरणे स महेश्वरः । जन्तोर्दक्षिणकर्णे तु मत्तारं समुपादिशेत् ॥ इति श्रुत्यभिप्रायोऽत्र दर्शितः ।
'Wherever in Kāśī death occurs, that Maheśvara instructs my liberating mantra into the creature's right ear' — thus the purport of the Śruti is indicated here.
राज्यं पालयितुं पुत्रानादिदेश स राजा ।
That king instructed his sons to govern the kingdom.
पुनरपि स पुत्रानवोचत् - अयमपारः संसारो दुःखरूपः ।
Again he spoke to his sons: 'This boundless *saṃsāra* is of the nature of suffering.
पामरास्तु तं सुखरूपं मत्वा सांसारिकभोगाय धनमेवात्यादरेणोपार्जयन्ति ।
The ignorant, however, thinking it to be pleasant, eagerly amass only wealth for worldly enjoyment.
न तु मुक्त्यर्थमात्मविचारं कुर्वन्ति ।
They do not, however, perform inquiry into the *ātman* for the sake of liberation.
ईदृशपामरजनैः सह वासं विहायैकान्ते निजसुखलाभायाहं यतिष्ये इति ।
Giving up living with such vulgar people, I shall strive in solitude for the attainment of my own innate bliss.''
124 · पुत्राणामपि राज्यजिहासा
पितृवाक्यमिदं श्रुत्वा सद्युक्तिबुद्धियुक्तास्त्रयोऽपि पुत्रा एकान्ते सम्भूयैवं समालोचयन् - पितास्मान् संसारसागरे दुःखोदर्के पातयित्वा स्वयं ब्रह्मानन्दं प्रतिपित्सति ।
Having heard these words of their father, all three sons, endowed with sharp reasoning and intellect, gathered in private and deliberated thus: 'Father, casting us into the ocean of *saṃsāra* which yields only sorrow, desires to attain the bliss of Brahman for himself.
यस्मादात्मविचारासक्तोऽपारदुःखरूपत्वादखण्डमसपत्नमपि राज्यं पिता जिहासति, तस्माद्वयमपीदं राज्यमत्यन्तदुःखरूपं परित्यजेम इति ।
Since father, intent upon inquiry into the Self, desires to abandon even an undivided, unrivaled kingdom because it is of the nature of limitless suffering, therefore we too ought to renounce this kingdom which is fraught with utter suffering.'
125 · स्वगृहान्निर्गत्य त्रयाणां गुरूपसदनं
एवं निर्णीय ते त्रयोऽपि पुत्रा मुमुक्षवः शुभसन्ततिरिति पितुर्नामान्वर्थीकुर्वन्तः सद्गुरुमन्वेष्टुं राजगृहान्निर्ययुः ।
Having thus resolved, those three sons, desirous of liberation and making meaningful the name of their father Śubhasantati ('one with noble lineage'), departed from the royal palace in search of a true Guru.
अनेकदेशानटित्वान्ततस्ते गङ्गातटमेव प्राप्य तत्र विविक्ते देशेऽत्युन्नतशाखास्कन्धफलपलाशशालिभिर्वृक्षैर्निबिडिते वने कस्यचिद्वटतरोर्मूले चिन्मुद्रया जीवब्रह्मैक्यं स्वशिष्येभ्यो निर्दुष्टेभ्य उपदिशन्तं गुणातीतं श्रीसद्गुरुं ददृशुः ।
After wandering through many lands, reaching at last the bank of the Gaṅgā, in a solitary spot within a forest dense with trees bearing lofty branches, trunks, fruits, and foliage, they saw at the root of a certain banyan tree the venerable true Guru, who, transcending the guṇas, was instructing his blemishless disciples on the oneness of jīva and Brahman by means of the cinmudrā.
कैलासे महाभाण्डीरवटमूले सनकादिभ्यस्तत्त्वमुपदिशन्तं परमशिवं श्रीदक्षिणामूर्तिमिव ते तं विभाव्य, साष्टाङ्गं प्रणिपत्य, मोक्षेच्छया यथाविधि तं शरणं गतास्तन्निकटे षण्मासान् ब्रह्मचर्यमूषुः ।
Viewing him as Supreme Śiva in the form of Lord Dakṣiṇāmūrti expounding the Truth to Sanaka and the sages at the foot of the great Bhāṇḍīra banyan tree in Kailāsa, they prostrated with all eight limbs, took refuge in him duly with the desire for mokṣa, and lived in celibate discipleship near him for six months.
ततः श्रीसद्गुरुः प्रसन्नो भूत्वा मधुरया गिरा केन प्रयोजनेनागता यूयम्, के यूयम्, कुतो वात्रागमनम्, इति तान् पप्रच्छ ।
Then the venerable Guru, being pleased, asked them with a gentle voice: 'For what purpose have you come? Who are you? From where have you arrived here?'
तदा तत्त्वदृष्टिर्भ्रात्रोरिङ्गितज्ञः साञ्जलिपुटः सविनयं प्रत्यब्रवीत् ।
Then Tattvadṛṣṭi, understanding the intention of his two brothers, replied humbly with folded hands.
126 · तत्त्वदृष्टिर्गुरोरनुमतिं प्रार्थयते
हे भगवन् । वयं त्रयोऽपि भ्रातरः शुभसन्ततेः राज्ञः कुमाराः अज्ञाः अत्यन्तं शोच्याः निजस्वरूपजिज्ञासवो भवन्तं शरणं गताः ।
‹O venerable Lord! All three of us are brothers, sons of King Śubhasantati; being ignorant, deeply pitiable, and desirous of knowing our own essential nature, we have taken refuge in you.
भवान् हि कृपासमुद्रः कल्पतरुचिन्तामणिकामधेनुवच्च विराजते ।
You indeed are an ocean of compassion and shine like the wish-fulfilling tree, the wish-granting gem, and the celestial wish-yielding cow.
वयं तु दुःखवशंवदाः ।
We, however, are subservient to misery.
यद्याज्ञा दीयते1,2,3
If permission is granted—
टिप्पणी
1.
अङ्गुष्ठतर्जनीयोगश्चिन्मुद्रेति कीर्त्यते ।
The joining of the thumb and the index finger is called the cinmudrā.
इयं भद्रामुद्रा, लोपामुद्रा, तर्कमुद्रा, ज्ञानमुद्रा चेति कीर्त्यते ।
This is also designated as bhadrāmudrā, lopāmudrā, tarkamudrā, and jñānamudrā.
2.
स्तेयम्, हिंसा, अब्रह्मचर्यमित्येते त्रयः शरीरदोषाः ।
Theft, injury, and unchastity—these three are bodily defects.
अनृतम्, परनिन्दा, कटुभाषणम्, वृथालापः, इत्येते चत्वारो वाग्दोषाः ।
Untruth, slandering others, harsh words, and idle prattle—these four are vocal defects.
इच्छा, चिन्ता, बुद्धिमान्द्यमित्येते त्रयो मनोदोषाः ।
Longing, anxiety, and intellectual dullness—these three are mental defects.
नृसिंहतापिन्युपनिषत्प्रसिद्धा एते दश दोषाः ।
These ten blemishes are well known in the Nṛsiṁhatāpinī Upaniṣad.
3.
तृतीयतरङ्गोक्तविधानेन ।
[Meaning: 'properly'] according to the procedure stated in the third wave/chapter.
शिष्यःतर्ह्यस्मदभिप्रायं निवेदयामः इति तत्त्वदृष्टिः प्राह ।
'—then we shall state our intent,' thus spoke Tattvadṛṣṭi.
गुरुःहे शिष्य । श‍ृणु मे वचः ।
‹O disciple! Listen to my words.
गुरुःतच्छ्रवणेन त्वद्धृदयग्रन्थयः संशयाश्च समूलमुन्मूलिता भवेयुः, त्वं च परमानन्दं प्राप्नुयाः इति गुरुरवोचत् ।
By hearing that, the knots of your heart and your doubts will be uprooted from their very base, and you will attain supreme bliss,› said the Guru.
127 · मुमुक्षाभिव्यञ्जकस्तत्त्वदृष्टिप्रश्नः
श्रीगुरोः कारुण्यं ज्ञात्वा हृदयानन्दसन्दोहतुन्दिलः संस्तत्त्वदृष्टिः स्वाभिलषितकार्यं सिद्धमिति निश्चित्य सविनयं पप्रच्छ - हे भगवन् ।
Sensing the compassion of the revered Guru, filled with a flood of joy in his heart, and feeling assured that his desired goal was accomplished, Tattvadṛṣṭi asked humbly: 'O venerable Lord!
भवान् कृपानिधिः श्रीसदाशिवदक्षिणामूर्तिसमः सर्वज्ञः ।
You are a treasure of grace, equal to Lord Sadāśiva in the form of Dakṣiṇāmūrti, and omniscient.
वयं तु सर्वेऽज्ञाः जननमरणादिदुःखरूपसंसाराद्बिभीमः ।
We, on the other hand, are all ignorant, and are terrified of this saṁsāra which is of the nature of suffering such as birth and death.
अस्माकं तन्निवृत्तेः परमानन्दप्राप्तेश्चोपायो वक्तव्यः ।
The means for its cessation and for the attainment of supreme bliss must be told to us.
नानाप्रकारोपासनानि कर्माणि चानुष्ठितानि ।
Various kinds of meditations and ritual actions have already been performed by us.
नैवास्मदभिलषितार्थसिद्धिरभूत्, प्रत्युत संसारात्मकबन्ध एव दृढीभवति ।
Yet our desired goal was not accomplished at all; on the contrary, the bondage of saṁsāra only becomes firmer.
तस्मात् येनोपायान्तरेण वयं कृतार्था भवेम तमुपायमस्मान् शाधि भोः ।
Therefore, O Master, please instruct us in that other means by which we may become fulfilled!'
ज्ञानोपदेशः॥ १२८–१६८ ॥
128 · शिष्यस्य मोक्षेच्छा भ्रान्तिजन्येत्युपपादनपूर्वकं महावाक्योपदेशः
आत्यन्तिकदुःखनिवृत्तिः परमानन्दप्राप्तिश्च मोक्ष इति कथ्यते ।
Absolute cessation of misery and the attainment of supreme bliss is called mokṣa.
शिष्यस्य मोक्षेच्छां ज्ञात्वा गुरुस्तदुपायभूतं वेदान्तैकसमधिगम्यं ज्ञानमुपदिशति ।
Understanding the disciple's desire for liberation, the Guru imparts that knowledge which is knowable solely through Vedānta and serves as its means.
ज्ञानस्वरूपस्य नानाशास्त्रेषु नानाप्रकारेणोक्तत्वेऽपि जीवब्रह्मभेदनिवर्तकज्ञानस्यैव मोक्षसाधनत्वेन वेदेषु प्रतिपादितत्वात्तादृशमेव ज्ञानमुपदिशति -
Although the nature of knowledge has been described in various ways across different scriptures, because only that knowledge which removes the difference between jīva and Brahman is established in the Vedas as the means to liberation, he instructs precisely such knowledge:
हे शिष्य । परमानन्दावाप्तौ जननमरणादिदुःखरूपसंसारनिवृत्तौ च तवोत्पन्नेच्छा भ्रान्तिजन्येत्यवेहि ।
'O disciple, know that your desire for attaining supreme bliss and for the cessation of *saṃsāra*, which is of the nature of miseries like birth and death, is born of delusion.'
यतस्त्वं निसर्गत एव निरतिशयपरमानन्दस्वरूपोऽसि तस्मात्सदा परमानन्दस्वरूपेणैव सतस्तव पुनस्तत्प्राप्तीच्छा न युज्यते ।
'Because you are by nature the very unexcelled supreme ānanda, therefore, for you who are ever of the nature of supreme bliss, a desire to attain it again is inappropriate.'
यन्न प्राप्तं तल्लाभायैवोचितेच्छा ।
'A desire is proper only for obtaining that which has not already been attained.'
त्वत्स्वरूपं तु त्वया सर्वदा प्राप्तमेवेत्यतस्तत्प्राप्तये तव जायमानेच्छा भ्रममन्तरा न सङ्गच्छते ।
'Your true nature, however, is already ever attained by you; therefore, the desire arising in you to attain it makes no sense except as a delusion.'
किञ्च जननमरणादिरूपः संसारो यदि कदाचित् त्वय्यभूत्तदा तव तन्निवृत्तये इच्छोचिता भवेत् ।
'Furthermore, if *saṃsāra* in the form of birth and death had ever existed in you, then your desire for its cessation would be justified.'
वस्तुतस्तु स संसार ईषदपि कालत्रयेऽपि नास्त्येव त्वयि ।
'In reality, however, that *saṃsāra* does not exist in you in the least across the three periods of time.'
तस्मात्कालत्रयेऽप्यविद्यमानस्य संसारदुःखस्य निविवृत्सा ते भ्रममन्तरा न घटते ।
'Therefore, your desire to be rid of the misery of *saṃsāra*, which does not exist across past, present, and future, is untenable except through delusion.'
हे शिष्य त्वं तु जननमरणादिसर्वसंसारशून्यचिन्मात्रस्वरूपब्रह्मैवासि ।
'O disciple, you are indeed Brahman itself, whose nature is pure Consciousness devoid of all *saṃsāra* such as birth and death.'
तस्मान्मा स्मर कदापि जननमरणादिदुःखरूपं संसारम् ।
'Therefore, never dwell upon *saṃsāra*, which is merely misery consisting of birth, death, and so forth.'
अत्राक्षेपसमाधानानि॥ १२९–१६८ ॥
सुखविषयकाक्षेपसमाधानानि॥ १२९–१३२ ॥
129 · आत्मन आनन्दरूपत्वे विषयसम्बन्धादानन्दभानं नोचितमित्याक्षेपः
हे स्वामिन् । ममात्मा यदि नित्यनिरतिशयपरमानन्दरूप एव भवति, तदा विषयेन्द्रियसम्बन्धाधीनतया आत्मन्यानन्दानुभवो नोपपद्येत ।
'O Master, if my ātman is indeed of the nature of eternal, unexcelled supreme ānanda, then the experience of bliss in the ātman contingent upon contact between sense-objects and senses would not be tenable.'
अनुभूयत एव तु विषयसम्बन्धादात्मन्यानन्दः ।
'Yet bliss is indeed experienced in the Self through contact with objects.'
तस्मान्नैवानन्दरूप आत्मा ।
'Therefore, the ātman is not at all of the nature of bliss.'
किन्तु विषयसम्बन्धादेवात्मन्यानन्दो जायते ।
'Rather, bliss is generated in the Self only through contact with objects.'
130
अज्ञस्य विषयप्रवृत्तौ सत्यां तदीयान्तर्मुखवृत्तौ आत्मानन्दो भाति; विषयेषु नास्त्यानन्द इति समाधानम् - हे शिष्य ।
The resolution is: 'When an ignorant person engages with sense-objects, the bliss of the ātman shines in his inward-turned mental modification; there is no bliss in the objects themselves' — O disciple!
यस्य बुद्धिरात्मस्वरूपं न जानाति तस्य विषयेच्छा जायते ।
He whose intellect does not know the true nature of the ātman develops desire for sense-objects.
भोगसाधनानां स्त्रीधनपुत्रादीनामत्र विषयशब्देन ग्रहणम् ।
Here, by the word 'viṣaya' (sense-object), means of enjoyment such as women, wealth, children, etc. are understood.
विषयेच्छस्य पुंसो बुद्धिश्चञ्चला भवति ।
The intellect of a person who desires sense-objects becomes restless.
चञ्चलायां बुद्धावात्मस्वरूपानन्दप्रतिबिम्बो न भासते ।
In a restless intellect, the reflection of the bliss of the Self's nature does not shine.
अभिलषितविषयलाभे तु क्षणमात्रं बुद्धिः स्थिरीभवति ।
However, upon obtaining the desired object, the intellect becomes steady for a mere moment.
तदा बुद्धिवृत्तिरन्तर्मुखा भवति ।
At that time, the mental modification becomes inward-turned.
तस्यामन्तर्मुखायां वृत्तावात्मस्वरूपानन्दः प्रतिफलति ।
In that inward-turned modification, the bliss of the Self's true nature is reflected.
तादृशात्मस्वरूपानन्दप्रतिबिम्बमनुभवितुः पुंसो विषयेभ्यो ममानन्दोऽजायत इति भ्रान्तिरुत्पद्यते ।
To the person experiencing such reflection of the bliss of the Self, the delusion arises: 'Bliss arose to me from sense-objects.'
वस्तुतस्तु नैवास्ति जडे विषये आनन्दलेशोऽपि ।
In reality, however, there is not even a trace of bliss in an insentient object.
किञ्च आनन्दोत्पत्तेर्विषयाधीनत्वे यत्किञ्चिद्विषयजन्यानन्दमनुभवतः पुंसो विषयान्तरे इच्छोत्पत्तिदशायामपि प्राचीनविषयानन्दोऽनुवर्तितुमर्हति; न तु तथास्त्यनुभवः ।
Furthermore, if the arising of bliss were dependent on objects, then for a person experiencing bliss produced by some object, the bliss of that prior object ought to continue even when desire for another object arises; but experience is not so.
अस्मत्सिद्धान्ते तु विषयान्तरासक्त्या पुनरपि बुद्धिचाञ्चल्ये सति तस्यां चञ्चलबुद्धौ न स्वरूपानन्दप्रतिबिम्बो भातीति समाधानं ज्ञेयम् ।
In our siddhānta, however, the resolution is to be understood thus: when the intellect becomes restless again due to attachment to another object, the reflection of essential bliss does not shine in that restless intellect.
१. आत्मा स्वभावत एवानन्दस्वरूपः ।
1. The ātman is by its very nature blissful.
मनसो व्याकुलतायां सन्निहितोऽपि पदार्थो यथा न चक्षुर्गोचरो भवति, तथा यावद्रजोगुणसम्पर्काद्बुद्धिश्चञ्चला भवति तावदात्मन आनन्दांशो न बुद्धौ प्रतिभासते ।
Just as an object, though near, is not visible to the eyes when the mind is agitated, so as long as the intellect is restless from contact with rajoguṇa, the bliss aspect of the ātman does not shine in the intellect.
यथा दर्पणे प्रचलति सति तस्मिन्नुपलभ्यमानोऽपि मुखादिप्रतिबिम्बो नैव स्फुटस्तथा रजोगुणसम्पर्काच्चलन्त्यां बुद्धावात्मनः सच्चिदंशयोः प्रतिबिम्बे भासमानेऽपि नानन्दांशप्रतिबिम्बो भासते ।
Just as when a mirror is moving, the reflection of the face etc., though perceived in it, is not at all clear, so in an intellect agitated by contact with rajoguṇa, even though the reflection of the existence and consciousness aspects of the ātman shines, the reflection of the bliss aspect does not shine.
इष्टवस्तुलाभे सति तद्विषयकेच्छायाः, रजोगुणहेतुकबुद्धिचाञ्चल्यस्य च निवृत्तौ सत्यां प्राप्तेष्टवस्तुविषयकज्ञानरूपया सात्त्विकवृत्त्या विषयोपहितचैतन्यस्वरूपानन्दो विभाव्यते ।
When the desired object is obtained, and the desire for it as well as the restlessness of the intellect caused by rajoguṇa have ceased, the essential bliss of Consciousness conditioned by the object is manifested through the sāttvika mental modification taking the form of knowledge of that attained desired object.
अथवा इष्टवस्तुलाभमात्रेण तद्विषयकेच्छारूपवृत्तिर्निवर्तते ।
Alternatively, by the mere attainment of the desired object, the mental modification in the form of desire for that object ceases.
तेनैव हेतुनान्या काचिदन्तर्मुखा सात्त्विकी वृत्तिरुदेति ।
For that very reason, another inward-turned sāttvika modification arises.
तथा अन्तःकरणोपहितात्मानन्दः प्रकाशते ।
Thereby, the bliss of the ātman conditioned by the antaḥkaraṇa shines forth.
ईदृशान्तर्मुखान्तःकरणवृत्तिप्रतिफलितात्मस्वरूपानन्दप्रतिबिम्बो विषयानन्दः, प्रतिबिम्बानन्दः, लेशानन्द इति च कथ्यते ।
Such a reflection of the bliss of the Self reflected in an inward-turned mental modification is called viṣayānanda (object-bliss), pratibimbānanda (reflected bliss), and leśānanda (fractional bliss).
२. दुःखात्मकविषयानुभवकालीनसुखस्य वस्तुत आत्मस्वरूपसुखत्वेऽपि, विषयनिष्ठतया तज्जन्यत्वेन च तत्सुखस्य भानं भ्रमाद्भवति ।
2. Although the happiness experienced at the time of engaging with painful sense-objects is in truth the essential bliss of the ātman, the appearance of that happiness as abiding in the object and as produced by it occurs due to error.
यथा शुनः शुष्कास्थिखादनकाले स्वतालुजन्यरक्ते अस्थिजन्यत्वभ्रमस्तद्वत् ।
Just as when a dog chews a dry bone, there is the delusion regarding the blood coming from its own palate that it is produced from the bone, so it is here.
किञ्चान्यत्, यदि विषयादेवानन्दो नियमेन जायेत तदा प्रवासादागतपुत्रदर्शनजन्यानन्दः सदानुवर्तितुमर्हति; न तु तथा भवति ।
Moreover, if bliss were invariably produced from the object itself, then the bliss produced by seeing a son returning from a journey should continue forever; but it does not happen that way.
तथा हि — कस्यचित् प्रियतरः पुत्रश्चिरप्रवासी कालान्तरे प्रत्यागमत् ।
To explain: someone's very dear son, who had been abroad for a long time, returned after a period.
तद्दर्शनक्षणे जायमानः पितुरानन्दः चिरकालमविच्छिन्नतयानुवर्तितुमर्हति, आनन्दहेतोः पुत्रस्य सदा सन्निहितत्वात् ।
The bliss of the father arising at the moment of seeing him ought to continue uninterruptedly for a long time, because the cause of bliss, the son, is always present.
न तु तथानुभूयते ।
However, it is not experienced so.
सिद्धान्ते तु पुत्रदर्शनादितत्तद्विषयजन्यानन्दस्य चिरमननुवृत्तिरेवमुपपद्यते - तत्तद्विषयलाभक्षणे बुद्धिर्निश्चलीभवति ।
In our siddhānta, however, the non-continuation for long of the bliss produced by respective objects such as seeing the son is accounted for thus: at the exact moment of acquiring each respective object, the intellect becomes motionless.
तदा निश्चलायां बुद्धिवृत्तावात्मस्वरूपानन्दः प्रतिबिम्बितो भवति ।
At that time, the bliss that is the essential nature of the *ātman* becomes reflected in the motionless mental modification (*buddhi-vṛtti*).
स एवानन्दोऽनुभूयते ।
That very *ānanda* alone is experienced.
ततो विषयान्तरेच्छया पुनरपि बुद्धेश्चाञ्चल्ये सति तस्यां बुद्धौ स्वरूपानन्दप्रतिफलनस्य विच्छेदात्, पुरत एव सत्यपि प्राचीनविषये, नानन्दानुवृत्तिः ।
Thereafter, when the intellect becomes agitated again by the desire for another object, because of the interruption of the reflection of the essential *ānanda* in that intellect, there is no continuance of *ānanda*, even though that previous object is still present right before oneself.
तस्मान्न विषयेऽस्त्यानन्दः ।
Therefore, bliss does not exist in the object.
किञ्च यदि नियमेन विषयाधीन एवानन्दो भवेत्तदा समाधौ योगानन्दो न प्रकाशेत ।
Moreover, if *ānanda* were invariably dependent only on sense-objects, then in *samādhi*, the bliss of yoga would not shine forth.
तथा सुषुप्तावपि नानन्दभानं स्यात् ।
Likewise, even in deep sleep (*suṣupti*), there would be no manifestation of bliss.
सुषुप्तिसमाध्योर्दृश्यरूपविषयसम्बन्धस्याभावात् ।
For in both deep sleep and *samādhi*, there is an absolute absence of contact with perceived external objects.
तस्मान्न विषये आनन्दलेशोऽप्यस्ति ।
Therefore, there is not even a trace of *ānanda* in any object.
किन्त्वात्मस्वरूपानन्द एव सर्वात्मना सर्वत्रावभासते ।
Rather, it is the *ānanda* which is the very nature of the *ātman* that alone shines forth completely everywhere.
रसो वै सः, रसँ ह्येवायं लब्ध्वानन्दी भवति (तै. ब्र. ७) एतस्यैवानन्दस्यान्यानि भूतानि मात्रामुपजीवन्ति (बृ. ४.३.३२) इत्यादिश्रुतेः ।
This is supported by scriptural texts such as: 'He is indeed the essence of bliss; for having attained this essence, this individual becomes blissful' (तै. ब्र. ७) and 'Other beings subsist on only a fraction of this very bliss' (बृ. ४.३.३२).
हे शिष्य ।
O disciple!
निरतिशयानन्दस्वरूप एवात्मेति विषयसम्बन्धाच्च स आनन्दोऽभिव्यज्यते इति जानीहि अदृश्यो दृश्यते राहुर्गृहीतेन यथेन्दुना । तथानुभवमात्रात्मा दृश्येनात्मावलोक्यते ॥ इति स्मृतेः ।
Know that the *ātman* is of the nature of unsurpassable bliss alone, and that this *ānanda* is manifested through contact with objects, as declared by the *smṛti*: 'Just as the invisible Rāhu is seen through the seized moon, so also the Self, whose nature is pure experience, is perceived through the perceived object.'
अयमेव समीचीनः सिद्धान्तः ।
This alone is the correct *siddhānta*.
यद्यस्त्यत्र ते संशयो निर्व्यलीकमेव पृच्छ ।
If you have any doubt regarding this, ask frankly.
गुरुःपुनः सुस्फुटमेव त्वां बोधयेयमिति गुरुराह ।
'I shall explain it to you again very clearly,' said the Guru.
131
ज्ञानिनोऽपि विषयेष्विच्छा, विषयसम्बन्धादात्मानन्दावभासश्च भवति न वेति तत्त्वदृष्टिः पृच्छति -
Tattvadṛṣṭi asks whether a desire for objects and the manifestation of the bliss of the Self from contact with objects occurs in a jñānin as well:
हे सद्गुरो । विषयसम्बन्धादात्मानन्दावभासक्रमोऽज्ञानिविषये प्रतिपादितो भवद्भिः, न ज्ञानिविषये ।
'O true Guru, the process of the manifestation of the bliss of the Self through contact with sense-objects was explained by you with regard to an ignorant person, not with regard to an enlightened one.'
यतो यस्य बुद्धिरात्मस्वरूपविमुखा, तमधिकृत्य प्रस्तावः कृतः पूर्वं भवद्भिः ।
'Because the earlier presentation was made by you with reference to one whose mind is turned away from his own true nature.'
तादृश्चाज्ञान्येव, न ज्ञानी ।
'And such a person is only an ignorant one, not an enlightened one.'
तस्मादिदानीं ज्ञानिनोऽपि विषयेष्विच्छा1,2
'Therefore now, whether desire for objects in a jñānin too [and bliss-manifestation occur]...'
टिप्पणी
1.
चित्तैकाग्रतारूपयोगाभिव्यङ्ग्य आनन्दः ।
[The bliss referred to here is] the bliss manifest through yoga in the form of one-pointedness of mind.
2.
सुषुप्तिदृष्टान्तस्तु सर्वजनप्रसिद्ध्यर्थम् ।
The example of deep sleep, however, is given because it is universally familiar to everyone.
शिष्यःतस्यापि विषयसम्बन्धात्पूर्वोक्तक्रमेण सुखाभिव्यक्तिश्च जायते न वेति बोधयितुमर्हन्ति भवन्तः, इति ।
'...whether for him (the jñānin) too, manifestation of happiness occurs through contact with objects in the manner described previously, or not — your venerable self ought to enlighten me on this.'
132 · व्यवहारकाले ज्ञान्यप्यात्मविमुख एव; स विषयानन्दस्य स्वरूपानन्दादभिन्नतां मन्यते
हे शिष्य ! श‍ृणु सावधानमनाः ।
O disciple! Listen with an attentive mind.
यद् उक्तम् आत्मस्वरूपवैमुख्यम् एव विषयेच्छादिकारणम् इति, तत् न केवलम् अज्ञस्य एव, किन्तु ज्ञानिनः अपि तुल्यम् एव तत् ।
That which was stated — that turning away from one's own essential nature alone is the cause of desire for sense-objects, etc. — that is not true only of the ignorant, but is equally true of the knower as well.
ज्ञानी च यदा व्यवहारे प्रवर्तते तदा स तत्त्वविस्मरणपूर्वकम् एव प्रवर्तते ।
And when the knower engages in empirical activity, he engages only preceded by a temporary forgetting of the Truth.
विषयप्रवृत्तिकालेऽज्ञवद् आस्ते ज्ञान्यपि ।
Even the knower behaves like an ignorant person at the time of engagement with sense-objects.
ज्ञानिनः हि चित्तं सदा एव आत्माकारम् एव यदि स्यात् तदा तस्य जीवनादिनिमित्तभोजनादिव्यवहारः अपि न सिद्ध्येत् ।
For if the knower's mind were always shaped solely in the form of the ātman, then even activities such as eating, which are meant for sustaining life, would not be possible for him.
तस्माद् आत्मविमुखा बुद्धिः उभयोः समा ।
Therefore, the intellect turned away from the ātman is common to both.
अज्ञस्य बुद्धिः सदा विषयासक्तत्वाद् आत्मविमुखा एव तिष्ठति ।
The intellect of an ignorant person always remains turned away from the ātman because of attachment to sense-objects.
ज्ञानिनः तु बुद्धिः यदा आत्मनः विमुखा भवति, तदा विषयेच्छा तत्सम्पर्काद् आत्मस्वरूपानन्दाभिव्यक्तिः च अज्ञस्य इव तस्य अपि जायते ।
However, when the knower's intellect turns away from the ātman, then the desire for objects and, through contact with them, the manifestation of the ānanda of one's own essential nature arise for him as well, just as for the ignorant person.
तथापि अस्ति अत्र विशेषः - विषयसम्पर्काद् भासमानः अपि आनन्दः स्वस्वरूपानन्दात् न अतिरिच्यते, किन्तु तदाभासः एव इति विजानाति ब्रह्मवित् ।
Even so, there is a distinction here: the knower of Brahman knows that 'even the bliss experienced from contact with sense-objects is not different from the bliss of one's own essential nature, but is merely a reflection of it.'
तथा च विषयोपभोगे अपि ज्ञानिनः समाधिः एव सिद्ध्यति ।
And thus, even during the enjoyment of sense-objects, for the knower, it is *samādhi* alone that is accomplished.
अज्ञः तु अयम् आनन्दः स्वरूपानन्दः एव इति न एव वेद ।
The ignorant person, on the other hand, does not at all know that 'this bliss is the bliss of one's own essential nature alone.'
परमार्थतः तु ज्ञानी अज्ञानी च इति उभयोः अपि स्वरूपम् आनन्दः एव ; अज्ञस्य विषये आनन्दप्रतीतिः भ्रान्तिः एव ।
In ultimate truth, however, the essential nature of both the knower and the non-knower is *ānanda* alone; the experience of bliss in sense-objects for the ignorant person is sheer delusion.
दुःखविषयकप्रश्नप्रत्युक्तयः॥ १३३–१६८ ॥
133 · सांसारिकदुःखस्याश्रयप्रश्नः
हे सद्गुरो स्वामिन् ।1,2
O noble Guru! O Master!
टिप्पणी
1.
जाग्रदाकारवृत्त्युद्भवे न स्वप्नाकारवृत्तिर्जायते, स्वप्नाकारवृत्त्युद्भवे च न जाग्रदाकारवृत्तिर्जायते ।
When a waking-form mental modification arises, a dream-form mental modification is not born, and when a dream-form mental modification arises, a waking-form mental modification is not born.
एवमेव ज्ञानिनो बुद्धिः यदा आत्माकारा तदा नानात्माकारा भवति, यदा अनात्माकारा तदा नात्माकारा भवति ।
Just so, when the intellect of a *jñānin* takes the form of *ātman*, it is not of the form of *anātman*; when it takes the form of *anātman*, then it is not of the form of *ātman*.
यद्यप्येकान्तःकरणाधिकरणकभिन्नविषयकसामान्यविशेषरूपवृत्तिद्वयं युगपज्जायेत, तथापि विशेषरूपवृत्तिद्वयं तु नैव जायेत ।
Even if two mental modifications—one general and one specific—having different objects could arise simultaneously in a single internal organ, two specific mental modifications can never arise simultaneously.
यथा व्यवहारान्तरासक्तः पुरुषः पेटिकास्थधनं हस्तेन स्पृशन्नपि न स्मरति तत् धनम्, व्यवहारावसाने तु तद्धनं स्मरति; एवमेव ज्ञान्यपि व्यवहारदशायां यदा विषयाभिमुखो भवति तदा तस्य तत्त्वविस्मरणं भवति, व्यवहारसमाप्तौ पुनरपि तत्त्वनिष्ठ एव स भवति ।
Just as a person engaged in some other work, even while touching money inside a box with his hand, does not think of that money, but remembers it upon the completion of that work; even so, when a *jñānin* during practical worldly interactions turns towards sense-objects, he experiences a temporary lapse of attention to Truth, but upon the conclusion of those interactions, he becomes firmly established in Truth once again.
अत एवोक्तं भाष्यकारैः श्रीभगवत्पूज्यपादैरध्यासप्रकरणे - पश्वादिभिश्चाविशेषात् । अतः समानः पश्वादिभिः पुरुषाणां प्रमाणप्रमेयव्यवहारः (शा. भा.) इति ।
Therefore it has been stated by the revered Commentator, Śrī Śaṅkarācārya, in the Adhyāsa section: And because there is no difference (in behaviour) from animals etc. Hence, the worldly behaviour concerning means and objects of knowledge is identical for men and animals (Śāṅkara-bhāṣya).
2.
ज्ञानिनो विषयोपभोगकालेऽपि, विषये दोषदर्शनरूपविवेकस्य, विषयमिथ्यात्वनिश्चयपूर्वकवैराग्यस्य, विषयभोगानां परिणामे दुःखपर्यवसायित्वावधारणस्य विषयानन्दस्य स्वरूपानन्दाव्यतिरिक्तत्वनिश्चयस्य च जागरूकत्वात्, स्वरूपानुसन्धानरूपसमाधिसदृशत्वाच्च सिंहो माणवकः इतिवत् ज्ञानिनो विषयोपभोगे समाधित्वोक्तिरौपचारिकी ।
Because even during the enjoyment of sense-objects, discrimination in the form of seeing faults in objects, dispassion born of ascertainment of the unreality of objects, the conviction that sense pleasures culminate in sorrow, and the certainty that sensual joy is not separate from the essential bliss of the Self remain fully awake; and because it resembles *samādhi* in the form of continuous reflection upon one's true nature, the statement calling the *jñānin*'s enjoyment of objects *samādhi* is purely figurative, just like saying 'the boy is a lion'.
शिष्यःत्वं परमानन्दस्वरूपोऽसि इति भवता यदुक्तं प्राक्, तदहं सम्यग्जानामि ।
That which was stated by you earlier—'You are of the nature of supreme bliss'—that I understand well.
शिष्यःजननमरणादिसंसाररूपमहादुःखं कालत्रयेऽपि त्वयि नास्त्येव; अतस्तन्निवृत्तये तवेच्छात्यन्तासङ्गतेति भवदुक्तविषये तु कश्चन संशयो भवति ।
However, regarding what was stated by you: 'The great sorrow of transmigration consisting of birth, death, etc., does not exist in you at any of the three times (past, present, or future); therefore, your desire for its removal is completely unwarranted'—in this matter, a doubt arises in me.
शिष्यःयद्यनुभूयमानमिदं जननमरणादिदुःखं मयि नास्ति, तर्हि मदन्यं कमाश्रित्य तदवतिष्ठते इति दयया मे वद भोः ।
If this sorrow of birth, death, etc., which is being experienced, does not exist in me, then depending on whom other than me does it abide? Please tell me this out of compassion, O Venerable Master!
संसारदुःखस्याश्रयान्तरावगमे हि मयि तन्नास्तीति मम दृढा प्रतीतिः स्यादिति शिष्यः पृच्छति ।
'For, only when another locus of the misery of *saṃsāra* is known, can I have the firm conviction that it does not exist in me'—thus the disciple asks.
134 · न कस्यापि संसारोऽस्तीति गुरोरुत्तरं
हे शिष्य ।
O disciple!
श‍ृणु मे वचनम्, तेन ते सर्वसंशयनिवृत्तिः स्यात् ।
Listen to my words, through which all your doubts will be resolved.
जननमरणादिसंसारदुःखं न कुत्रचिदप्यस्ति ।
The misery of worldly existence consisting of birth, death, and so forth does not exist anywhere at all.
अनुभूयमानमपीदं दृश्यं जगत् कालत्रयेऽपि त्वयि मयि अन्यत्र वा कुत्रचिदप्यणुमात्रमपि नास्त्येव ।
Even though this visible universe is being experienced, it does not exist at all in any of the three periods of time—neither in you, nor in me, nor anywhere else—even to the extent of an atom.
अत एवास्य जगतः अत्यन्तनाशः न कुत्रचिदपि सम्भवति । इति ।
For this very reason, an absolute destruction of this world is never possible anywhere (since it was never created).
135 · असतः संसारस्य कथं प्रतीतिरिति प्रश्नः
हे कृपालो सद्गुरो ।
O compassionate, noble Guru!
जननमरणादिसंसारदुःखं मयि वान्यत्र वा कुत्रचिदपि न स्याच्चेत्, कथं तर्हि तत्प्रत्यक्षीभवति ।
If the sorrow of transmigratory life consisting of birth, death, etc., does not exist in me, or elsewhere, or anywhere at all, then how does it become directly perceived?
न ह्यत्यन्तासद्वस्तु कदाचिदप्युपलभ्यते ।
For an absolutely non-existent object is never perceived at any time.
शिष्यःवन्ध्यापुत्रगगनारविन्दाद्यसद्वस्तुवत् संसारोऽप्यत्यन्तासंश्चेन्न कदाचिदप्युपलभ्येत, उपलभ्यते तु, तस्माज्जन्ममरणादिदुःखरूपः संसारो नास्तीत्युक्तिर्न युज्यते; इति शिष्यः पृच्छति ।
If *saṃsāra* were also absolutely non-existent like unreal entities such as the son of a barren woman or a sky-lotus, it would never be perceived at all; but it is perceived. Therefore, the statement that *saṃsāra* in the form of the misery of birth and death does not exist is not tenable'—thus the disciple inquires.
136 · संसारप्रतीतिर्मिथ्येति गुरोरुत्तरं
जननमरणादिप्रवाहरूपं जगत् परमार्थतः कालत्रयेऽप्यसदपि, प्रत्यगात्मैव ब्रह्मेत्यजानतां केवलं मिथ्याभूतमवभासते ।
The universe, consisting of a continuous stream of births and deaths, though in absolute reality non-existent in all three periods of time, appears purely as an illusory appearance to those who do not know that the inner *ātman* alone is Brahman.
यथा स्वप्ने अनुभूयमानपदार्थाः, आकाशे नैल्यं, रज्जौ सर्पादयश्च परमार्थतः कालत्रयेऽपि असन्तोऽपि मिथ्यैवावभासन्ते, तद्वज्जगत् परमार्थतोऽसदपि मिथ्यारूपेणावभासते ।
Just as objects experienced in a dream, blueness in the sky, and a snake in a rope appear solely as false appearances despite being non-existent in absolute reality throughout all three periods of time, similarly the world, though non-existent in absolute reality, appears in an illusory form.
टिप्पणी
1.
यथा रज्जौ कल्पितसर्पस्य व्यावहारिकसत्तयात्यन्ताभावोऽस्ति, तथा ब्रह्मणि कल्पितस्य जगतः पारमार्थिकसत्तयात्यन्ताभावोऽस्ति ।
Just as there is absolute non-existence of the imagined snake in the rope with respect to empirical reality, so also there is absolute non-existence of the imagined world in Brahman with respect to absolute reality.
तथा च पारमार्थिकसत्तया जगतोऽत्यन्ताभाव एव तस्य नित्यनिवृत्तिरित्युच्यते ।
And therefore, the absolute non-existence of the world from the standpoint of absolute reality alone is said to be its eternal cessation.
2.
अर्थे ह्यविद्यमानेऽपि संसृतिर्न निवर्तते । ध्यायतो विषयानस्य स्वप्नेऽनर्थागमो यथा ॥ (भा. पु. ३.२७.४) ।
'Indeed, even though the objective world is non-existent, transmigration does not cease for the person who broods on sense objects, just as calamities befall one in a dream.' (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.27.4)
अविद्यमानोऽप्यवभासते द्वयो ध्यातुर्धिया स्वप्नमनोरथौ यथा । तत्कर्म सङ्कल्पविकल्पकं मनो बुधो निरुन्ध्यादभयं ततः स्यात् ॥ (भा. पु. ११.२.३८) इति भागवते ।
'Duality, though non-existent, appears through the intellect of one who contemplates it, just like dreams and daydreams. Therefore, the wise person should restrain the action-oriented mind full of desires and doubts; thence fearlessness arises.' (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 11.2.38) — thus in the Bhāgavata.
137 · रज्जौ सर्पप्रतीतिः कथमिति प्रश्नः
रज्जौ प्रतीयमानसर्पादयो यथा मिथ्या तथैव प्रत्यगात्मनि प्रतीयमानसंसारदुःखमपि मिथ्येति यदुक्तम्, तत्र दृष्टान्तज्ञानमन्तरा दार्ष्टान्तिकज्ञानासम्भवाद्रज्जौ सर्पः कथमवभासत इति प्रथमतस्तावन्मां बोधयन्तु भवन्त इति शिष्यो दृष्टान्तविषये पृच्छति ।
As to what was said — that just as the snake etc. perceived in a rope are false, so too the misery of *saṃsāra* perceived in the innermost *ātman* is false — regarding that, since knowledge of the illustrated principle is impossible without understanding the illustrative example, the disciple asks regarding the example: 'May your reverence first explain to me how a snake appears in a rope.'
शिष्यः स्वप्रश्नस्याशयं वर्णयति॥ १३८–१४३ ॥
138 · ख्यातिचतुष्टयं
रज्जुसर्पशुक्तिरजतादिभ्रमविषये मतचतुष्टयं श्रूयते ।
Regarding the illusion of rope-snake, shell-silver, etc., four views are heard in philosophical traditions.
तत्र (१) शून्यवादी असत्ख्यातिमाह ।
Among them, (1) the Śūnyavādin proposes *asatkhyāti* (cognition of the non-existent).
(२) क्षणिकविज्ञानवादी आत्मख्यातिमाचष्टे ।
(2) The Kṣaṇikavijñānavādin propounds *ātmakhyāti* (cognition of internal mind-forms as external).
(३) नैयायिका वैशेषिकाश्चान्यथाख्यातिमातिष्ठन्ते ।
(3) The Naiyāyikas and Vaiśeṣikas maintain *anyathākhyāti* (cognition of an object as otherwise).
(४) साङ्ख्याः प्राभाकराश्चाख्यातिं वदन्ति ।
(4) The Sāṅkhyas and the Prābhākara Mīmāṃsakas declare *akhyāti* (non-discrimination / non-cognition of difference).
139 · असत्ख्यातिः
तत्रासत्ख्यातिमङ्गीकुर्वतां शून्यवादिनामेवमाशयः - रज्जौ तावत्सर्पोऽत्यन्तमसन् ।
Among these, the purport of the Śūnyavādins who accept *asatkhyāti* is as follows: first of all, in the rope the snake is completely non-existent.
तथैवान्यात्रापि (वल्मीकादावपि) सर्पोऽत्यन्तमसन्नेव ।
Similarly, elsewhere too (even in an anthill, etc.), a snake is completely non-existent.
एवमत्यन्तासतः सर्पस्य प्रतीती रज्जौ भवति ।
Thus, the perception of an utterly non-existent snake occurs in the rope.
इमामेवासत्ख्यातिमाहुः शून्यवादिनः ।
This very phenomenon the Śūnyavādins call *asatkhyāti*.
अत्यन्तासतः सर्पस्य ख्यातिः = स्फुरणमभिवदनं चासत्ख्यातिरिति ।
The manifestation (*sphuraṇa*) and verbal expression (*abhivadana*) of an utterly non-existent snake is *asatkhyāti*.
140 · आत्मख्यातिः
विज्ञानवादिनोऽभिप्रायस्तु - रज्जौ वान्यत्र वा बुद्धेर्बहिः कुत्रचिदपि न सर्पोऽस्ति ।
The view of the Vijñānavādin, on the other hand, is: neither in the rope nor anywhere else outside the mind does any snake exist.
एवं सकलपदार्था अपि न बुद्धेर्बहिर्वर्तन्ते ।
Similarly, no external objects exist outside the mind.
बुद्धिरेव सकलपदार्थानामाकारान् धत्ते ।
Consciousness alone assumes the forms of all external objects.
सा च बुद्धिः क्षणिकविज्ञानरूपा ।
And that intellect is of the nature of momentary consciousness (*kṣaṇika-vijñāna*).
प्रतिक्षणमुत्पत्तिविनाशशालि यद्विज्ञानं तदेव सर्पात्मना अवभासते ।
The consciousness which undergoes origination and destruction every moment alone appears in the form of a snake.
इयमात्मख्यातिरिति वर्ण्यते ।
This is described as *ātmakhyāti*.
आत्मा = क्षणिकविज्ञानरूपा बुद्धिः, तस्याः ख्यातिः = स्फुरणमभिवदनञ्चात्मख्यातिरिति ।
'Ātman' = the intellect of the form of momentary consciousness; its 'khyāti' = manifestation and verbal assertion — this is *ātmakhyāti*.
अन्यथाख्यातिः॥ १४१–१४२ ॥
141 · तत्र नैयायिकवैशेषिकाणां मतं
वल्मीकादौ पारमार्थिकसर्पोऽस्ति ।
A real snake exists in a place such as a termite mound.
व्यवहितोऽपि स सर्पश्चक्षुषा गृह्यते ।
Even though concealed, that snake is grasped by the eye.
चक्षुर्गतदोषबलात् व्यवहितोऽपि सर्पः पुरतश्चक्षुःसन्निकृष्टो भाति ।
By the power of the defect residing in the eye, the snake, though distant and screened, appears right in front in contact with the eye.
पारमार्थिकसर्पस्य चक्षुषश्च मध्ये कुड्यादिरूपव्यवधानसत्त्वेऽपि दोषसचिवचक्षुषा व्यवहितसर्पोऽपि गृह्यत एव ।
Even though there exists an obstruction such as a wall in between the real snake and the eye, the distant snake is indeed perceived by the eye that is assisted by defects.
अस्ति प्रतीत्यवसरे न पुरो न पश्चादाश्चर्यमेतदवभाति तथापि विश्वम् । यद्वा किमद्भुतमिवेह महेन्द्रजालं मायाविकल्पितमपि प्रतिभासते हि ॥
It exists only at the time of perception, neither before nor after; yet this wondrous universe appears! Or what wonder is there in this: like a grand magician's show, even though imagined by *māyā*, it is indeed perceived!
ननु दोषसमवधानेन वस्तुनः सामर्थ्यहानिरेव दृश्यते, न वृद्धिः ।
An objection may be raised: By the presence of a defect, only the impairment of an object's capacity is seen, never its enhancement.
यथा वातपित्तकफादिदोषैर्जाठराग्नेरशितपीतपचनशक्तिः कुण्ठिता भवति, तथा तिमिरादिदोषैश्चक्षुषः शक्तिरपि कुण्ठितैव भवेत् ।
Just as the digestive fire's power of digesting food and drink is impaired by humours such as wind, bile, and phlegm, so too the power of the eye should only become impaired by eye-defects like cataract.
किञ्च, यदि वल्मीकस्थः सर्पो दोषसहितचक्षुषा गृह्यते, तर्हि शुद्धनेत्रेण व्यवहितवस्तुप्रत्यक्षं न भवति, किन्तु दुष्टनेत्रेणैवेति वक्तव्यम् ।
Moreover, if the snake inside the termite mound is perceived by the defective eye, then one would have to assert that perception of a hidden object does not occur through a healthy eye, but only through a diseased eye.
तस्माद्दोषसहितचक्षुषः सामर्थ्यं वर्धत इत्यत्र दृष्टान्तो नास्तीति चेत् ।
If it be argued that therefore there is no example showing that the capacity of the eye increases when combined with defects—
नायं दोषः, दृष्टान्तसद्भावात् ।
This is no fault, because a suitable example does exist.
तथा हि, पित्ताधिक्यप्रयुक्तभस्मकरोगाभिभूतस्य कस्यचिच्चतुर्गुणितमप्यन्नं क्षुधां शमयितुं नालं भवति ।
To explain: for a person afflicted with the disease of morbid appetite (*bhasmaka-roga*) caused by an excess of bile (*pitta*), even fourfold food is not sufficient to satisfy the hunger.
तत्र पित्तदोषेण यथा जाठराग्नेः पाचनशक्तिर्वर्धते, तथा चक्षुषोऽपि दोषैर्व्यवहितसर्पादिप्रत्यक्षीकरणशक्तिर्वर्धत इति वक्तुं युक्तम् ।
Just as in that case the digestive capacity of the stomach fire increases due to the defect of bile, likewise it is appropriate to state that the capacity of the eye to perceive concealed objects such as a snake increases due to ocular defects.
इत्थं च वल्मीकादिप्रदेशान्तरे स्थितसर्पस्य, अन्यथा = प्रकारान्तरेण = पुरोऽवस्थितरज्जुदेशे ख्यातिः = स्फुरणमभिवदनं च अन्यथाख्यातिरिति कथ्यते ।
And thus, the apprehension—that is, the manifestation and verbal expression—of a snake residing elsewhere in a place like a termite mound, occurring *otherwise* (i.e. in another manner, in the location of the rope situated in front), is called *anyathākhyāti*.
142 · अत्र नव्यनैयायिकचिन्तामणिकारमतं
दोषसहितचक्षुषा वल्मीकगतः सर्पो यदि दृश्येत तर्हि मध्यस्थपदार्थान्तरदर्शनमप्यापद्यते ।
If the snake in the termite mound were perceived by the defective eye, then perception of all intervening objects would also undesirably result.
तस्माद्व्यवहितं वस्तु न नेत्रेण गृह्यते ।
Therefore, a concealed object is never grasped by the eye.
किन्तु दुष्टनेत्रस्य रज्जुर्न स्वस्वरूपेण भासते, भासते तु सर्पाद्याकारेण ।
Rather, to one with defective vision, the rope does not appear in its own true form, but instead appears in the form of a snake and the like.
तस्मात् रज्जोः, अन्यथा = प्रकारान्तरेण = सर्पाद्याकारेण ख्यातिः = स्फुरणमभिवदनं चान्यथाख्यातिरिति ।
Therefore, the cognition—that is, the appearance and verbal expression—of the rope occurring *otherwise* (i.e. in an altered manner, namely in the form of a snake etc.) is called *anyathākhyāti*.
143 · अख्यातिमतम्, पूर्वोक्तमतत्रयखण्डनं च
तत्राख्यातिवादिनोऽयमाशयः - असत्ख्यातिमतरीत्या यद्यसदपि प्रतीयेत तर्हि वन्ध्यापुत्रशशश‍ृङ्गादयोऽपि प्रतीयेरन् ।
Herein, the intent of the proponent of *akhyāti* is this: if, according to the doctrine of *asatkhyāti*, even what is non-existent could be cognized, then the son of a barren woman, hare's horns, etc., would also be cognized.
तथा प्रतीत्यभावादसङ्गतमेवासत्ख्यातिमतम् ।
Because there is no such cognition, the theory of *asatkhyāti* is entirely untenable.
यदि क्षणिकविज्ञानवादिमतरीत्या प्रतिक्षणमन्यथा भवन्ती बुद्धिः सर्पाद्याकारतां प्राप्नुयात्तदा क्षणादूर्ध्वं तस्य सर्पस्य प्रतीतिर्न स्यात् ।
If, according to the doctrine of the momentary-cognitionists (Vijñānavāda), the intellect changing moment by moment were to assume the form of a snake, etc., then after one moment there would be no continued cognition of that snake.
परन्तु यावद्भ्रमकालं सर्पप्रतीतिरनुवर्तते ।
However, the cognition of the snake persists throughout the duration of the delusion.
तस्मादात्मख्यातिमतमप्यनुपादेयमेव ।
Therefore, the view of *ātmakhyāti* is also unacceptable.
टिप्पणी
1.
व्यवहितं वस्तु शुद्धनेत्रेण नोपलभ्यते, किन्तु दुष्टनेत्रेणोपलभ्यत इत्युक्तिर्लोकविरुद्धा ।
The claim that a distant/concealed object is not perceived with a healthy eye, but is perceived with a defective eye, is contrary to common experience.
2.
इदं प्राचीनमतम् ।
This is the ancient view.
अस्मिन्मते देशान्तरस्थवस्तुनो देशान्तरे भानमेव भ्रान्तिरित्युच्यते ।
In this view, the manifestation of an object situated in another place in a different place is itself called delusion.
सिद्धान्तोक्तार्थाध्यासज्ञानाध्यासरूपभ्रान्तिर्नास्मिन् मतेऽभ्युपगम्यते ।
Delusion in the form of *arthādhyāsa* (superimposition of object) and *jñānādhyāsa* (superimposition of cognition) as stated in the Siddhānta is not accepted in this view.
3.
चिन्तामणिकारमते एकस्य वस्तुनो रूपान्तरेण भासमानता भ्रान्तिरिति कथ्यते ।
In the view of the author of Cintāmaṇi, the appearance of one object under the form of another is called error (*bhrānti*).
अयमेव ज्ञानाध्यासः ।
This alone is *jñānādhyāsa*.
4.
दोषबलादट्टस्थरजतं यदि शुक्तौ भ्रान्तिदेशे भासेत, तदा आपणं तत्स्थसुवर्णादिनिखिलं वस्तु दोषवशादुपलभ्येत ।
If silver situated in a market were to appear in mother-of-pearl at the locus of delusion due to a defect, then the market and all objects situated in it, such as gold, should also be perceived due to the defect.
न चैवमुपलभ्यते ।
And it is not perceived in this way.
अन्यथाख्यातेः प्रथमः प्रकारः चिन्तामणिकारमतेन खण्डितः ।
The first mode of *anyathākhyāti* is refuted by the view of the author of Cintāmaṇi.
चिन्तामणिकारप्रदर्शितान्यथाख्यातिप्रकारोऽप्यसङ्गत एव ।
The variety of *anyathākhyāti* demonstrated by the author of Cintāmaṇi is also untenable.
ज्ञेयाधीनं ज्ञानम् इति हि प्रसिद्धिः ।
For there is the well-known maxim: 'Knowledge is dependent upon the object of knowledge.'
अत्र तु ज्ञेया रज्जुः, ज्ञानं तु सर्पविषयकमिति सुतरां विरुद्धमुच्यते ।
Here, however, the object present is the rope, but the cognition is about a snake; saying this is utterly contradictory.
तस्माच्चिन्तामणिकाराभिमतान्यथाख्यातेरादरानर्हत्वात्, अख्यातिरेव शरणमिति साङ्ख्याः प्राभाकराश्चाहुः ।
Therefore, since the *anyathākhyāti* favored by the Cintāmaṇikāra is unworthy of regard, *akhyāti* alone is the only resort, say the Sāṅkhyas and the Prābhākaras.
अख्यातिमतं - रज्जौ सर्पादिभ्रमदशायां नेत्रं स्ववृत्तिद्वारा रज्ज्वा सह संयुज्य अयम् इति रज्जोः सामान्यज्ञानं जनयति ।
The *akhyāti* view is: at the time of the illusion of a snake in a rope, the eye, making contact with the rope through its *vṛtti*, produces a general cognition of the rope as 'this'.
तदा सर्पस्मरणं च जायते ।
Then, remembrance of a snake also arises.
ततः अयं सर्पः इति ज्ञानं जायते ।
Thereafter arises the cognition 'this is a snake'.
तत्र ग्रहणस्मरणात्मकज्ञानद्वयमस्ति ।
There exists a duality of cognitions comprising direct perception and memory.
अयम् इति रज्जोः सामान्यांशप्रत्यक्षज्ञानम् ।
'This' is the direct perception of the general aspect of the rope.
सर्पः इति तु पूर्वानुभूतसर्पस्य स्मरणरूपमपरं ज्ञानम् ।
'Snake', however, is a second cognition in the form of remembrance of a previously experienced snake.
इत्थं अयं सर्पः इत्यत्र ज्ञानद्वयमस्ति ।
Thus, in 'this is a snake', there are two distinct cognitions.
अत्र अयम् इति रज्जोः सामान्यांशज्ञानस्य पूर्वानुभूतसर्पस्मरणरूपज्ञानस्य च परमार्थत्वेऽपि भयरूपप्रमातृदोषेण तिमिररूपप्रमाणदोषेण च, मम ज्ञानद्वयमभूत् तत्रैकं रज्जुसामान्यांशप्रत्यक्षं सर्पस्मरणरूपज्ञानमपरमिति, विवेकः पुरुषस्य नोत्पद्यते ।
Here, even though both the cognition of the rope's general aspect as 'this' and the cognition consisting of memory of the previously seen snake are real (true cognitions), due to the defect of the knower (fear) and of the instrument of knowledge (dimness/cataract), the discrimination does not arise in the person: 'Two cognitions occurred to me; of them, one is the perception of the rope's general aspect, and the other is a cognition in the form of memory of a snake.'
एतज्ज्ञानद्वयाविवेक एव भ्रम इति साङ्ख्याः प्राभाकराश्च वदन्ति ।
The Sāṅkhyas and the Prābhākaras declare that the non-distinction between these two cognitions is itself error (*bhrama*).
भ्रमोत्पत्तिस्थले च सर्वत्रैवमेव बोद्ध्यमिति चाहुः ।
And they say that it must be understood in this very manner everywhere in cases of delusion.
एवं रज्ज्वादौ सर्पादिभ्रमोत्पत्तिविषये मतचतुष्टयं पूर्वोक्तप्रकारेण श्रूयते ।
Thus, concerning the occurrence of the delusion of snake etc. in a rope etc., the four views are reported as explained above.
शिष्यःतत्र भवदभिमतमुत्तमं मतं यत्, तद्भवदुपदेशाद्विजिज्ञासे इति तत्त्वदृष्टिः पृच्छति ।
'Among these, whichever is the highest view favored by you, that I desire to learn from your instruction,' thus asks Tattvadṛṣṭi.
अख्यातिमतखण्डनम्॥ १४४–१४५ ॥
144
भयपलायनाद्यनुपपत्त्या रज्जौ सर्पानुभवो वाच्यः ।
On account of the impossibility of fear, fleeing, and so forth otherwise, an actual direct experience of the snake in the rope must be accepted.
हे सोम्य ! भ्रमस्थले असत्ख्यातिः, आत्मख्यातिः, अन्यथाख्यातिः, अख्यातिः इत्येतन्मतचतुष्टयमपि युक्तिविरहितम् ।
O gentle one! In the matter of illusion, this quartet of views — asat-khyāti, ātma-khyāti, anyathā-khyāti, and akhyāti — is entirely devoid of logical justification.
पूर्वोक्तमतचतुष्टयविलक्षणमनिर्वचनीयख्यातिनामकं 1मतान्तरमस्ति पञ्चमम्; तदेवोपादेयम् ।
There is a fifth alternative doctrine distinct from the aforementioned four doctrines, named anirvacanīya-khyāti; that alone is to be accepted.
पूर्वोक्तासत्ख्यात्यादिम...
[Refutation of] the aforementioned views such as asat-khyāti...
टिप्पणी
1.
पूर्वोक्तमतचतुष्टयातिरिक्तं सत्ख्यातिः इति पञ्चमं पूर्वपक्षिमतमस्ति ।
Apart from the four doctrines mentioned before, there is a fifth opponent's doctrine known as 'sat-khyāti'.
तन्मतरीत्या, शुक्तौ शुक्त्यवयवैः सह रजतावयवोऽपि सदा वर्तते ।
According to that view (Rāmānuja's sat-khyāti), silver-particles always exist in mother-of-pearl alongside the mother-of-pearl particles.
शुक्त्यवयववद्रजतावयवोऽपि सत्यः, न मिथ्या ।
Just like the particles of mother-of-pearl, the silver particles too are real, not illusory.
यथा शुक्तौ दुष्टनेत्रेन्द्रियसम्प्रयोगवशात् सिद्धान्तेऽविद्यापरिणामरूपानिर्वचनीयरजतं तत्काले जायते, तथात्र मते दुष्टनेत्रेन्द्रियसम्प्रयोगवशाद्रजतावयवेभ्यः सत्यरजतमपि शुक्तौ जायते ।
Just as in our established conclusion (siddhānta) an ineffable silver that is a modification of avidyā arises in the mother-of-pearl at that time due to defective contact of the eye sense-organ, so too in their view real silver is produced in the mother-of-pearl from the subtle silver components due to defective ocular contact.
सिद्धान्ते अधिष्ठानसाक्षात्कारादनिर्वचनीयरजतनिवृत्तिवत्, अत्र मते शुक्तिज्ञानात् सत्यरजतमपि स्वावयवेषु लीयत इति वदन्ति ।
Just as in the Advaita siddhānta the ineffable silver disappears upon direct cognition of the substratum, so in this view they claim that upon knowledge of the mother-of-pearl, the real silver dissolves back into its own constituent particles.
इदमपि मतं हेयमेव ।
This view too is utterly unfit for acceptance.
शुक्तिरजतदृष्टान्तेन हि प्रपञ्चमिथ्यात्वानुमितिर्जायते ।
For the inferential conclusion of the unreality of the world is established through the example of shell-silver.
सत्ख्यातिवादे तु शुक्तिरजतस्य सत्यत्वात् तद्दृष्टान्तेन न प्रपञ्चमिथ्यात्वं साधयितुं शक्यते ।
In the sat-khyāti theory, however, because the shell-silver is considered real, it would be impossible to prove the falsity of the world using that example.
एतन्मतखण्डनपरयुक्त्यन्तराणि बालानां दुर्बोधत्वान्नेह लिख्यन्ते ।
Other detailed arguments refuting this doctrine are not written here, as they would be too difficult for beginners to comprehend.
तत्रयं नोपादेयमित्यख्यातिवादिना दर्शितः; अख्यातिमतमपि नोपादानमर्हतीति प्रदर्श्यतेऽधुना ।
That the prior triad of doctrines is unacceptable was already shown by the proponent of akhyāti; now it is shown that the akhyāti doctrine too does not deserve acceptance.
अख्यातिमतरीत्या अयं सर्पः इति ज्ञाने अयम् इति रज्ज्वात्मकाधिष्ठानसामान्यांशप्रत्यक्षज्ञानम् ।
According to the akhyāti doctrine, in the cognition 'this is a snake', the part 'this' is direct perceptual knowledge of the general feature of the rope-substratum.
सर्पः इति त्वन्यत्र पूर्वदृष्टसर्पस्य स्मरणात्मकज्ञानमिति स्थितिः ।
Whereas 'snake' is a cognition of the nature of remembrance of a snake seen elsewhere in the past — such is their thesis.
तत्र पूर्वदृष्टसर्पस्मरणमेवाङ्गीकृत्य पुरोवर्तिरज्जौ सर्पज्ञानानङ्गीकारे, पुरोऽवस्थितरज्जुं दृष्ट्वा पुरुषो भीत्या न पलायेत, रज्जुं दृष्ट्वा पुरुषः पलायत इति तु सर्वजनीनम् ।
Now, if one only admits the remembrance of a snake seen in the past and refuses to admit a cognition of a snake in the rope present before oneself, a person seeing the rope lying in front would not flee in fear; but that a person does flee upon seeing the rope [mistaken for a snake] is universally known.
तस्मात्पुरोऽवस्थितरज्ज्वामेव सर्पः प्रत्यक्षतया भासते इति, न तु पूर्वदृष्टसर्पस्मरणमात्रमिति च वाच्यम् ।
Therefore, it must be admitted that a snake appears perceptually right in the rope present before the person, and not that it is mere remembrance of a previously seen snake.
अन्यथा रज्जौ सर्पज्ञानाभावेन पुरुषस्य पलायनादि नोपपद्येत ।
Otherwise, in the absence of a cognition of a snake in the rope, the person's actions such as fleeing would remain inexplicable.
145 · बाधज्ञानबलादपि रज्जौ सर्पानुभवो वाच्यः
किञ्च रज्जुयाथात्म्यज्ञानानन्तरं मम मिथ्यासर्पो रज्ज्वामभात् इति बाधरूपानुभवबलादपि पुरुषस्य रज्जावेव सर्पः स्वरूपतः प्रतीतः, न तु पूर्वानुभूतसर्पस्मरणमात्रमभवदिति वक्तव्यं भवति ।
Furthermore, on the strength of the sublating experience following the knowledge of the true nature of the rope — 'A false snake appeared to me in the rope' — it must be affirmed that the snake itself was directly experienced right in the rope, and that it was not merely the recollection of a previously experienced snake.
अपि च अयं सर्पः इत्यत्र जायमानं ज्ञानमेकमेव, न तु ज्ञानद्वयम् ।
Moreover, the knowledge arising here as 'this is a snake' is a single unitary cognition, not two separate cognitions.
न ह्येकस्मिन् क्षणे एकान्तःकरणवृत्तित्वेन स्मरणात्मकमनुभवात्मकं च ज्ञानद्वयं जायेत ।
For two cognitions — one of the nature of remembrance and the other of the nature of direct perception — cannot arise simultaneously in a single moment as a single modification of the mind (antaḥkaraṇa-vṛtti).
तस्मादख्यातिमतमप्यसङ्गतत्वादनुपादेयमेव ।
Therefore, the akhyāti doctrine too is wholly untenable and unacceptable.
पूर्वोक्तमतचतुष्टयलक्षणं तत्खण्डनादिकं च विवरणस्वाराज्यसिद्ध्यादिग्रन्थेषु विस्तरतो वर्णितम् ।
The definitions and refutations of the four aforementioned theories of error have been described extensively in treatises such as the Vivaraṇa and Svārājyasiddhi.
तेषां मतानां स्वरूपमात्रजिज्ञासूनां ज्ञानसौकर्यार्थं तत् सङ्क्षिप्योक्तमत्र ।
For the convenience of those who wish to understand the mere outline of those doctrines, it has been stated here in summary.
सिद्धान्तिनोऽनिर्वचनीयख्यातिनिरूपणम्॥ १४६–१४९ ॥
146 · अनिर्वचनीयख्यातिलक्षणं
अन्तःकरणवृत्तिश्चक्षुरादिकरणद्वारा बहिर्निर्गत्य विषयसमानाकारा भवति ।
The modification of the inner organ (antaḥkaraṇa-vṛtti), having gone out through sense-organs such as the eye, assumes the very form of the object.
तया वृत्त्या विषयावरणभङ्गे सति विषय उपलभ्यते ।
When the veil concealing the object is broken by that vṛtti, the object is perceived.
तस्या वृत्तेः सौराद्यालोकोऽपि साधको भवति ।
Light such as solar light is also an auxiliary cause for that vṛtti.
आलोकं विना पदार्थो न प्रकाशते, तस्मादालोकः सहकारी; इति क्रमः ।
Without light an object is not revealed; therefore light is an auxiliary cause—such is the process.
रज्ज्वादौ 1सर्पादिभ्रमोत्पत्तिदशायामन्तःकरणवृत्तिश्चक्षुर्द्वारा बहिर्निर्गत्य रज्ज्वा सह संयुज्यते ।
At the time of the emergence of the illusion of a snake etc. on a rope etc., the modification of the inner organ goes out through the eye and connects with the rope.
तथापि सा तमादिदोषैः प्रतिबद्धा सती न रज्जु
Even so, being obstructed by defects like dim darkness, it does not [take the form of] the rope...
टिप्पणी
1.
तमःशब्देन मन्दान्धकारो गृह्यते ।
By the word tamas (darkness), dim darkness (twilight) is meant.
तथा हि, प्रौढप्रकाशे रज्ज्वाद्यधिष्ठानस्य विशेषांशाज्ञानं न जायेत ।
To explain: in full bright light, ignorance of the specific feature of the substratum (like a rope) would not arise.
गाढतमसि अधिष्ठानस्य सामान्यांशज्ञानमपि न जायेत ।
In pitch darkness, even the knowledge of the general aspect of the substratum would not arise.
अधिष्ठानस्य सामान्यांशज्ञानम्, विशेषांशाज्ञानं च विना अध्यासो नैव जायेतेति द्वितीयतरङ्गे (६७) आवर्तेऽभिहितम् ।
That 'without the knowledge of the general feature of the substratum and the ignorance of its specific feature, adhyāsa cannot occur at all' was stated in the second wave, section (67).
मन्दान्धकारे अधिष्ठानसामान्यांशज्ञानतद्विशेषांशाज्ञानयोः सम्भवात्तमःशब्देन मन्दान्धकारग्रहणमेव न्याय्यम् ।
Because both the knowledge of the general aspect of the substratum and ignorance of its specific aspect are possible in dim darkness, taking dim darkness as the meaning of the word tamas is indeed appropriate.
नेत्रमान्द्यरूपतिमिरदोषोऽपि तमःशब्देन गृह्यते ।
The eye-defect of timira (visual impairment) in the form of visual weakness is also understood by the word tamas.
आदिशब्देन काचकामलादिनेत्ररोगाश्च गृह्यन्ते ।
And by the word ādi ('and the like'), eye-diseases like cataract (kāca), jaundice (kāmalā), and others are comprehended.
समानाकारा भवति ।
[...the mental modification does not] become identical in form with the rope.
ततो न रज्जोरावरणभङ्गो जायते ।
Therefore, the destruction of the veil concealing the rope does not take place.
इत्थमावरणभञ्जकवृत्तिसंसर्गे सत्यपि यदा दोषैः रज्ज्वामावरणभङ्गो न जायते तदा अधिष्ठानभूतरज्ज्ववच्छिन्नचैतन्यनिष्ठाविद्यायां कश्चन विक्षेपो जायते ।
Thus, even though there is contact with the veil-breaking vṛtti, when the removal of the veil over the rope does not occur due to defects, then a certain projection (vikṣepa) arises in the avidyā located in the consciousness conditioned by the rope that serves as substratum.
तदा साविद्या सर्पाकारेण परिणमते ।
Then that avidyā transforms into the form of a snake.
स चाविद्याकार्यभूतः सर्पो यदि सन् स्यात्, न स रज्जुसाक्षात्कारेण निवर्तेत; निवृत्तिश्चानुभूयते ।
And if that snake, which is an effect of avidyā, were real (sat), it would not be sublated by the direct perception of the rope; yet its sublation is experienced.
तस्मान्नैव सन् स सर्पः ।
Therefore, that snake is certainly not real (sat).
अत्यन्तासंश्चेत्स्यात्स सर्पो वन्ध्यापुत्रादिवन्नोपलभ्येत, उपलभ्यते तु ।
If that snake were utterly non-existent (asat), it would not be perceived, like the son of a barren woman; however, it is perceived.
तस्मान्नाप्यसन् स सर्पः ।
Therefore, that snake is not non-existent (asat) either.
किन्तु सदसद्विलक्षणोऽनिर्वचनीयः ।
Rather, it is distinct from both the real and the unreal—indefinable (anirvacanīya).
एवमेव शुक्त्याद्यधिकरणेष्वपि आरोपितरजतादयस्तात्कालिकतया अनिर्वचनीयतयोत्पन्नाः सन्तः प्रतिभान्ति ।
In the exact same way, in substrata like mother-of-pearl, superimposed silver and so forth appear, having been produced as indefinable entities for the duration of the cognition.
अस्यनिर्वचनीयस्य सर्पादेः ख्यातिः = प्रसिद्धिः = प्रतीतिः = स्फुरणमभिवदनञ्चानिर्वचनीयख्यातिरित्युच्यते ।
The cognition (khyāti) = awareness = perception = flashing forth and verbal articulation of this indefinable snake etc. is called Anirvacanīya-khyāti.
147 · भ्रमस्थले सर्पज्ञानमप्यविद्यापरिणामः; सर्पतज्ज्ञानयोर्युगपदेवोत्पत्तिलयौ; सर्पः साक्षिभास्यश्च
यथा सर्पादिरविद्यापरिणामस्1तथा तादृशसर्पादिज्ञानरूपवृत्तिरप्यविद्यापरिणाम एव, न त्वन्तःकरणपरिणामः ।
Just as the illusory snake and the like are transformations of avidyā, so too is the modification in the form of the cognition of such a snake etc. only a transformation of avidyā, and not a transformation of the internal organ (antaḥkaraṇa).
अत एवाधिष्ठानरज्ज्वादिसाक्षात्कारेण आरोपितसर्पादिरिवारोपितसर्पादिज्ञानमपि बाध्यते ।
For this very reason, just like the superimposed snake and the like, the superimposed cognition of the snake and the like is also sublated by the direct perception of the substratum rope, etc.
तस्यान्तःकरणपरिणामत्वे तु न बाधो युज्यते ।
If it were a transformation of the internal organ, however, sublation would not be tenable.
अतः आरोपितसर्पादिवत् तज्ज्ञानमप्यविद्याकार्यत्वात् सदसद्विलक्षणमनिर्वचनीयं भवति ।
Therefore, like the superimposed snake etc., its cognition too, because of being an effect of avidyā, is distinct from both real and unreal, and is indeterminable (anirvacanīya).
अपि त्वयं विशेषः - प्रातिभासिकसर्पादिः रज्ज्वाद्युपहिताधिष्ठानचैतन्यस्थतमोगुणप्रधानाविद्यांशपरिणामः ।
There is, however, this distinction: the apparent snake etc. is a transformation of the portion of avidyā predominated by tamo-guṇa resting in the substratum-consciousness conditioned by the rope, etc.
तद्विषयकवृत्तिज्ञानन्तु इदमाकारवृत्त्यभिव्यञ्जकसाक्षिचैतन्यस्थसत्त्वगुणप्रधानाविद्यांशपरिणाम इति विवेकः ।
Whereas the cognitive modification regarding it is a transformation of the portion of avidyā predominated by sattva-guṇa resting in the witness-consciousness that manifests the modification of the form 'this'—such is the distinction.
रज्ज्वाद्युपहितचैतन्यस्थाविद्या यदा सर्पाद्याकारेण परिणमते, तदैव तद्वृत्त्युपहितसाक्षिचैतन्यस्थाप्यविद्या सर्पादिज्ञानाकारेण परिणमते ।
When the avidyā residing in the consciousness conditioned by the rope etc. transforms into the form of the snake and the like, at that very moment the avidyā residing in the witness-consciousness conditioned by that vṛtti also transforms into the form of the cognition of the snake etc.
येन कारणेन रज्ज्वाद्युपहितचैतन्यस्थाविद्यायां क्षोभो जायते तेनैव कारणेन साक्षिचैतन्यस्थाविद्यायामपि क्षोभो जायते ।
By whichever cause an agitation is produced in the avidyā resting in the consciousness conditioned by the rope etc., by that very cause an agitation is also produced in the avidyā resting in the witness-consciousness.
तस्माद्भ्रमस्थले सर्पादि
Therefore, in the case of illusion, the snake etc. ...
टिप्पणी
1.
ननु सद्विलक्षणमसत् ।
[Objection]: What is distinct from the real is unreal.
अतः सद्विलक्षणस्यानिर्वचनीयस्यासद्विलक्षणत्वोक्तिर्विरुद्ध्यते ।
Therefore, to assert distinctness from the unreal in the case of the indeterminable, which is distinct from the real, is contradictory.
तथासतो विलक्षणं सदेव ।
Likewise, what is distinct from the unreal is necessarily real.
अतोऽसतो विलक्षणस्यानिर्वचनीयस्य सद्विलक्षणत्वोक्तिरप्यसङ्गतैव ।
Therefore, to assert distinctness from the real in the case of the indeterminable, which is distinct from the unreal, is also completely untenable.
तस्मात्सदसद्विलक्षणतृतीयपदार्थस्यैवाभावादनिर्वचनीयपदात् शाब्धबोध एव नोदेष्यतीति चेन्न ।
If it is argued: 'Therefore, because there is no third category of entity distinct from both real and unreal, no verbal comprehension will arise at all from the word anirvacanīya' — this is not so.
त्रिकालाबाध्यत्वस्यैव सत्त्वात्, तद्विलक्षणमित्यस्य कालत्रयेऽपि बाध्यमित्यर्थः सिद्ध्यति ।
For 'reality' means being unsublatable in all three periods of time; hence, the phrase 'distinct from that' establishes the meaning 'sublatable in all three periods of time'.
निःस्वरूपवन्ध्यापुत्रादि असदित्युच्यते ।
That which is devoid of any ontological nature, such as the son of a barren woman, is called 'unreal' (asat).
ततो विलक्षणमित्यस्य स्वरूपवदित्यर्थः ।
The phrase 'distinct from that' means 'possessing an apparent form'.
तस्माद्बाध्यत्वे सति स्वरूपवत्त्वमनिर्वचनीयपदस्यार्थः ।
Therefore, the meaning of the word anirvacanīya is 'possessing an apparent form while being subject to sublation'.
तथा च रज्जुसर्पादिरिव प्रपञ्चस्यप्यनिर्वचनीयतयैव भानं वेदान्तनिपुणानां भवति ।
And so, for those adept in Vedānta, just like the rope-snake etc., the phenomenal world too appears only as indeterminable (anirvacanīya).
२. उपादानस्य कार्याभिमुखत्वं क्षोभः ।
2. 'Agitation' (kṣobha) means the orientation of the material cause toward producing its effect.
विषयास्तज्ज्ञानानि च युगपदेवोत्पद्यन्ते, रज्ज्वाद्यधिष्ठानसाक्षात्कारेण युगपदेव प्रलीयन्ते च ।
The objects and their cognitions arise simultaneously, and upon the direct perception of the substratum rope etc., they dissolve simultaneously.
इत्थं च भ्रमस्थले बाह्यचैतन्यस्थाविद्यांशः सर्पादिविषयोपादानाकारणं भवति ।
And thus, in the case of illusion, the portion of avidyā located in the external consciousness serves as the material cause of the object such as the snake.
अन्तःसाक्षिचैतन्यस्थाविद्यांशः सर्पादिविषयकज्ञानरूपवृत्त्युपादानकारणं भवति ।
The portion of avidyā resting in the internal witness-consciousness serves as the material cause of the vṛtti in the form of the cognition regarding the snake etc.
स्वप्ने त्वन्तःसाक्ष्याश्रयाविद्यागततमोगुणांशो विषयाकारेण परिणमते, तादृशाविद्यागतसत्त्वगुणांशस्तज्ज्ञानाकारेण परिणमते ।
In dream, however, the tamo-guṇa portion residing in the avidyā supported by the internal witness transforms into the form of dream objects, while the sattva-guṇa portion residing in such avidyā transforms into the form of their cognitions.
अत एव स्वप्नेऽन्तःस्थाविद्यैव विषयतज्ज्ञानयोरुभयोरुपादानकारणं भवति ।
Therefore, in dream, the internally located avidyā alone serves as the material cause for both the objects and their cognitions.
अनेनैव हेतुना बाह्यरज्जुसर्पादयः आन्तरस्वाप्निकपदार्थाश्च साक्षिभास्या इत्युच्यन्ते ।
For this very reason, both external rope-snakes etc. and internal dream entities are described as directly illumined by the witness (sākṣi-bhāsya).
अविद्यावृत्तिद्वारा यद्यत् साक्षी प्रकाशयति तत्तत् साक्षिभास्यमित्युच्यते ।
Whatever the witness illuminates through the medium of an avidyā-vṛtti is called 'illumined by the witness' (sākṣi-bhāsya).
148 · रज्जुसर्पः तज्ज्ञानं चाविद्यायाः परिणामश्चेतनस्य विवर्तश्च
अनिर्वचनीयरज्जुसर्पादिस्तज्ज्ञानं च भ्रम इति अध्यास इति चोच्यते ।
The indeterminable rope-snake and its cognition are called 'delusion' (*bhrama*) and 'superimposition' (*adhyāsa*).
अयं च भ्रमोऽविद्यायाः परिणामश्चैतन्यस्य विवर्तश्च भवति ।
And this delusion is a transformation (*pariṇāma*) of *avidyā* and an apparent modification (*vivarta*) of Consciousness.
उपादानकारणसमस्वभावकोऽन्यथाभावः परिणामः, अधिष्ठानविषमस्वभावकोऽन्यथाभावो विवर्त इति च विवेकः ।
And the distinction is this: an alteration that shares the same order of reality (nature) with its material cause is *pariṇāma*; whereas an alteration that has a different order of reality from its substratum (*adhiṣṭhāna*) is *vivarta*.
उपादानकारणमविद्या, स चानिर्वचनीया ।
The material cause is *avidyā*, and that is indeterminable (*anirvacanīyā*).
तथा रज्जुसर्पादि तज्ज्ञानञ्चानिर्वचनीयमेव ।
Likewise, the rope-snake etc. and its cognition are indeed indeterminable.
तस्माद्रज्जुसर्पादि तज्ज्ञानञ्चाविद्यासमस्वभावकतदन्यथाभावरूपत्वादविद्यापरिणामो भवति ।
Therefore, because the rope-snake etc. and its cognition are of the nature of an alteration of *avidyā* sharing the same reality-status with it, they are a transformation (*pariṇāma*) of *avidyā*.
रज्ज्वाद्यवच्छिन्नाधिष्ठानचैतन्यं तु सत्स्वरूपमास्ते ।
However, the substratum Consciousness delimited by the rope etc. is of the nature of true Existence (*sat*).
रज्जुसर्पादि तज्ज्ञानं हि सद्विलक्षणं भवति ।
For the rope-snake etc. and its cognition are distinct from the real (*sat-vilakṣaṇa*).
तस्माद्रज्जुसर्पादि तज्ज्ञानं च स्वाधिष्ठानचैतन्याद्विरुद्धस्वभावकतदन्यथाभावरूपत्वाच्चैतन्यविवर्तो भवति ।
Therefore, because the rope-snake etc. and its cognition are an apparent modification possessing a nature opposed to its own substratum Consciousness, they are an apparent modification (*vivarta*) of Consciousness.
ततो रज्जुसर्पादि तज्ज्ञानञ्चाविद्यापरिणामः, चैतन्यस्य विवर्तश्चेति सिद्धम् ।
Hence, it is established that the rope-snake etc. and its cognition are a transformation (*pariṇāma*) of *avidyā* and an apparent modification (*vivarta*) of Consciousness.
149
रज्जुसर्पतज्ज्ञानयोः क्रमेण रज्जूपहितचैतन्यमन्तःकरणोपहितचैतन्यं चाधिष्ठानम् ।
Consciousness conditioned by the rope and Consciousness conditioned by the internal organ are, respectively, the substrata of the rope-snake and its cognition.
रज्जुतत्त्वज्ञानं तयोर्निवर्तकम् ।
The knowledge of the true nature of the rope is the dispeller of both of them.
मिथ्याभूतसर्पाद्यधिष्ठानं रज्ज्वाद्युपहितचैतन्यमेव, न तु रज्ज्वाद्यचेतनम्; रज्ज्वादेरपि सर्पादिवत्कल्पितत्वात् ।
The substratum of the illusory snake etc. is solely Consciousness conditioned by the rope etc., and not the insentient rope etc.; because the rope etc., too, like the snake etc., is superimposed.
न ह्येकं कल्पितं वस्तु कल्पितवस्त्वन्तरस्याधिष्ठानं भवेत् ।
For one superimposed object cannot be the substratum of another superimposed object.
अतो रज्ज्वाद्युपहितचैतन्यमेव सर्पाद्यधिष्ठानम्, न रज्ज्वाद्यचेतनम् ।
Therefore, Consciousness conditioned by the rope etc. alone is the substratum of the snake etc., not the insentient rope etc.
रज्जुविशिष्टचैतन्यस्याधिष्ठानत्वाङ्गीकारे, उभयोः रज्जोश्चैतन्यस्य चाधिष्ठानत्वं भवेत् ।
If Consciousness as qualified by the rope were accepted as the substratum, then both the rope and Consciousness would have to be the substratum.
तत्र रज्जोरधिष्ठानत्वस्य बाधितत्वात्, रज्जूपहितचैतन्यमेवाधिष्ठानं न तु रज्जुविशिष्टचैतन्यम् ।
There, since the rope's status as a substratum is sublated, Consciousness conditioned by the rope alone is the substratum, and not Consciousness qualified by the rope.
तथा सर्पादिज्ञानस्यापि साक्षिचैत1
Similarly, of the cognition of the snake etc., too, the Witness-Conscio[usness alone is the substratum]...
टिप्पणी
1.
उदाहरणं - यथा घटं प्रति मृदुपादानकारणम् ।
For example — just as clay is the material cause with respect to a pot.
कुलालादिर्निमित्तकारणम् ।
The potter and others are the efficient cause.
न्यमेवाधिष्ठानम् ।
[...usness] alone is the substratum.
इत्थं सर्वत्र भ्रमस्थले विषयस्य तज्ज्ञानस्य चोपाधिभेदादधिष्ठानं भिद्यते, नत्वेकम् ।
In this manner, everywhere in instances of illusion, the substratum differs on account of the difference of limiting adjuncts between the object and its cognition; it is not one.
विशेषरूपेण रज्जोरज्ञानं यथाविद्यायां क्षोभोत्पादनद्वारा सर्पादेस्तज्ज्ञानस्य च कारणं तथा विशेषरूपेण रज्जुज्ञानं तदुभयोर्निवृत्तिकारणं भवति ।
Just as ignorance of the rope in its specific form is the cause of the snake etc. and its cognition through generating agitation in avidyā, so the knowledge of the rope in its specific form becomes the cause of the cessation of both of them.
अत्राक्षेपसमाधानानि॥ १५०–१५९ ॥
150 · रज्जुज्ञानेन सर्पनिवृत्तिर्न स्यादित्याक्षेपः
ननु रज्ज्वादिज्ञानेन न सर्पादिर्निवर्तेत ।
[Objection:] If it is argued that the snake etc. would not cease by the knowledge of the rope etc.
मिथ्यावस्तुनो यदधिष्ठानम्, तज्ज्ञानेनैव मिथ्यावस्तु निवर्तेतेत्यद्वैतसिद्धान्तः ।
For the Advaita doctrine is that an illusory object ceases only by the knowledge of whatever is its substratum.
मिथ्याभूतसर्पाद्यधिष्ठानं तु रज्ज्वाद्युपहितचैतन्यमेव, न रज्ज्वादिरिति प्रागभिहितम् ।
And it was previously stated that the substratum of the illusory snake etc. is only consciousness conditioned by the rope etc., not the rope etc. itself.
तस्माद्रज्ज्वादिज्ञानेन न सर्पादिनिवृत्तिर्भवेदिति चेत्-
Therefore, if it is objected that the snake etc. would not cease by the knowledge of the rope etc.—
151 · रज्जुज्ञानमेव सर्पाद्यधिष्ठानज्ञानं भवतीति समाधिः- अत्रोच्यते
रज्ज्वादिजडपदार्थविषयकज्ञानमन्तःकरणवृत्तिरूपम् ।
Knowledge which has insentient objects like a rope for its content is in the form of a vṛtti of the internal organ (antaḥkaraṇa).
वृत्तेस्तु प्रयोजनमावरणभङ्गः ।
The purpose of the vṛtti, however, is the destruction of the veil (āvaraṇa-bhaṅga).
इदञ्चावरणमज्ञानस्य शक्तिः ।
And this veil is the veiling power (āvaraṇa-śakti) of ajñāna.
यस्मादावरणं जडमनाश्रित्य तदधिष्ठानचैतन्यमेवाश्रयति, तस्मादन्तःकरणवृत्त्या रज्ज्वादिविषयाकारापन्नया रज्ज्वाद्यवच्छिन्नचैतन्यावरणमेव भज्यते ।
Because the veil does not rest upon an insentient thing but rests only upon its Consciousness-substratum, therefore, by the vṛtti of the internal organ which has taken the shape of the object (such as the rope), only the veil covering the Consciousness delimited by the rope etc. is destroyed.
वृत्तिस्थचिदाभासस्तु रज्जुमात्रं प्रकाशयति ।
The reflection of Consciousness (cidābhāsa) residing in the vṛtti, on the other hand, illuminates only the rope.
चैतन्यस्य स्वयम्प्रकाशरूपत्वात्तत्प्रकाशाय नाभास उपयुज्यते ।
Because Consciousness is self-luminous by nature, the reflected consciousness (ābhāsa) is not needed for its illumination.
अयमर्थो विस्तरतः उपरिष्टादस्मिन्नेव तरङ्गे कथयिष्यते ।
This subject will be explained in detail later in this very chapter.
इत्थं चिदाभासविशिष्टान्तःकरणवृत्तिरूपज्ञानस्य केवलवृत्तिरूपांशश्चैतन्यनिष्ठावरणं नाशयति, चिदाभासरूपांशस्तु रज्जुं प्रकाशयतीति प्रयोजनद्वयं सिद्ध्यति ।
Thus, in the knowledge consisting of the antaḥkaraṇa-vṛtti qualified by the reflection of Consciousness (cidābhāsa), the mere vṛtti aspect destroys the veil residing in Consciousness, while the cidābhāsa aspect illuminates the rope; thus a twofold purpose is accomplished.
तस्माद्वृत्तिज्ञानस्य न केवलजडात्मकरज्जुर्विषयीभवति ।
Therefore, the purely insentient rope alone does not become the object of vṛtti-knowledge.
किन्त्वधिष्ठानचैतन्येन सहिता रज्जुः चिदाभाससहितवृत्तेर्विषयीभवति ।
Rather, the rope along with its substratum Consciousness becomes the object of the vṛtti coupled with cidābhāsa.
अत एव सिद्धान्तग्रन्थे अन्तःकरणजन्यवृत्तिज्ञानं अखण्डं ब्रह्म विषयीकरोति इत्यभिहितम् ।
For this very reason, it is stated in the doctrinal text: 'The vṛtti-knowledge produced by the antaḥkaraṇa makes indivisible Brahman its object.'
इत्थं यतो रज्जुज्ञानेन भग्नावरणं सत् सर्पाद्यधिष्ठानरज्ज्वाद्यवच्छिन्नचैतन्यं स्वयमेव प्रकाशते, ततो रज्जुज्ञानमेव सर्पाद्यधिष्ठानज्ञानरूपमपि भवति ।
Thus, since the Consciousness delimited by the rope etc. (the substratum of the snake etc.), having its veil removed by the knowledge of the rope, shines of itself, therefore the knowledge of the rope itself is also in the nature of the knowledge of the substratum of the snake etc.
ततश्च रज्जुज्ञानेन सर्पादिनिवृत्तिर्युज्यत एव ।
And therefore, the sublation of the snake etc. by the knowledge of the rope is indeed entirely consistent.
152 · रज्जुज्ञानेन सर्पज्ञानं न निवर्तेतेत्याक्षेपः
ननूक्तप्रकारेण रज्जुज्ञानेन सर्पे निवृत्तेऽपि सर्पविषयकज्ञानं नैव निवर्तेत ।
Now, [an objection is raised:] in the manner stated, even though the snake has ceased through the knowledge of the rope, the cognition having the snake as its object would not cease at all.
सर्पस्याधिष्ठानं रज्ज्ववच्छिन्नचैतन्यम्, सर्पज्ञानस्याधिष्ठानं तु साक्षिचैतन्यमिति भेदः ।
For there is a distinction: the substratum of the snake is Consciousness delimited by the rope, whereas the substratum of the snake-cognition is the witness-Consciousness (sākṣī-caitanya).
उक्तरीत्या तु रज्जुसाक्षात्कारेण रज्ज्ववच्छिन्नचैतन्यमेव प्रकाशेत, न साक्षिचैतन्यम् ।
And according to the method explained, by the direct perception of the rope, only Consciousness delimited by the rope would shine forth, not the witness-Consciousness.
अतो रज्जुज्ञाने उत्पन्नेऽपि सर्पज्ञानाधिष्ठानसाक्षिचैतन्यं नैव ज्ञायते ।
Therefore, even when the knowledge of the rope arises, the witness-Consciousness which is the substratum of the snake-cognition is not known at all.
अज्ञाते चाधिष्ठाने तदारोपितनिवृत्तिर्न दृष्टा, किन्तु ज्ञाते एवाधिष्ठाने ।
And when the substratum is unknown, the cessation of what is superposed upon it is never observed; rather, it is observed only when the substratum is known.
तस्माद्रज्जुज्ञानेन सर्पज्ञानस्य निवृत्तिर्नोपपद्यत इति चेत् ।
Therefore, if it be argued that the cessation of the snake-cognition through the knowledge of the rope is not logically tenable —
सर्पाभावात्सर्पज्ञानस्य कारणे लयरूपनिवृत्तिरिति समाधिः॥ १५३–१५५ ॥
153 · सर्पाभावात्सर्पज्ञानाभावः
अत्रोच्यते ।
Here it is stated in reply:
विषयाधीनं हि ज्ञानं भवति ।
For knowledge is indeed dependent on its object.
रज्जुसाक्षात्कारेणोक्तरीत्या रज्ज्ववच्छिन्नचैतन्यारोपितसर्परूपविषयनिवृत्त्या सर्पज्ञानमपि स्वविषयाभावान्निवर्तत एव ।
By the direct realization of the rope in the manner described, through the sublation of the object in the form of the snake superimposed on the rope-delimited consciousness, the snake-cognition too surely ceases owing to the absence of its own object.
154 · साक्षिज्ञानमन्तरा सर्पज्ञानं न निवर्तेतेत्याक्षेपः
ननु कथमधिष्ठानज्ञानमन्तरा तदारोपितभ्रमो निवर्तेत ।
Objection: How could an illusion superimposed on a substratum cease without knowledge of that substratum?
सर्पज्ञानमपि कल्पितम् ।
The snake-cognition too is illusory.
तस्य ह्यधिष्ठानं साक्षिचैतन्यम् ।
For its substratum is the witness-consciousness (*sākṣi-caitanya*).
तज्ज्ञानमन्तरा तत्र कल्पितसर्पज्ञानं न निवर्तेतेति चेत्-
