If it be argued that without knowledge of that (*sākṣin*), the snake-cognition superimposed upon it would not cease —
155
साक्षिज्ञानमन्तरापि सर्पज्ञानं निवर्तेतेति समाधानमत्राप्युच्यते ।
The resolution is stated here: even without knowledge of the *sākṣin*, the snake-cognition can cease.
निवृत्तिर्द्विविधा - आत्यन्तिकनिवृत्तिः, कारणात्मनावस्थितिरूपा निवृत्तिश्चेति ।
Cessation is of two kinds: absolute cessation (*ātyantika-nivṛtti*), and cessation in the form of abiding as the cause (*kāraṇātmanāvasthiti-rūpā nivṛtti*).
स्वकारणेन सहैव कार्यस्य निवृत्तिरात्यन्तिकी निवृत्तिरित्युच्यते ।
The cessation of an effect along with its very cause is called absolute cessation (*ātyantikī nivṛttiḥ*).
कल्पितवस्तूनां सर्वेषां कारणं तु तदधिष्ठानचैतन्याश्रिततदावारकाज्ञानमेव ।
The cause of all superimposed objects, however, is solely the *avidyā* that rests in their substratum-consciousness and veils it.
तस्मादधिष्ठानचैतन्यापरोक्षज्ञानेनैवाज्ञानं तत्कार्यञ्च सर्वमारोपितं निःशेषं निवर्तते ।
Therefore, by the direct knowledge of the substratum-consciousness alone, *avidyā* and all its superimposed effects cease completely without residue.
कार्यस्य कारणे लयरूपनिवृत्तिस्तु विनाप्यधिष्ठानज्ञानं जायेत ।
However, the cessation of an effect in the form of dissolution (*laya*) into its cause can occur even without knowledge of the substratum.
सुषुप्तौ प्रलये च सकलपदार्थानां विनैवाधिष्ठानज्ञानमज्ञाने स्वकारणे लयो भवति ।
In deep sleep and cosmic dissolution, the dissolution of all entities into their material cause, *avidyā*, occurs even without knowledge of the substratum.
तदा सर्वदृश्यपदार्थलयहेतुस्तत्तद्भोगप्रदकर्मोपरम एव ।
At that time, the cause for the dissolution of all perceived entities is solely the cessation of the *karma* that yields their respective experiences.
एवमेवान्तराप्यधिष्ठानसाक्षिज्ञानम्, सर्पज्ञानं निवर्तते ।
Just in this way, even without knowledge of the substratum witness, the snake-cognition ceases.
तत्र सर्पज्ञानविषयीभूतसर्पाभाव एव सर्पज्ञाननिवृत्तेः कारणं भवति ।
In that case, the absence of the snake that was the object of the snake-cognition is itself the cause of the cessation of the snake-cognition.
इत्थं च रज्जुज्ञानेन सर्पो निवर्तते, ततश्च सर्पज्ञानविषयीभूतसर्पाभाव एव सर्पज्ञानस्य लयरूपनिवृत्तौ निमित्तं भवति ।
Thus, by the knowledge of the rope the snake ceases, and consequently the absence of the snake which was the object of the snake-cognition serves as the occasioning cause for the cessation of the snake-cognition in the form of dissolution.
156 · रज्जुज्ञानसमये सर्पज्ञानाधिष्ठानभूतसाक्षिभानमपि सम्भवतीति समाधानं
अथवा सर्पस्तज्ज्ञानं चेत्युभयमपि रज्जुज्ञानेनैव निवर्तते ।
Or rather, both the snake and its cognition are removed by the knowledge of the rope alone.
तथा हि, रज्जुसाक्षात्कारसमयेऽन्तःकरणं नेत्रद्वारा बहिर्निर्गत्य रज्जुदेशं प्राप्य तत्समानाकारं भवति ।
To explain: at the time of the direct perception of the rope, the internal organ goes out through the eye, reaches the locus of the rope, and assumes a form identical with it.
अतो रज्जुसाक्षात्कारसमये वृत्त्युपहितचैतन्यं रज्जूपहितचैतन्यञ्चेत्युभयमप्येकीभवति ।
Therefore, at the time of the direct perception of the rope, both the Consciousness conditioned by the vṛtti and the Consciousness conditioned by the rope become unified.
न तयोरस्ति भेदः ।1
There is no difference between the two.
टिप्पणी
1.
पटस्य स्वोपादानभूततन्तुभिः सह दाहः आत्यन्तिकनिवृत्तिः ।
The burning of a cloth along with the threads that are its material cause is absolute cessation (ātyantika-nivṛtti).
घटस्य ध्वंसे मृद्भावापत्तौ लयरूपनिवृत्तिः ।
Upon the destruction of a pot, when it attains the nature of clay, it is cessation in the form of dissolution (laya-rūpa-nivṛtti).
अत्रायं हेतुः - न हि क्वचिदपि चैतन्यस्यास्ति भेदः स्वरूपतः, किन्तूपाधिनिबन्धन एव सः ।
Here this is the reason: indeed, nowhere is there any intrinsic difference in Consciousness; rather, that difference is solely caused by adjuncts (upādhis).
वृत्त्युपहितचैतन्यस्य रज्जूपहितचैतन्यस्य च भेदप्रयोजकोपाधिर्वृत्ती रज्जुश्च ।
The adjuncts causing the difference between the Consciousness conditioned by the vṛtti and the Consciousness conditioned by the rope are the vṛtti and the rope.
यदा वृत्ती रज्जुश्चेत्युपधिद्वयं विभिन्नदेशस्थं तदा तदुपहितचैतन्ययोर्भेदः सिद्ध्यति ।
When the two adjuncts, namely the vṛtti and the rope, are located in different places, then a difference between the Consciousnesses conditioned by them is established.
यदा तूपाध्योरेकदेशस्थत्वं भवति तदा नोपहितचैतन्ययोर्भेदः ।
When, however, the two adjuncts are situated in the same place, then there is no difference between the conditioned Consciousnesses.
अयमर्थो वेदान्तपरिभाषादिग्रन्थेषु प्रसिद्धः ।
This point is well known in texts such as the Vedāntaparibhāṣā.
विभिन्नदेशस्थोपाधिभ्यामेवोपहितचैतन्ययोर्भेदः कल्प्यते ।
Difference between the conditioned Consciousnesses is posited solely because of the two adjuncts being in different places.
द्वयोरप्युपाध्योरेकदेशस्थत्वे तु ताभ्यामुपहितं चैतन्यमप्येकमेवेति सिद्ध्यति ।
When, however, both adjuncts reside in the same place, it is established that the Consciousness conditioned by them is also one alone.
उक्तरीत्या रज्जुसाक्षात्कारदशायां रज्जूपहितचैतन्यं वृत्त्युपहितचैतन्यञ्चेत्येतदुभयमेकीभवति ।
In the manner stated, during the state of the direct perception of the rope, both the Consciousness conditioned by the rope and the Consciousness conditioned by the vṛtti become unified.
तत्र साक्षिचैतन्यमेव वृत्त्युपहितचैतन्यमित्युच्यते, अन्तःकरणे तद्वृत्तौ च स्थित्वाप्यसङ्गतया तयोरवभासकचैतन्यमात्रस्य साक्षित्वाभिधानात् ।
There, the Witness-Consciousness alone is designated as the Consciousness conditioned by the vṛtti, because Consciousness alone which, though residing in the internal organ and its modification, illuminates them remaining unattached, is called the sākṣin.
उक्तरीत्या रज्जुसाक्षात्कारसमये साक्षिचैतन्यस्य रज्जूपहितचैतन्यस्य चाभेदः सिद्धः ।
In the manner stated, at the time of the direct realization of the rope, the non-difference between the Witness-Consciousness and the Consciousness conditioned by the rope is established.
रज्जूपहितचैतन्यं च रज्जुज्ञानेनावभासते ।
And the Consciousness conditioned by the rope shines forth through the knowledge of the rope.
रज्जूपहितचैतन्यादपृथग्भूतं साक्षिचैतन्यमपि रज्जुज्ञानेनैवावभासते ।
The Witness-Consciousness, which is non-separate from the Consciousness conditioned by the rope, also shines forth through the knowledge of the rope alone.
एवं रज्जुसाक्षात्कारसमये सर्पज्ञानाधिष्ठानभूतसाक्षिचैतन्यस्य भानसत्त्वात्, तत्र कल्पितसर्पज्ञानस्यापि निवृत्तिः सम्भवति ।
Thus, since the Witness-Consciousness which is the substratum of the snake cognition shines forth at the time of the direct perception of the rope, the cessation of the imagined snake cognition superposed on it is also possible.
157 · सकलत्रिपुटीभानसमये साक्षिभानमवश्यं भवतीति निरूपणं
अथवा कूटस्थदीपे विद्यारण्यमुनिभिरित्थमुक्तं - अन्तःकरणस्य वृत्तिश्चिदाभाससहिता चक्षुरादिकरणद्वारा बहिर्निर्गत्य घटादिविषयान् प्रकाशयति । तत्र घटादिरूपो विषयः, चिदाभाससहितवृत्तिरूपं घटादिविषयकं ज्ञानम्, चिदाभाससहितान्तःकरणरूपो ज्ञाता; एतत्त्रयमपि साक्षी प्रकाशयति इति ।
Or rather, in the Kūṭasthadīpa chapter, sage Vidyāraṇya has stated: 'The mental mode accompanied by the reflection of Consciousness goes out through the sense-doors such as the eye and illumines external objects like a pot. There, the object is of the form of the pot etc.; the cognition having pot etc. as its object is of the form of the mental mode accompanied by reflected Consciousness; and the knower is of the form of the mind accompanied by reflected Consciousness; and the sākṣin illumines all three of these.'
अस्यायमर्थः - अयं घटः इति ज्ञाने साभासान्तःकरणवृत्त्या घटमात्रं प्रकाशते ।
The meaning of this is: in the cognition 'This is a pot', by the mental mode endowed with the reflected Consciousness, the pot alone shines forth.
घटमहं जानामि इत्यत्र तु अहम् इति शब्दस्यार्थो यो ज्ञाता, घट इति यो ज्ञेयः, जानामि इति यत् घटविषयकं ज्ञानम्, इत्येतत् त्रयमपि त्रिपुटीरूपं साक्षी प्रकाशयतीति ।
In the experience 'I know the pot', however, the knower denoted by the word 'I', the known object denoted by 'pot', and the knowledge of the pot denoted by 'I know' — this entire triad (triputī) is illumined by the sākṣin.
ज्ञाता, ज्ञेयम्, ज्ञानं चेत्येतत् त्रयमपि त्रिपुटीत्युच्यते ।
The knower, the known, and the knowledge — this triad is called the tripuṭī.
इत्थमेव सर्वत्र निखिलत्रिपुटीप्रकाशकः साक्ष्येव ।
In this very manner, everywhere, the illuminer of the entire tripuṭī is the sākṣin alone.
यदि साक्षी स्वयमज्ञातः स्यात् तदा त्रिपुटीज्ञानं न साक्षिणा ज्ञायेत ।
If the sākṣin itself were unknown, then the knowledge of the tripuṭī would not be known by the sākṣin.
तस्मात्सकलत्रिपुटीज्ञानदशायां साक्षिज्ञानमप्यवश्यं जायत एव स्वयम्प्रकाशत्वात्साक्षिणः, इत्यभ्युपेयम् ।
Therefore, at the time of any cognition of the tripuṭī, the manifestation of the sākṣin also necessarily occurs, because the sākṣin is self-luminous — this must be accepted.
अनेन च साक्षिज्ञानेन सर्पज्ञानं निवर्तते ।
And through this shining forth of the sākṣin, the cognition of the snake is removed.
उक्तरीत्या सर्पादिमिथ्याविषयस्य तज्ज्ञानस्य च पृथगेवाधिष्ठानमित्यभ्युपगमपक्षे इयन्त्याक्षेपसमाधानानि समभवन् ।
In the stated manner, under the position that the illusory object like a snake and its cognition have separate substrata, so many objections and answers had to be raised.
158 · मिथ्यासर्पस्य तज्ज्ञानस्य चाधिष्ठानं साक्ष्येवेति निरूपणं
मिथ्यासर्पस्य तज्ज्ञानस्य च पृथगधिष्ठानत्वपक्षे दोषात्तयोरेकमेवाधिष्ठानमितीदानीं निरूप्यते ।
Because of defects in the view that the illusory snake and its cognition have separate substrata, it is now expounded that they have only one single substratum.
तत्र न हि बाह्यरज्ज्ववच्छिन्नचैतन्यं सर्पस्य तज्ज्ञानस्य चाधिष्ठानं भवतीति शक्यते वक्तुम् ।
There, it cannot indeed be said that the Consciousness delimited by the external rope is the substratum of both the snake and its cognition.
यावन्ति ज्ञानानि जायन्ते तानि सर्वाण्यपि प्रमातारं साक्षिणं वाश्रित्य जायन्त इति नियमः ।
For there is a rule that whatever cognitions arise, they all arise resting upon either the knower (pramātṛ) or the witness (sākṣin).
तस्मात् बाह्यरज्ज्ववच्छिन्नचैतन्यं न सर्पज्ञानस्याश्रयो भवितुमर्हति ।
Therefore, the Consciousness delimited by the external rope cannot be the locus of the cognition of the snake.
सर्पस्य तद्विषयकभ्रमरूपज्ञानस्य चाधिष्ठानमन्तःकरणोपहितसाक्षिचैतन्यमित्यभ्युपगमे शरीस्यान्तरेवान्तःकरणप्रदेशे सर्पोपलब्धिरभ्युपगन्तव्या स्यात्, न तु बाह्यरज्जुदेशे ।
And if it were accepted that the substratum of both the snake and the erroneous cognition regarding it is the witness Consciousness conditioned by the mind, then one would have to accept that the perception of the snake occurs only inside the body in the region of the mind, and not in the external location of the rope.
अन्तेरेवोत्पन्नः सर्पो मायाबलेन बहिरवभासते इत्यङ्गीकारे आत्मख्यातिमतसिद्धिः प्रसज्यते ।
If it is asserted that the snake, produced only internally, appears outside by the power of māyā, it would result in accepting the doctrine of Ātmakhyāti (the Buddhist idealist view of error).
तच्च प्रागेव खण्डितम् ।
And that has already been refuted earlier.
इत्थं रज्जूपहितचैतन्यस्य सर्पज्ञानाधिष्ठानत्वासम्भवात्, अन्तःकरणोपहितचैतन्यस्य सर्पाधिष्ठानत्वासम्भवाच्च मिथ्यासर्पतज्ज्ञानयोरेकाधिष्ठानत्वपक्षो यद्यप्यसङ्गत इति भाति, तथापि वक्ष्यमाणरीत्या अन्तःकरणवृत्त्युपहितचैतन्यस्योभयाधिष्ठानत्वसम्भवान्न दोषः ।
Thus, since the rope-conditioned Consciousness cannot be the substratum of the snake-cognition, and the mind-conditioned Consciousness cannot be the substratum of the snake, although the position of a single substratum for both the illusory snake and its cognition might seem untenable, nevertheless, in the manner to be explained, because the Consciousness conditioned by the mental mode can serve as the substratum of both, there is no defect.
तथा हि, चक्षुर्द्वारा रज्जुदेशं गतस्यान्तःकरणस्येदमाकारवृत्त्युपहितचैतन्याश्रिताविद्या सर्पाकारेण तज्ज्ञानाकारेण च परिणमते ।
To explain: the avidyā residing in the Consciousness conditioned by the 'this'-formed mode of the mind, which has reached the location of the rope through the eye, transforms into the form of the snake and into the form of its cognition.
वृत्त्युपहितचैतन्यस्थाविद्यायास्तमोगुणांशः सर्पस्योपादानकारणम्; तस्या एव सत्त्वगुणांशः सर्पज्ञानस्योपादानकारणम् ।
The tamoguṇa aspect of the avidyā located in the mode-conditioned Consciousness is the material cause of the snake; the sattvaguṇa aspect of that very same avidyā is the material cause of the snake-cognition.
एवं सर्पतज्ज्ञानयोर्वृत्त्युपहितचैतन्यमेवाधिष्ठानम् ।
Thus, the Consciousness conditioned by the mental mode alone is the substratum of both the snake and its cognition.
अन्तःकरणवृत्तेर्बाह्यरज्जुदेशस्थत्वात्तद्वृत्त्युपहितचैतन्यमपि बहिरेवास्ते ।
Because the mental mode is situated at the external locus of the rope, the Consciousness conditioned by that mode is also located outside alone.
अतस्तदेव सर्पस्याश्रयः ।
Therefore, that very Consciousness is the locus of the snake.
अन्तःकरणस्य स्वरूपं यावत्तावदेव साक्षिस्वरूपमपि ।
To whatever extent the mind extends, to that exact extent is the sākṣin as well.
शरीरान्तःस्थान्तःकरणमेव वृत्तिरूपेण परिणतम् ।
The mind situated inside the body has itself transformed into the form of the vṛtti.
तस्माद्वृत्त्युपहितचैतन्यं साक्षी भवति ।
Therefore, the Consciousness conditioned by the mental mode is indeed the sākṣin.
अतस्तदेव सर्पज्ञानस्याश्रयः ।
Hence, that very Consciousness is the locus of the snake-cognition.
रज्जुप्रत्यक्षकाले रज्जूपहितचैतन्यवृत्त्युपहितचैतन्ययोरेकीभावात् रज्जुज्ञानेनैव मिथ्यासर्पतज्ज्ञानयोर्निवृत्तिरुपपद्यते ।
At the time of direct perception of the rope, due to the unification of the rope-conditioned Consciousness and the mode-conditioned Consciousness, the sublation of both the illusory snake and its cognition by the knowledge of the rope alone becomes fully justified.
159 · एकस्यामेव रज्जौ नानापुरुषाणां भिन्नभिन्नभ्रमादपि साक्षिचैतन्यमेव भ्रमाधिष्ठानं
किञ्चैकस्यामेव रज्ज्वां नानापुरुषाणां भिन्नभिन्नाः भ्रमाः भवन्ति - यथा कस्यचित् सर्प इति, अन्यस्य दण्ड इति, अपरस्य मालेति, एकस्य भूच्छिद्रमिति, इतरस्य तैलधारेति च ।
Furthermore, in one and the same rope, diverse illusions arise in different persons — such as 'a snake' for one, 'a stick' for another, 'a garland' for a third, 'a crack in the earth' for one, and 'a stream of oil' for another.
अथवा सर्वेषां सर्प इत्येकरीत्यैव भ्रमो जायताम् ।
Or, let the illusion arise uniformly for all of them as 'a snake'.
तत्र यस्य पुरुषस्य रज्जुसाक्षात्कारो जायते तस्यैव तदीयवृत्त्यवच्छिन्नचैतन्ये कल्पितोऽध्यासो निवर्तते ।
There, the superimposed *adhyāsa* imagined upon the *cit* delimited by the *vṛtti* ceases for that person alone in whom direct perception of the rope occurs.
यस्य तु रज्जुसाक्षात्कारो न भवति तस्याध्यासनिवृत्तिर्नास्ति ।
However, for him who does not have direct perception of the rope, there is no cessation of the superimposition.
तस्मात् वृत्त्यवच्छिन्नचैतन्यमेव कल्पितानां सर्वेषामधिष्ठानम्, न तु रज्ज्वादिविषयोपहितचैतन्यम् ।
Therefore, the *cit* delimited by the *vṛtti* alone is the substratum (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of all superimposed objects, and not the *cit* conditioned by the external object such as the rope.
रज्जूपहितचैतन्यस्य सर्पदण्डाद्यधिष्ठानत्वे नानापुरुषाणां भिन्नभिन्नतया प्रतीयमानानि सर्पदण्डादीनि वस्तूनि सर्वाण्यपि, एकैकस्यापि पुरुषस्य प्रतीयेरन्; न तु तथा प्रतीयते ।
If the *cit* conditioned by the rope were the substratum of snake, stick, etc., then all the objects such as snake and stick perceived differently by various people would be perceived by each and every person; but it is not perceived in that manner.
वृत्त्युपहितचैतन्यस्य मिथ्यासर्पाद्यधिष्ठानत्ववादिमतरीत्या तु न दोषः ।
However, according to the doctrine which maintains that the *cit* conditioned by the *vṛtti* is the substratum of the illusory snake, etc., there is no such defect.
यस्य पुरुषस्य वृत्त्युपहितचैतन्ये यद्वस्तु कल्पितं तद्वस्तु तस्यैव प्रतीयते, नान्यस्येति वक्तुं शक्यत्वात् ।
Because it is possible to state that whatever object is superimposed on the *vṛtti*-conditioned *cit* of a particular person, that object is perceived by him alone and not by another.
इत्थं बाह्यभ्रमविषयसर्पादीनां तज्ज्ञानानां च वृत्त्युपहितसाक्षिचैतन्यमेवाधिष्ठानम् ।
Thus, the witness-consciousness (*sākṣi-caitanya*) conditioned by the *vṛtti* alone is the substratum of external illusory objects like snakes and also of their cognitions.
स्वप्नोपलब्धपदार्थानां तज्ज्ञानानां चान्तःकरणोपहितसाक्ष्येवाधिष्ठानम् ।
And of objects experienced in dream and of their cognitions, the witness (*sākṣin*) conditioned by the *antaḥkaraṇa* alone is the substratum.
एवं च सदसद्विलक्षणानर्वचनीयाविद्यायाः परिणामभूतानिर्वचनीयसर्पादीनां ख्यातिः = प्रतीतिः = प्रसिद्धिः = स्फुरणमभिवदनञ्च अनिर्वचनीयख्यातिः इत्युच्यते ।
And thus, the cognition (*khyāti* = perception = known appearance = shining forth and verbal expression) of illusory snakes etc., which are the transformations of *avidyā* that is indeterminable (*anirvacanīya*) and distinct from real and unreal, is termed *anirvacanīya-khyāti*.
160 · मिथ्याजगत आधाराधिष्ठानविषयकप्रश्नः
हे स्वामिन् ।
O Master!
प्रतीयमानस्यापारस्य मिथ्याभूतस्यास्य जगत आधारः कः ।
What is the support (*ādhāra*) of this boundless, illusory world that is being perceived?
अधिष्ठानं च किम् ।
And what is its substratum (*adhiṣṭhāna*)?
कृपया वद मे प्रभो ।
Please tell me, O Lord!
इति तत्त्वदृष्टिः पृच्छति ।
Thus does Tattvadṛṣṭi ask.
पूर्वप्रश्नस्योत्तरम्॥ १६१–१६२ ॥
161 · मिथ्याजगत आत्मैवाधारोऽधिष्ठानं च
हे शिष्य ।
O disciple!
त्वन्निजस्वरूपाज्ञानात् (आत्मनो ब्रह्मरूपेणाज्ञानात्) तवेदं मिथ्याजगत् प्रतिभासते ।
Due to ignorance of your own true nature (i.e. due to not knowing the *ātman* as Brahman), this illusory world appears to you.
अतस्त्वमेवास्य जगत आधारोऽधिष्ठानं च ।
Therefore, you yourself are both the support (*ādhāra*) and the substratum (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of this world.
रज्ज्वज्ञानान्मिथ्याभूतः सर्पः प्रतिभासते ।
Due to ignorance of the rope, the illusory snake appears.
तत्र मिथ्याभूतसर्पादीनां रज्जुराधारोऽधिष्ठानं च भवति ।
In that case, the rope is both the support and the substratum of the illusory snake and so forth.
यद्यपि मुख्यसिद्धान्तभूतद्वितीयपक्षे मिथ्यासर्पाद्यधिष्ठानं वृत्त्युपहितचैतन्यमिति प्रथमपक्षे रज्जूपहितचैतन्यमिति चोक्तत्वान्न कस्मिंश्चिदपि पक्षे रज्ज्वादि जडमधिष्ठानं भवति, तथापि प्रथमपक्षे चैतन्यनिष्ठाधिष्ठानत्वे रज्जुरुपाधिर्भवतीत्यतः स्थूलदृष्ट्या रज्जुरेवाधिष्ठानमित्युच्यते ।
Although in neither view is the inert rope etc. the substratum — since in the primary conclusive second view the substratum of the illusory snake etc. is stated to be *vṛtti*-conditioned *cit*, and in the first view to be rope-conditioned *cit* — nevertheless, in the first view, because the rope serves as the *upādhi* for the substratum-hood abiding in *cit*, from a gross perspective the rope itself is said to be the substratum.
मिथ्याभूतसर्पादेर्यथा रज्जुरधिष्ठानमाधारश्च भवति तथा मिथ्याजगतस्त्वमेवाधिष्ठानमाधारश्च भवसि ।
Just as the rope is the substratum and support of the illusory snake and the like, even so you alone are the substratum and support of the illusory world.
162 · आत्मनः सामान्यरूपमाधारः, विशेषरूपमधिष्ठानमत्रेदमाकूतं
रज्जोः स्वरूपद्वयमस्ति, एकं सामान्यरूपम्, अपरं विशेषरूपमिति च ।
The rope has two aspects of nature: one is its general form, and the other is its specific form.
तत्र इयम् इति सामान्यरूपम्; रज्जुः इति विशेषरूपम् ।
Between those two, 'this' is the general aspect, while 'rope' is the specific aspect.
अयं सर्पः इति भ्रान्तिदशायां मिथ्याभूतसर्पेण तादात्म्यापन्नं सद्भासमानं अयम् इति यत्स्वरूपं तत् सामान्यरूपम् ।
That nature which appears as 'this', having attained identity with the illusory snake during the state of error 'This is a snake', is the general form.
भ्रान्तिदशायां यत्स्वरूपं न भासते, यस्य स्वरूपस्य साक्षात्कारमात्रेण भ्रमो निवर्तते तदेव रज्जोः विशेषरूपम् ।
That specific nature of the rope which does not appear during the state of error, and by the mere direct perception of which the delusion ceases, is its specific form.
एवं आत्मनोऽप्येकं सामान्यरूपमपरं विशेषरूपमिति रूपद्वयमस्ति ।
Likewise, for the ātman too there are two forms: one general form and another specific form.
तत्र सद्रूपं सामान्यरूपम्, असङ्गत्वकूटस्थत्वनित्यत्वशुद्धत्वमुक्तत्वादि विशेषरूपम् ।
Among these, the nature of pure Existence is the general form; unattachedness, immutability, eternity, purity, ever-free nature, and so forth constitute the specific form.
तथा हि, स्थूलसूक्ष्मशरीरसङ्घातोऽस्ति इति कार्यकरणसङ्घातभ्रान्तिदशायामपि मिथ्याभूतकार्यकरणसङ्घातादभिन्नतया सद्रूपं प्रकाशते ।
To explain: even during the state of delusion regarding the aggregate of body and organs, as in 'The aggregate of gross and subtle bodies exists', the nature of Existence shines forth as non-different from the illusory aggregate of body and senses.
अत एव सद्रूपमात्मनः सामान्यरूपं इत्युच्यते ।
Therefore, the nature of pure Existence is called the general form of the ātman.
कार्यकरणसङ्घातभ्रमसमये आत्मनोऽसङ्गत्वकूटस्थत्वनित्यत्वशुद्धत्वमुक्तत्वादिस्वरूपं न प्रतिभाति ।
At the time of delusion concerning the aggregate of body and sense organs, the nature of the ātman characterized by unattachedness, immutability, eternity, purity, ever-free state, etc. does not appear.
आत्मनोऽसङ्गत्वादिस्वरूपेण भाने तु शरीरादिसङ्घातभ्रमो निःशेषं निवर्तते ।
However, upon the manifestation of the ātman in its nature as unattachedness and so forth, the error regarding the aggregate of body and senses ceases without remainder.
तस्मादसङ्गत्वकूटस्थत्वनित्यत्वशुद्धत्वमुक्तत्वाद्वितीयत्वव्यापकत्वादिकमात्मनो विशेषरूपम् ।
Therefore, unattachedness, immutability, eternity, purity, ever-free state, non-duality, all-pervasiveness, and so forth constitute the specific form of the ātman.
समस्तभ्रमेषु सामान्यरूपं आधारः इति विशेषरूपं अधिष्ठानं इति चोच्यते ।
In all superimpositions, the general aspect is called the substratum (ādhāra), and the specific aspect is called the ground (adhiṣṭhāna).
मिथ्यासर्पाश्रयभूतरज्जोः इयम् इति सामान्यरूपं सर्पस्याधारः, रज्जुः इति विशेषरूपं अधिष्ठानं च यथा भवति, तथा मिथ्याप्रपञ्चाश्रयभूतात्मनः सामान्यात्मकसद्रूपं प्रपञ्चस्याधारः, असङ्गत्वाद्वितीयत्वादिविशेषरूपं अधिष्ठानं च भवति ।
Just as in the rope that is the locus of the illusory snake, the general aspect 'this' is the substratum (ādhāra) of the snake, and the specific aspect 'rope' is the ground (adhiṣṭhāna); exactly so, of the ātman who is the locus of the illusory universe, the general aspect of pure Existence is the substratum of the universe, and the specific aspect consisting of unattachedness, non-duality, etc., is its ground.
अयं च विभाग आधाराधिष्ठानयोः श्रीमच्छङ्करभगवत्पादाचार्यप्रशिष्यभूतसर्वज्ञात्ममुनीन्द्रेण सङ्क्षेपशारीरकाख्यग्रन्थे प्रदर्शितः ।
And this distinction between substratum (ādhāra) and ground (adhiṣṭhāna) has been expounded by the great sage Sarvajñātman, the grand-disciple of Śrīmat Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda, in his treatise named Saṅkṣepa-śārīraka.
163
मिथ्याजगत आत्मनोऽन्यो द्रष्टा वक्तव्य इति प्रश्नः—
The question stating that a seer of the illusory world distinct from the ātman must be explained:
हे स्वामिन् श्रीसद्गुरो !
O Master, venerable True Guru!
को वास्य मिथ्याभूतजगतो द्रष्टा भवेत् ।
Who indeed could be the seer of this illusory world?
न ह्यस्य मिथ्याजगत आधाराधिष्ठानोभयात्मक आत्मैव द्रष्टा भवितुमर्हति ।
For the ātman itself, which is of the nature of both substratum and ground of this illusory world, cannot reasonably be its seer.
तथा अदृष्टत्वात् ।
Because such a thing is never seen in experience.
तस्मात् सर्वजगत आधाराधिष्ठानभावेन स्थितत्वादात्मनस्तदन्येनैव केनचित् तद्द्रष्ट्रा भाव्यम् ।
Therefore, since the ātman exists as the substratum and ground of the entire universe, its seer must be someone other than it.
सर्पाद्याधाराधिष्ठानभूतरज्ज्वादेरन्य एव तद्द्रष्टा पुरुषो यथा भवति, तद्वत् ।
Just as the person who sees the snake is someone entirely distinct from the rope, etc., which serves as its substratum and ground, so it must be here.
शिष्यःको वास्ति जगतोऽस्य द्रष्टा प्रत्यगात्मनोऽन्यः इति शिष्यः पृच्छति ।
'Who then is the seer of this world distinct from the inner ātman?' — thus the disciple asks.
164 · तत्र समाधानं
लोके यद्यन्मिथ्यावस्तु, तत्सर्वं स्वाधिष्ठाने कल्पितं भवति ।
In the world, whatever illusory object exists, all of that is superimposed upon its own substratum.
अधिष्ठानं च द्विविधम्, एकं चेतनात्मकमपरं जडात्मकमिति ।
And the substratum is twofold: one of the nature of consciousness (*cit*), and the other of the nature of insentient matter (*jaḍa*).
यत्राधिष्ठानं जडमित्यङ्गीक्रियते, तत्राधिष्ठानादन्य एव द्रष्टा भवति ।
Where the substratum is admitted to be insentient, there the seer is distinct from the substratum.
यत्र चेतनमधिष्ठानम्, तत्र स्वस्मिन्नारोपितस्य सर्वस्याधिष्ठानमेव द्रष्टृ, नान्यत् ।
Where consciousness is the substratum, there the substratum itself is the seer of everything superimposed upon itself, and nothing else.
यथा स्वप्नप्रचञ्चस्याधिष्ठानं साक्षिचैतन्यम्; तदेव तद्द्रष्टृ च भवति ।
Just as the *sākṣin*-consciousness is the substratum of the dream-world, and that very consciousness is also the seer of that dream.
एवमेवास्य जाग्रज्जगतोऽप्यात्मैवाधिष्ठानम्; स एव तस्य द्रष्टा च ।
In the exact same way, the *ātman* alone is the substratum of this waking world as well, and it alone is its seer.
मन्दाधिकारिसमाधानार्थं स्थूलदृष्ट्या रज्ज्वादिकं सर्पाद्यध्यासाधिष्ठानमित्याश्रित्यैतादृशशङ्कासमाधाने कृते ।
Such objection and resolution were previously framed from a gross viewpoint, assuming the rope and the like to be the substrata of superimpositions like the snake, only for the sake of satisfying dull qualified aspirants.
परमार्थतस्त्वद्वैतसिद्धान्ते सर्पाद्यध्यासाधिष्ठानं साक्षिचैतन्यमेव, द्रष्टृ च तदेव ।
In ultimate truth, however, in the Advaita doctrine, the substratum of the superimposition of snake etc. is only the *sākṣin*-consciousness, and that very consciousness alone is the seer.
तस्मात् कल्पितसकलदृश्याण्डकोटिसहस्राणामधिष्ठानभूतात्मैव द्रष्टा ।
Therefore, the *ātman* alone, being the substratum of thousands of crores of superimposed observable universes, is the seer.
गुरुःनास्मिन् पक्षे शङ्कासमाधानादिकं प्रसज्यत इति गुरुराह ।
'In this view, no objection, resolution, etc., ever arises' — thus declared the Guru.
165 · मिथ्यासंसारनिवर्तनेच्छा नोचिता
हे सोम्य ।
O gentle one!
इत्थं मिथ्याभूतं संसारदुःखं भ्रान्त्या त्वयि प्रतिभासते ।
In this manner, the illusory suffering of *saṃsāra* appears in you merely through error.
तस्मान्मिथ्यासंसारदुःखनिविवृत्सा तव न युज्यते ।
Therefore, the desire to eradicate the unreal sorrow of *saṃsāra* is not appropriate for you.
तत्रायं दृष्टान्तः - यदि कश्चन मान्त्रिकः कस्मैचित् पुरुषाय स्वमन्त्रप्रभावान्मिथ्याभूतं शत्रुं प्रदर्शयति, तदा तच्छत्रुविनाशाय न स पुरुषो यतते; तद्वन्मिथ्याभूतसंसारनिवृत्तये तवेच्छा न युज्यते ।
Here is an illustration for this: if a magician displays an illusory enemy to some person through the power of his mantra, that person does not strive for the destruction of that illusory enemy; similarly, your desire for the cessation of illusory *saṃsāra* is not appropriate.
तथा चोक्तं गौडपादैर्माण्डूक्योपनिषत्कारिकायाम्- प्रपञ्चो यदि विद्येत निवर्तेत न संशयः । मायामात्रमिदं द्वैतमद्वैतं परमार्थतः ॥ (मा. आ. १७) इति ।
And so it has been stated by Gauḍapādācārya in the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad Kārikā: If the world-phenomenon really existed, it would certainly cease to be; this duality is mere *māyā*, non-duality is the ultimate reality. (मा. आ. १७)
तथा वराहोपनिषदि चोक्तम्- अज्ञानमेव न कुतो जगतः प्रसङ्गो जीवेशदेशिकविकल्पकथातिदूरे । एकान्तनिर्मलचिदेकरसस्वरूपं ब्रह्मैव केवलमहं परिपूर्णमस्मि ॥ इति ।
Likewise, it is declared in the Varāha Upaniṣad: There is no ignorance at all; whence can there be any talk of the world? Any discourse regarding distinctions of jīva, Īśvara, and Guru is infinitely far away. I am Brahman alone, absolute, all-full, whose very nature is singular, ever-pure consciousness.
166 · मिथ्यासंसारस्यापि दुःखहेतुत्वात्तन्निवृत्त्युपायप्रश्नः
हे स्वामिन् ।
O Master!
जगत् त्वयि मिथ्यैव स्वप्नादिवत् प्रतिभाति, न चास्ति तत् परमार्थसद्रूपेण इति यदुक्तं तत्सत्यमेव ।
What was stated—that 'The world appears in you merely as illusory, like a dream etc., and it does not exist in the form of absolute reality'—is certainly true.
तथापि, यथा मयि मिथ्यारूपेण वा रूपान्तरेण वा स जननमरणादिरूपः संसारो न प्रतिभासेत, तथा उपायः कृपयोपदिश्यतां मह्यम् ।
Even so, please graciously instruct me in the means such that this saṃsāra, consisting of birth and death, may not appear in me either in an illusory form or in any other form.
मिथ्याभूतसंसारनिवृत्तये साधनान्वेषणं तव न युज्यते इति भवदुक्तं यद्यपि सत्यमेव तथापि यस्य मिथ्यापदार्थो दुःखहेतुर्भवति तेन स मिथ्यापदार्थस्तन्निवृत्तिसाधनैर्निवर्तनीय एव भवति ।
Although what you said—that 'Searching for a means to remove illusory saṃsāra is not fitting for you'—is true, nevertheless, for whoever an illusory object causes suffering, by him that illusory object must indeed be eliminated through the means of its removal.
तथा हि, कस्यचित् प्रतिदिनं भयङ्करदुःस्वप्नदर्शनं जायते ।
To illustrate: someone has terrifying nightmares every day.
स च मिथ्याभूतस्यापि तस्य स्वप्नस्य निवृत्तये जपपादप्रक्षालनाद्यनेकोपायाननुतिष्ठति ।
And he practices many remedies, such as chanting (*japa*), washing his feet, and so on, to ward off that dream, even though it is illusory.
तथा मिथ्याभूतोऽप्ययं संसारो जन्मादिदुःखहेतुत्वेन मे प्रतिभाति ।
Similarly, even though it is illusory, this saṃsāra appears to me as the cause of suffering such as birth, etc.
अतस्तन्निवर्तनमिच्छामि ।
Therefore, I desire its removal.
तस्मात्तन्निवृत्त्युपायं कृपया वद भोः इति शिष्यप्रश्नः ।
Hence, please tell me the means for its cessation, O revered Sir'—this is the disciple's question.
गुरुओरुत्तरम्॥ १६७–१६८ ॥
167 · आत्माज्ञानहेतुकसंसारनिवृत्तावात्मज्ञानमेवोपायः
हे शिष्य ।
O disciple!
जगद्रूपदुःखस्यात्यन्तनिवृत्तये पृष्ट उपायः प्रागेव निरूपितः ।
The means you asked for, for the absolute cessation of the suffering in the form of the world, has already been expounded earlier.
श्रद्धाभक्तिपुरःसरं तत्र दृढनिश्चयः क्रियताम् ।
Let firm conviction be established therein with faith and devotion.
ततो जगद्रूपदुःखमणुमात्रमपि त्वयि न दृश्येत ।
Then, not even the slightest atomic particle of suffering in the form of the world will be perceived in you.
हे सोम्य ।
O gentle one!
अद्वितीयासङ्गचिन्मात्ररूपस्वात्मस्वरूपस्यापरिज्ञानाज्जगद्रूपदुःखं तव प्रतिभाति ।
Suffering in the form of the world appears to you due to the lack of knowledge of your own true nature as non-dual, unattached, pure Consciousness (*cit*).
तच्च तवात्मस्वरूपपरिज्ञानमात्रान्निवर्तेत ।
And that will cease merely by thoroughly knowing your own true Self.
यद्वस्तु यस्याज्ञानाद्भवति तद्वस्तु तस्य ज्ञानमात्रान्निवर्तत इति नियमः ।
Whatever object arises from the ignorance of something, that object ceases merely through the knowledge of that thing—this is the invariable rule.
रज्ज्वज्ञानात्प्रतीयमानः सर्पः रज्जुरेवेयम् इति रज्जुज्ञानमात्राद्यथा निवर्तते, तथा आत्मज्ञानात्प्रतीयमानं जगदप्यात्मतत्त्वसाक्षात्कारमात्रेण निवर्तेत ।
Just as a snake appearing due to ignorance of the rope vanishes merely by knowing 'This is only a rope', likewise the world, appearing due to ignorance of the Self, will cease merely through direct realization of the true nature of the Self.
तच्चात्मतत्त्वज्ञानमुपदिष्टपूर्वमपि भूयोऽनुव्याख्यास्यामि - कालत्रयेऽपि मयि जगदणुमात्रमपि नास्ति; मिथ्यात्वात्, स्वप्नवत् ।
And although that knowledge of the truth of the Self has already been taught, I shall explain it once more: 'In all three periods of time, there is not even the slightest particle of the world in me, because it is illusory, like a dream.'
यन्मिथ्या तदधिष्ठानं न दूषयेत् ।
What is illusory cannot taint its substratum (*adhiṣṭhāna*).
न हि मरीच्युदकमूषरदेशमार्द्रीकरोति ।
For the water of a mirage never wets the desert land.
तथा मयि प्रतीयमानमपीदं जगत् मिथ्यात्वान्न मे कामपि हानिं कर्तुं प्रभवति ।
Likewise, even though this world appears in me, being illusory it is incapable of causing any harm whatsoever to me.
अहं सच्चिदानन्दानन्ताद्वितीयासङ्गब्रह्मस्वरूप एवास्मि, इत्येवं निश्चय एव ज्ञानं इत्युच्यते ।
'I am indeed the nature of Brahman which is Existence-Consciousness-Bliss, infinite, non-dual, and unattached'—such firm conviction alone is called knowledge (*jñāna*).
एतदेव ज्ञानमासुप्तेरामृतेश्च निरन्तरमभ्यस्यमानं मोक्षसाधनम्, नान्यत् किञ्चिदपि ।
This knowledge alone, continuously practiced from the waking moment till falling asleep and from birth till death, is the means to *mokṣa*, and nothing else whatsoever.
गुरुःतदिदं ज्ञानं पूर्वमेवोपदिष्टवानस्मीति गुरुराह ।
'This very knowledge I have already imparted to you'—said the Guru.
168 · ज्ञानमेवाज्ञाननाशकम्, न कर्मोपासनादि
हे सोम्य !
O gentle one!
अस्य जगत उपादानकारणमज्ञानम् ।
The material cause of this world is *avidyā*.
अस्याज्ञानस्य नाशमनु तत्कार्यं सर्वं दृश्यं जगत् स्वयमेव विनश्यति, उपादाननाशानन्तरं तत्कार्यस्य स्थित्ययोगात् ।
Following the destruction of this *avidyā*, its entire perceptible effect, the world, perishes by itself, since the existence of an effect is impossible after the destruction of its material cause.
तस्याज्ञानस्य नाशस्तु ज्ञानमात्रेण जायते, न तु कर्मोपासनादिभिः साधनान्तरैः; यतो ज्ञानमेव साक्षादज्ञानविरोधि न कर्मोपासनादिकम् ।
The destruction of that *avidyā*, however, occurs through knowledge alone, and not by other means such as action (*karma*) and meditation (*upāsanā*); because knowledge alone is directly opposed to *avidyā*, not action, meditation, and the like.
यथा गृहान्तर्विद्यमानं तमः केनापि व्यापारेणानिवर्त्यमपि केवलप्रकाशेन निवर्त्यते तथाज्ञानरूपं निबिडं तमो ज्ञानात्मकप्रचण्डप्रकाशेनैव निवर्त्येत, न तु केनचिदपि साधनान्तरेण ।
Just as the darkness inside a house, which cannot be dispelled by any physical exertion, is dispelled only by light, likewise the dense darkness in the form of *avidyā* can be dispelled only by the brilliant light of knowledge, and not by any other means whatsoever.
हे सोम्य !
O gentle one!
द्वैतरूपं जगत् यथा निःशेषं निवर्तेत तथाहं ते साधनमुपादिशम् ।
I have instructed you in the means by which the world of duality may completely cease.
तदेतन्मनसि धारयन् पुनःपुनर्युक्तिभिरनुचिन्तय ।
Holding this in your mind, reflect upon it again and again through reasonings.
गुरुःततोऽपि संशयो यदि स्याद्यथेच्छं पृच्छेति गुरुराह ।
If even after that a doubt should remain, ask freely as you please, said the Guru.
पूर्वोपदिष्टविषये आक्षेपसमाधानानि॥ १६९–२२५ ॥
जीवब्रह्मणोरभेदनिरूपणम्॥ १६९–१८८ ॥
जीवब्रह्माभेदविषये तत्त्वदृष्टिप्रश्नः॥ १६९–१७१ ॥
169
गुरूपदेशं सङ्ग्रहेणानूद्य शिष्यः स्वशङ्कां सूचयति-
Having summarized the Guru's teaching in brief, the disciple expresses his doubt:
हे स्वामिन् !
O Master!
जगत्कारणमज्ञानम्, तस्याज्ञानस्य तत्प्रयुक्तजगतश्च नाशो ज्ञानेनैव जायते इति भवदुपदिष्टं सम्यगवगच्छामि ।
*Avidyā* is the cause of the world, and the destruction of that *avidyā* as well as the world produced by it occurs only through knowledge — this teaching taught by your revered self I understand well.
परन्तु जगन्मिथ्या, जीव आनन्दस्वरूपः, अतश्च स जीवो ब्रह्मणो न भिन्नः इति भवतोपदिष्टेऽर्थे जगन्मिथ्यात्वम्, जीवस्यानन्दरूपत्वं चावगच्छामि ।
However, in the teaching imparted by you: the world is illusory, the *jīva* is of the nature of bliss (*ānanda*), and therefore that *jīva* is not distinct from Brahman, I comprehend the illusoriness of the world and the bliss-nature of the *jīva*.
जीवो ब्रह्माभिन्नः इत्यंशं तु नावधारयामि, तयोर्भेदशङ्कैव मे मनसि परिवर्तते, इति तत्त्वदृष्टिः पृच्छति ।
The part that 'the *jīva* is non-different from Brahman' I cannot comprehend; only the doubt of difference between them keeps revolving in my mind, thus asks Tattvadṛṣṭi.
170
जीवब्रह्मणोः स्वरूपभेदात्तयोरैक्यमसङ्गतमिति शङ्का-
The doubt that 'on account of essential difference between *jīva* and Brahman, their identity is inconsistent' [is elaborated]:
हे स्वामिन् !
O Master!
अहं हि पुण्यपापयोः कर्ता, तत्फलभूतजननमरणसुखदुःखादीन्यनुभवामि ।
I am indeed the agent of virtues and sins (*puṇya* and *pāpa*), and I experience their fruits consisting of birth, death, pleasure, pain, and so forth.
विचित्ररचनाविशिष्टं जगन्मयि प्रतिभाति ।
The world endowed with variegated creation appears to me.
जगत्कारणीभूतमूलाज्ञाननिवृत्तयेऽहं ब्रह्म विजिज्ञासे ।
I desire to know Brahman for the removal of the root-*avidyā* which has become the cause of the world.
ब्रह्मणस्तु पुण्यपापे न स्तः ।
For Brahman, on the other hand, merit and sin do not exist.
जन्ममरणसुखदुःखादिक्लेशलेशोऽपि ब्रह्मणो न सम्भवति ।
Not even a trace of suffering such as birth, death, pleasure, or pain is possible in Brahman.
अत एव तस्य न ज्ञानेच्छापि ।
For this very reason, it has no desire for knowledge either.
तस्मान्मम ब्रह्मणश्च मिथः स्वरूपतो भेद एव वर्तते ।
Therefore, between me and Brahman there exists only mutual difference in intrinsic nature.
ततो द्वयोरैक्यं नैव घटेत ।
Hence identity between the two cannot hold at all.
यद्यपि जन्मादिसंसारः परमार्थतो मय्यपि नास्त्येव, तथापि मिथ्याभूतो जन्ममरणात्मकः संसारो मयि स्वप्नवत् भ्रान्त्या प्रतिभाति ।
Even though this worldly existence beginning with birth does not exist in me in ultimate reality, nevertheless this illusory *saṃsāra* consisting of birth and death appears to me through delusion, like a dream.
ब्रह्मणि तु तन्नैव प्रतिभाति ।
In Brahman, however, that does not appear at all.
जीवब्रह्मणोरित्थं भेदसद्भावादैक्यं न सम्भवति ।
Thus, because difference exists between *jīva* and Brahman, their identity is impossible.
अयं च प्रमेयगतसंशयः ।
And this is a doubt pertaining to the subject matter (*prameya-gata-saṃśaya*).
171 · श्रुत्याकर्मोपासनविधिबलाच्च जीवब्रह्मभेदशङ्का
हे स्वामिन् ।
O Master!
मम संशयान्तरम् अपि जायते ।
Another doubt also arises in me.
श्रुत्या एव वक्ष्यमाण-प्रकारेण जीव-ब्रह्मणोः भेदः प्रतिपाद्यते - द्वा सुपर्णा सयुजा सखाया समानं वृक्षं परिषस्वजाते । तयोः अन्यः पिप्पलं स्वादु अत्ति अनश्नन् अन्यः अभिचाकशीति (मु. ३.१.१, श्वे. ४.६) इति हि श्रुतिः ।
By Śruti itself the difference between jīva and Brahman is established in the manner about to be described: Two birds of beautiful plumage, inseparable companions and friends, perch upon the same tree; of these two, one eats the sweet fruit, while the other looks on without eating (Muṇḍaka 3.1.1, Śvetāśvatara 4.6) — such indeed is the Śruti.
अयम् अर्थः - बुद्धि-रूपे एकस्मिन् वृक्षे द्वौ पक्षिणौ वसतः ।
This is the meaning: in one tree consisting of the intellect, two birds dwell.
तौ उभौ अपि समान-स्वभावौ ।
Both of them share a common nature.
तत्र एकः कर्म-फल-भोक्ता अपरः शुद्धः भोग-रहितः असङ्गः सन् कर्म-फल-भोक्तारम् प्रकाशयति ।
There, one is the enjoyer of the fruits of action; the other, being pure, free from enjoyment, and unattached, illuminates the enjoyer of the fruits of action.
अनयोः कर्म-फल-भोक्ता जीवः इति, अपरः परमात्मा इति च प्रतीयते ।
Of these two, the experiencer of the fruit of action is understood to be the jīva, and the other to be Paramātman.
इत्येवम् श्रुत्या एव जीव-ब्रह्मणोः भेद-प्रतिपादनात् न तयोः ऐक्यम् युक्तम् ।
Thus, because difference between jīva and Brahman is taught by Śruti itself, their identity is not tenable.
किञ्च, वेदे नाना-प्रकाराणि कर्माणि उपासनानि च तत्र तत्र कथितानि ।
Furthermore, various kinds of rituals and meditations are stated here and there in the Veda.
तानि निरर्थकानि स्युः जीव-ब्रह्मणोः एकत्व-अभ्युपगमे ।
They would become meaningless if identity between jīva and Brahman were accepted.
तथा हि - जीव-ब्रह्मणोः एकत्वम्, किं ब्रह्मणि जीव-स्वरूप-अन्तर्भावात्, किं वा जीवे ब्रह्म-स्वरूप-अन्तर्भावात् ।
To explain: is the identity of jīva and Brahman due to the inclusion of the nature of jīva in Brahman, or due to the inclusion of the nature of Brahman in the jīva?
न उभयथा अपि सम्भवति ।
Neither way is it possible.
ब्रह्मणि जीव-स्वरूप-अन्तर्भाव-अभ्युपगमे जीवस्य एव ब्रह्म-रूपत्वात् कर्म-उपासना-आदि-अधिकारि-अभाव-प्रसङ्गात् कर्म-उपासना-आदीनि निरर्थकानि स्युः ।
If inclusion of the jīva's nature in Brahman is accepted, since the jīva itself would be Brahman, there would be no qualified aspirant for rituals and meditations, and thus rituals and meditations would become futile.
जीवे च ब्रह्म-स्वरूप-अन्तर्भाव-अभ्युपगमे जीव-भाव-आपन्नत्वात् ब्रह्मणः उपास्य-अभाव-प्रसङ्गः इति उपासना-वाक्यानि निष्फलानि स्युः ।
And if inclusion of Brahman's nature in the jīva is accepted, because Brahman would have lapsed into the condition of a jīva, there would be no deity to be meditated upon, and thus the statements on meditation would become fruitless.
अपि च कर्म-फल-दातुः ईश्वरस्य अभावात् कर्म-अनुष्ठानम् अपि निष्फलं स्यात् ।
Moreover, in the absence of Īśvara who is the dispenser of the fruits of actions, the performance of rituals also would be fruitless.
कर्म-अतिरिक्तः ईश्वरः न अस्ति, स्वतन्त्रं कर्म एव फलं ददाति इति मीमांसक-उक्तिः अपि न युज्यते; जडत्वात् कर्मणः ।
Nor does the Mīmāṃsaka's assertion hold good: There is no Īśvara other than karma; autonomous karma alone bestows the fruit; because karma is insentient.
न हि जडस्य कर्मणः फल-दातृत्व-रूप-सामर्थ्यम् घटते ।
For insentient karma cannot possess the capacity of bestowing fruits.
अतः सर्वज्ञात् एव ईश्वरात् कर्म-फल-सिद्धिः वाच्या ।
Therefore, the attainment of the fruits of action must be said to come from the omniscient Īśvara alone.
तस्मात् जीव-आत्म-परम-आत्मनोः एकत्वम् न युज्यते इति ।
Therefore, identity between the jīvātman and the paramātman is not tenable.
अयम् च प्रमाण-गत-संशयः ।
And this is a doubt pertaining to the means of knowledge (pramāṇa).
समाधानम् -
The resolution:
स्वरूपभेदाज्जीवब्रह्मणोरैक्यासङ्गतिरिति शङ्कायाः॥ १७२–१८५ ॥
172 · आकशस्येव चैतन्यस्यापि चतुर्विधो भेदः
हे सौम्य ।
O gentle one!
त्वत्-सन्देह-निवर्तक-विचार-रूपम् उपदेशम् श‍ृणु - यथा एकस्य एव आकाशस्य (१) घट-आकाशः, (२) जल-आकाशः, (३) मेघ-आकाशः, (४) महा-आकाशः इति चतुर्विध-भेदः अस्ति तथा एकस्य एव चैतन्यस्य (१) कूटस्थः, (२) जीवः, (३) ईश्वरः, (४) ब्रह्म च इति भेद-चतुष्टयम् अस्ति ।
Listen to the instruction that consists of the inquiry that removes your doubts: just as for one single space there is a fourfold distinction, namely: (1) ghaṭākāśa (pot-space), (2) jalākāśa (water-reflected space), (3) meghākāśa (cloud-reflected space), and (4) mahākāśa (great space); so too for one single Consciousness there is a fourfold distinction: (1) kūṭastha, (2) jīva, (3) īśvara, and (4) brahman.
एषाम् स्वरूपम् विचार-पूर्वकम् यदा सम्यक् विजानासि तदा त्वदीय-सन्देहानाम् समाधानम् त्वम् स्वयम् एव जानीयाः ।
When you thoroughly understand their essential nature through critical inquiry, you will understand the resolution to your doubts entirely by yourself.
अतः तेषाम् स्वरूपम् मया अभिधीयमानम् अवधारय ।
Therefore, comprehend their true nature as it is expounded by me.
तद्-अधिगमेन तव निःसंशय-ज्ञान-उदय-द्वारा जन्म-आदि-दुःखम् निःशेषम् विनश्येत् ।
By the realization of that, through the arising of doubtless knowledge, your misery of birth and rebirth will be destroyed completely without residue.
चतुर्विधाकाशवर्णनम्॥ १७३–१७६ ॥
173 · घटाकाशः
जलपूरितघटावस्थानाय यावानाकाशोऽवकाशं ददाति तावानाकाशः घटाकाश इति पण्डितैरुच्यते ।
That amount of space which provides room for the accommodation of a water-filled pot is called 'ghaṭākāśa' (pot-space) by the learned.
टिप्पणी
1.
शिष्यःननु घटाद्बहिः स्थित आकाशो महाकाशः, तस्माद्भिन्नो घटान्तर्वर्त्याकाशो घटाकाश इति च प्रसिद्धिः ।
Objection: The space existing outside the pot is known as mahākāśa (great space), and distinct from it, the space enclosed inside the pot is commonly known as ghaṭākāśa (pot-space).
गुरुःतत्र घटाकाशस्य प्रसिद्धं लक्षणं विहाय लक्षणान्तरकरणे किं प्रयोजनमिति चेदत्रोच्यते ।
If it is asked: 'What is the purpose of abandoning the well-known definition of ghaṭākāśa and formulating a different definition?', here it is replied:
गुरुःघटान्तर्वर्त्याकाशो घटाकाशः इति प्रसिद्धलक्षणस्वीकारे घटो यत्र वर्तते स आकाशः पञ्चमः कपालाकाश इति वक्तव्यं भवेत् ।
If we accept the popular definition that 'ghaṭākāśa is the space enclosed inside the pot', then the space where the pot itself (its clay substance) is situated would have to be designated as a fifth type, 'kapālākāśa' (potsherd-space).
गुरुःस च पञ्चमप्रकार आकाशः शास्त्राप्रसिद्धः; [सिद्धान्ते आरम्भवादानङ्गीकारात्] ।
And such a fifth category of space is unrecognized in the śāstras, because in the Vedāntic siddhānta the Nyāya doctrine of new creation (ārambhavāda) is not accepted.
गुरुःतस्मादिदं द्वितीयं लक्षणमाश्रितं साधु ।
Therefore, adopting this second definition is proper.
174 · जलाकाशः
जलपूर्णे घटे नक्षत्रादिसहिताकाशः प्रतिबिम्बति ।
In a pot filled with water, space along with the stars and other celestial bodies is reflected.
तादृशाकाशप्रतिबिम्बो घटाकाशश्चेत्युभयं मिलित्वा जलाकाश इत्युच्यते ।
Both of these together—such a reflection of space and the pot-space itself—are called 'jalākāśa' (water-space).
नन्वाकाशस्य प्रतिबिम्बो न युज्यते, किन्तु केवलनक्षत्रादीनामेव स युज्यते ।
Objection: A reflection of space is untenable; rather, reflection is possible only for the stars and other objects in it.
रूपाभावान्नाकाशस्य प्रतिबिम्बः सम्भवति ।
Because of the absence of colour/form (rūpa), reflection of space cannot take place.
रूपवतो हि प्रतिबिम्बः स्यात् ।
Indeed, reflection can occur only for an object possessing form/colour.
तस्मान्नाकाशस्य प्रतिबिम्बो युज्यत इति चेन्न ।
If it is argued that therefore reflection of space is untenable, that is not correct.
जले आकाशप्रतिबिम्बानभ्युपगमे गोष्पदपरिमाणकस्वल्पजले महागजादिपरिमाणकगभीरतायाः प्रतिबिम्बो न स्यात् ।
If reflection of space in water were not accepted, then in a tiny pool of water measuring only a cow's footprint, the reflection of a great depth capable of submerging a huge elephant would not occur.
तथोपलभ्यमानत्वादाकाशप्रतिबिम्बोऽङ्गीकार्य एव ।
Since it is actually perceived in that manner, the reflection of space must certainly be accepted.
न च नीरूपपदार्थप्रतिबिम्बो नास्तीति वाच्यम् ।
Nor should it be contended that there is no reflection of a formless entity.
नीरूपस्यापि शब्दस्य प्रतिध्वनिदर्शनात् ।
For an echo (reflection) of even formless sound is observed.
स च प्रतिध्वनिः शब्दस्य प्रतिबिम्ब एव ।
And that echo is indeed the reflection of sound.
तस्मान्नीरूपस्याप्याकाशस्य प्रतिबिम्बो युज्यत एव ।
Therefore, the reflection of even formless space is certainly logically tenable.
175 · मेघाकाशः
मेघस्थितये यावानाकाशोऽवकाशं ददाति तावानाकाशः, मेघजले प्रतिबिम्बिताकाशश्चेत्युभयं मिलित्वा मेघाकाश इत्यभिधीयते ।
That amount of space which provides room for the stay of a cloud, and the space reflected in the cloud-water—both of these together are designated as 'meghākāśa' (cloud-space).
नन्वाकाशेऽस्ति मेघः ।
Objection: The cloud exists in space.
तत्र मेघे जलमाकाशप्रतिबिम्बश्चास्तीत्यत्र किं मानमिति चेन्न ।
If it is asked: 'What is the proof that there is water and a reflection of space in the cloud?', we say no (there is valid proof).
यद्यपि मेघे जलस्याकाशप्रतिबिम्बस्य च न प्रत्यक्षतो ग्रहणमथाप्यनुमानेन ग्रहणं सम्भवत्येव ।
Although water and the reflection of space in a cloud are not grasped by direct perception, their apprehension through inference is certainly possible.
तथा हि, मेघाज्जलवृष्टेर्दर्शनात्तत्र जलमस्तीत्यनुमीयते ।
To explain: from observing the shower of rain falling from a cloud, it is inferred that there is water in it.
यदि मेघे जलं न स्यात्तर्हि ततो जलवृष्टिर्न स्यात् ।
If there were no water in the cloud, then no rain would fall from it.
किञ्च, मेघस्थं जलमाकाशप्रतिबिम्बविशिष्टम्, स्वच्छद्रव्यत्वात्, दर्पणादिवत् इत्यनुमानेन मेघस्थजले आकाशप्रतिबिम्बानुमानं च सिद्ध्यति ।
Furthermore, by the inference: 'Water in the cloud is endowed with the reflection of space, because it is a transparent substance, just like a mirror, etc.', the inference of the reflection of space in cloud-water is established.
यद्यस्ति जलं तर्हि तज्जलमाकाशप्रतिबिम्बेन विना न स्यादिति हि नियमः ।
For the universal rule is that if water is present, that water cannot exist without a reflection of space.
एवं मेघे जलम्, तत्राकाशप्रतिबिम्बश्चानुमानेन प्रसिद्ध्यति ।
Thus, both water in the cloud and the reflection of space within it are established by inference.
176 · महाकाशः
ब्रह्माण्डस्यान्तर्बहिश्च व्याप्यैकरूपेण वर्तमान आकाशो महाकाश इत्युच्यते विद्वद्भिः ।
The space that exists pervading both inside and outside the universe in a single uniform manner is called 'mahākāśa' (great space) by the learned.
चैतन्यस्य चातुर्विध्यवर्णनम्॥ १७७–१८५ ॥
177 · उपोद्घातः
हे सोम्य ।
O gentle one!
चतुर्विधाकाशलक्षणमुक्तम् ।
The definition of the fourfold space has been stated.
टिप्पणी
1.
जलपूरितघटे दृश्यमानाकाशप्रतिबिम्बो घटान्तर्वर्त्याकाशप्रतिबिम्ब इति शङ्काव्यावृत्तये नक्षत्रादिसहितेत्याकाशविशेषणम् ।
In order to dispel the doubt whether the reflection of space seen in a water-filled pot is of the space inside the pot, the qualification of space as 'accompanied by stars, etc.' was given.
अपि च जलं विना प्रतिबिम्बासम्भवात् आकाशप्रतिबिम्बः इत्यनेन घटस्थजलसहिताकाशप्रतिबिम्बो ग्राह्यः ।
Moreover, since reflection is impossible without water, by 'reflection of space' is to be understood the reflection of space along with the water present in the pot.
2.
गुणो गुणमाश्रित्य न तिष्ठति, किन्तु द्रव्यमेवेति नियमः ।
A quality does not reside in another quality, but only in a substance—such is the general rule.
अतश्च गुणत्वेनाभिमतानि नीलपीतादिवर्णानि नीरूपाण्येव ।
And therefore, colours like blue, yellow, etc., which are regarded as qualities, are themselves devoid of form/colour.
तथापि तेषां स्वच्छदर्पणादौ प्रतिबिम्बो दृष्टः ।
Even so, their reflection is observed in a clear mirror and the like.
एवमेव रूपरहितयोराकाशचैतन्ययोश्च प्रतिबिम्बः सम्भवेदेव ।
Just so, reflection is certainly possible for both space and consciousness, even though they are formless.
चतुर्विधचैतन्यलक्षणमप्युच्यमानं श‍ृणु ।
Now listen also to the definition of the fourfold consciousness that is being stated.
तस्य श्रवणमात्रेण विचारस्य महाफलं ब्रह्मज्ञानमवाप्येत ।
By mere hearing of it, the great fruit of inquiry—the knowledge of Brahman—can be attained.
178 · कूटस्थवर्णनं
बुद्धेर्व्यष्ट्यज्ञानस्य वा अधिष्ठानभूतचैतन्यस्य कूटस्थः इत्यभिधा ।
The consciousness that is the substrate of the intellect or of individual avidyā is designated as Kūṭastha.
यन्मते बुद्धिविशिष्टश्चेतनो जीवस्तन्मते बुद्ध्यधिष्ठानचेतनः कूटस्थ इत्युच्यते ।
In the view where consciousness qualified by the intellect is the *jīva*, in that view consciousness that is the substrate of the intellect is called Kūṭastha.
यत्र तु मते व्यष्ट्यज्ञानविशिष्टचेतनो जीव इति कीर्त्यते तन्मते व्यष्ट्यज्ञानाधिष्ठानचेतनः कूटस्थ इति वर्ण्यते ।
In the view, however, where consciousness qualified by individual *avidyā* is declared to be the *jīva*, in that view the consciousness that is the substrate of individual *avidyā* is described as Kūṭastha.
अत्रायं सिद्धान्तः - जीवत्वापादकं विशेषणं यत् तदधिष्ठानस्य कूटस्थ इति नाम ।
Here this is the settled conclusion: whatever attribute brings about *jīva*-hood, the substrate of that attribute bears the name Kūṭastha.
अयं कूटस्थ उत्पत्त्यादिरहितः ।
This Kūṭastha is free from origination and other modifications.
अस्यायमभिप्रायः - ब्रह्मणो व्यतिरिक्ततया चिदाभासो यथोत्पद्यते, न तथा कूटस्थ उत्पद्यते; किन्तु ब्रह्मरूप एव स भवति ।
The purport of this is: unlike *cidābhāsa*, which is produced as distinct from Brahman, Kūṭastha is not produced; rather, it is identical in nature with Brahman itself.
यथा घटाकाशो महाकाशान्न व्यतिरिक्तः, किन्तु माहाकाशरूप एव भवति, तद्वत् ।
Just as the space in the pot is not different from the all-pervading space, but is of the nature of the great space itself, so is this.
अयं च कूटस्थ आत्मपदलक्ष्यार्थः ।
And this Kūṭastha is the implied meaning (*lakṣyārtha*) of the term *ātman*.
कूटस्थस्यैव प्रत्यगिति, निजस्वरूपमिति, जीवसाक्षीति च व्यपदेशः ।
Of Kūṭastha alone are the designations 'Pratyak' (inner Self), 'Nijasvarūpa' (one's true nature), and 'Jīvasākṣin' (witness of the jīva).
कूटस्थो घटाकाशस्थानीयः ।
Kūṭastha corresponds to the position of the space enclosed within the pot (*ghaṭākāśa*).
जीवस्वरूपवर्णनम्॥ १७९–१८३ ॥
बुद्धिप्रतिबिम्बितचैतन्यं जीवः॥ १७९–१८२ ॥
179 · जीवस्वरूपं
अनन्तकोटिकामकर्मवासनावासितबुद्धौ प्रतिफलितचैतन्यप्रतिबिम्बो जीव इति विद्वद्भिरुच्यते ।
The reflection of Consciousness mirrored in the intellect, which is perfumed by countless crores of desires, actions, and latent impressions, is called the jīva by the wise.
न हि तत् प्रतिबिम्बमात्रं जीव इत्युच्यते; किन्तु यथा घटाकाशसहिताकाशप्रतिबिम्बो जलाकाश इति कथ्यते, एवं कूटस्थसहितचिदाभासो जीव इति कीर्त्यते ।
For that mere reflection alone is not called the jīva; rather, just as the reflection of the sky together with the pot-space is spoken of as the 'water-space' (jalākāśa), so too the reflection of Consciousness (cidābhāsa) combined with the immutable Consciousness (kūṭastha) is designated as the jīva.
तस्माद्बुद्धिस्थचिदाभासो बुद्ध्यधिष्ठानचैतन्यं चेत्युभयं मिलित्वा जीव इति सिद्ध्यति ।1,2,3
Therefore, both the cidābhāsa located in the intellect and the Consciousness serving as the substratum of the intellect, taken together, are established as the jīva.
टिप्पणी
1.
केषुचिदद्वैतग्रन्थेषु जीव ईशो ब्रह्मेति चित्त्रैविध्यप्रक्रियाश्रिता ।
In some Advaita treatises, a framework of threefold Consciousness—as jīva, īśa, and Brahman—is adopted.
अनादिपदार्थषट्कनिरूपणे चैतन्यत्रैविध्यमेवोक्तम् ।
In the delineation of the six beginningless entities, only the threefold division of Consciousness is mentioned.
तत्र कूटस्थपरित्यागान्न कोऽपि दोषः स्यात् ।
There is no flaw in that omission of kūṭastha as a separate category.
कूटस्थब्रह्मणोर्न नाममात्रभेदादृतेऽन्यः कश्चन भेदोऽस्ति ।
Because there is no difference whatsoever between kūṭastha and Brahman other than a mere difference in name.
किञ्च विद्यारण्यमुनिकृतदृग्दृश्यविवेकाख्यग्रन्थे कूटस्थः पारमार्थिकजीवः, जाग्रत्कालिकान्तःकरणप्रतिबिम्बो व्यावहारिकजीवः, स्वप्नदृक् प्रातिभासिकजीव इति च निरूपितम् ।
Moreover, in the work titled Dṛgdṛśyaviveka composed by Sage Vidyāraṇya, it is expounded that kūṭastha is the absolute jīva (pāramārthika-jīva), the reflection in the internal organ during the waking state is the empirical jīva (vyāvahārika-jīva), and the dream-seer is the illusory jīva (prātibhāsika-jīva).
अनेन कूटस्थो जीवकोटावन्तर्भावितः ।
By this, kūṭastha is included in the category of the jīva.
2.
जीवो बुद्धिप्रतिबिम्ब इति, अविद्याप्रतिबिम्ब इति च वक्ष्यमाणत्वादत्र पक्षद्वयं सूचितम् ।
Because it will be stated later that the jīva is a reflection in the intellect and also a reflection in avidyā, two positions are indicated here.
3.
अत्र चिदाभासशब्देन बुद्ध्या (अन्तःकरणेन) सहितश्चिदाभासो ग्राह्यः ।
Here, by the word cidābhāsa, the reflection of Consciousness together with the intellect (the internal organ) is to be understood.
तथा चान्तःकरणमथवाविद्या, तत्स्थचिदाभासः, तदुभयाधिष्ठानकूटस्थचैतन्यं चेत्येतत्त्रयं मिलित्वा जीव इत्युच्यते ।
And thus, the internal organ (or avidyā), the cidābhāsa seated within it, and the kūṭastha-Consciousness acting as the substratum of both—this triad together is called the jīva.
(१) केवलान्तःकरणस्य जीवत्वोक्तौ घटादेर्जडस्यापि तदा-॥
(1) If the bare internal organ alone were asserted to be the jīva, then even insentient things like a pot would...
180 · आभासस्वरूपविवेचनं
प्राग् बिम्बरूपकूटस्थसहितचिदाभासो जीव इति प्रपञ्चितम् ।
Earlier, it was explained in detail that the jīva is the reflection of Consciousness (cidābhāsa) together with the immutable reality (kūṭastha) in the form of the original prototype (bimba).
अत इदं प्रतीयते - बुद्धौ प्रतिफलितो यः प्रतिबिम्बः स कूटस्थस्यैव, न तु बाह्यब्रह्मचैतनस्यस्य ।
From this, it is understood: the reflection that is cast in the intellect is of the kūṭastha alone, and not of the external Brahman-Consciousness.
यस्य प्रतिबिम्बोऽन्यत्र प्रतीयते, स एव बिम्ब इत्युच्यते ।
That whose reflection is perceived elsewhere is alone called the original prototype (bimba).
प्रकृते कूटस्थस्य बिम्बत्वाङ्गीकारात् जीवस्तत्प्रतिबिम्ब इत्येव प्रतीयते ।
In the present context, because the kūṭastha is accepted as the original prototype, the jīva is understood solely as its reflection.
तथा हि, अत्यन्तरक्तजपाकुसुमाद्युपाध्युपरिस्थस्वच्छस्फटिके तत्पुष्पादिरक्तिमा प्रतीयते ।
For instance, in a clear crystal placed upon an upādhi such as an intensely red hibiscus flower, the redness of that flower is perceived.
स च स्फटिकादिगतरक्तिमा तत्पुष्पादिप्रतिबिम्ब एव ।
And that redness appearing in the crystal is merely the reflection of that flower.
तथा कूटस्थाश्रितबुद्धौ कूटस्थस्य प्रकाशः प्रतिफलति ।
Similarly, the light of the kūṭastha is reflected in the intellect supported by the kūṭastha.
स प्रकाश एव चिदाभास इत्युच्यते ।
That reflected light alone is called cidābhāsa (the reflection of Consciousness).
अत्यन्तस्वच्छस्फटिकवत् बुद्धिरप्यत्यन्तनिर्मला; सत्त्वगुणकार्यत्वात्तस्याः ।
Like an extremely clear crystal, the intellect is also extremely pure, because it is an effect of the sattva guṇa.
तत्र प्रतिफलितकूटस्थप्रकाशस्यैव प्रतिबिम्ब इति समाख्या ।
The light of the kūṭastha reflected therein is designated as 'reflection' (pratibimba).

Since the intellect is presided over by the kūṭastha, it is appropriate that only the reflection of the kūṭastha occurs in the intellect; thus the view that 'the jīva is the reflection of the kūṭastha' was presented.
पत्तिः ।
...[would lead to the absurd] consequence.
अस्वच्छत्वाद्घटादेस्तन्न सम्भवतीति चेत् - स्वच्छदर्पणादेस्तदापत्तिः ।
If it is objected: 'Due to being non-transparent, that is not possible for a pot and the like,' then it would absurdly apply to a clean mirror, etc.

If you say: 'Because a mirror etc. are external, it does not apply to them,' then that consequence would apply to the internal sense organs.

(3) The statement that the substratum-Consciousness alone is the jīva is inconsistent; because it is changeless, the status of jīva, which involves modifications (such as agency and enjoyership), is untenable for it.

Moreover, since partial-abandonment implication (bhāgatyāga-lakṣaṇā) would then be impossible, only total-abandonment implication (jahal-lakṣaṇā), which discards the entire literal sense, would result; and this is not acceptable to the Commentator (Śaṅkarācārya).

Furthermore, that which, while non-distinct from the substratum, veils the substratum, is alone called the superimposed entity (āropya).
न ह्यधिष्ठानमन्तरा पृथगारोप्यं कुत्राप्यवभासते ।
For nowhere does a superimposed object ever appear separately without a substratum.
अनेनानुमानेन बुद्धिसहितचिदाभासो जीवः इत्येतदपास्तम् ।

(5) If it is argued: 'The combination of both the substratum-Consciousness and the reflected Consciousness is the jīva,' it is not so; because pure Consciousness is changeless, it is impossible for it to possess the nature of a jīva endowed with modifications such as agency and enjoyership.
(६) अधिष्ठानचैतन्यमन्तःकरणं चेत्युभयं मिलित्वा जीव इति चेत् - दर्पणं दर्पणाधिष्ठानचैतन्यं च मिलित्वा तर्हि जीवः स्यात् ।
(6) If you say: 'The substratum-Consciousness and the inner organ combining together form the jīva,' then a mirror combined with the Consciousness underlying the mirror would also become a jīva.
तयोर्जीवत्वं न सम्भवति ।
The nature of a jīva is impossible for those two.
तस्मादन्तःकरणम्, तत्प्रतिफलितचैतन्याभासः, तदुभयाधिष्ठानचैतन्यं चेत्येतत्त्रयमपि मिलित्वैव जीव इत्युच्यते ।
Therefore, the inner organ, the reflection of Consciousness reflected therein, and the Consciousness that is the substratum of both — this triad taken together is alone called the jīva.

Among these, since transmigration (saṁsāra) is impossible for the changeless kūṭastha, it must be admitted that the jīva alone is the transmigrating entity (saṁsārin).
तथा पञ्चदश्यामुक्तम् - चैतन्यं यदधिष्ठानं लिङ्गदेहश्च यः पुनः । चिच्छाया लिङ्गदेहस्था तत्सङ्घो जीव उच्यते ॥ (द्वै. ११) इति ।1
Likewise, it has been stated in the Pañcadaśī: The Consciousness which is the substratum, and the subtle body, and the shadow (reflection) of Consciousness situated in the subtle body — the aggregate of these is called the jīva (Dvaitaviveka 11).
टिप्पणी
1.
पटविलक्षणत्वे सति पटवद्भासमानत्वं पटाभासत्वं यथा, तथा चिद्विलक्षणत्वे सति चिद्वद्भासमानत्वं चिदाभासत्वम् ।
Just as being an appearance of cloth (paṭābhāsatva) is appearing like cloth while being distinct from cloth, so also being a semblance of consciousness (cidābhāsatva) is appearing like consciousness while being distinct from consciousness.
अथवा ब्रह्मचैतन्यस्य बुद्धौ प्रतिबिम्ब इति पक्षोऽपि सम्भाव्यत एव ।
Alternatively, the view that it is the reflection of Brahman-consciousness in the intellect is also certainly tenable.

To explain: in the water within a pot, there is only the reflection of the external great ether (*mahākāśa*), but not the reflection of the space within the pot.
घटस्थजले यावान् विस्तार उपलभ्यते तावान् विस्तारो घटान्तःस्थाकाशस्य नास्ति ।
The space inside the pot does not possess as much expanse as is perceived in the water situated in the pot.
घटस्थजले उपलभ्यमानविस्तारः आकाशस्य प्रतिबिम्ब एव ।
The expanse perceived in the water of the pot is indeed the reflection of space.
तस्माद्बाह्यमहाकाशस्यैव घटस्थजले प्रतिबिम्बो वाच्यः ।
Therefore, one must state that the reflection in the pot-water is indeed of the external great space.
एवं बुद्धौ व्यापकब्रह्मचैतन्यस्यापि प्रतिबिम्बो भवितुमर्हति ।
In the same way, the reflection of the all-pervasive Brahman-consciousness can also occur in the intellect.
व्यापकस्य ब्रह्मचैतन्यस्य प्रतिबिम्बो न युज्यत इतीयमाशङ्का आकाशदृष्टान्तेनैव निराकार्या ।
This doubt—that 'a reflection of the all-pervasive Brahman-consciousness is not tenable'—is to be refuted by the very analogy of space.

Just as the reflection of space is possible even though it is all-pervasive, so can the reflection of all-pervasive consciousness be possible.
रूपवत एव पदार्थस्य रूपविशिष्टे एव पदार्थान्तरे प्रतिबिम्बोदय इति नियमोऽपि नास्ति ।
There is also no rule that the emergence of a reflection occurs only of an object endowed with form in another object that is endowed with form.

Because it has been stated earlier that the reflection (echo) of sound, which is formless, is indeed seen in space, which is also formless.
तस्मात्सम्भवत्येव व्यापकनीरूपब्रह्मचैतन्यस्यापि प्रतिबिम्बः ।
Therefore, the reflection of the all-pervasive, formless Brahman-consciousness is certainly possible.
इत्थं बुद्धिस्थचिदाभासो बुद्ध्यधिष्ठानचैतन्यं चेत्युभयं मिलित्वा जीव इत्युच्यते ।
In this manner, the *cidābhāsa* residing in the intellect and the substrate consciousness of the intellect, taken together, are called the *jīva*.

This very *jīva* is the literal meaning (*vācyārtha*) of the word 'tvam' ('you').
जीवस्थचिदाभासं विहाय परिशिष्टः केवलकूटस्थ एव त्वम्पदलक्ष्यार्थः ।
Setting aside the *cidābhāsa* present in the *jīva*, the remaining pure *kūṭastha* alone is the implied meaning (*lakṣyārtha*) of the term 'tvam'.
अहंशब्दस्य वाच्यार्थो जीवः, लक्ष्यार्थस्तु केवलकूटस्थ इति विवेकः ।
The literal meaning of the word 'aham' ('I') is the *jīva*, whereas the implied meaning is pure *kūṭastha*—such is the distinction.

चिदाभास एव पुण्यपापाद्याश्रयः, न कूटस्थः ।
The reflection of Consciousness (cidābhāsa) alone is the locus of virtue, sin, and the like, not the kūṭastha.

Even though both kūṭastha and cidābhāsa joined together are empirically treated as the jīva, all the attributes of the jīva such as agency (kartṛtva) depend only upon the cidābhāsa.

Merit, sin, the experience of pleasure and pain that are their fruits, going to another world, returning here, and so on—all this is done solely by the intellect qualified by cidābhāsa, not by the kūṭastha.
कूटो नामायोघनविशेषः अयस्कारादिप्रसिद्धः ।
Kūṭa means a specific solid iron block (anvil), well known among blacksmiths.
तद्वन्निर्विकारतया तिष्ठतीति कूटस्थ उच्यते ।
Because it remains unchanging just like an anvil, it is called kūṭastha.

Alternatively, 'kūṭa' (deception/illusion) is the name of the illusory intellect and cidābhāsa.
तत्रासङ्गतयास्ते इति कूटस्थ इष्यते ।
Because it resides unattached within that (illusory complex), it is held to be kūṭastha.
अतः कूटस्थे कर्तृत्वादयो न सम्भवन्ति, किन्तु चिदाभासस्य ।
Therefore, agency and similar traits are not possible in the kūṭastha, but belong rather to the cidābhāsa.
भ्रान्त्या ते धर्माः कूटस्थे प्रतीयन्ते ।
It is only through delusion that those properties appear in the kūṭastha.
182 · वस्तुतः पुण्यपापादयो न चिदाभासस्यापि धर्माः, किन्तु बुद्धेरेव
विचार्यमाणे तु पुण्यपापतत्फलसुखदुःखलोकान्तरगमनागमनादि ।1
When properly investigated, however, merit and demerit, their fruits in the form of pleasure and pain, transmigration to other worlds, and so on [are attributes of the intellect alone].
टिप्पणी
1.
पूर्वं प्रतिबिम्बः कूटस्थस्यैवेति साधितम् ।
Earlier, it was established that the reflection belongs to the kūṭastha alone.
अधुना स ब्रह्मचैतन्यस्यापीत्युच्यते ।
Now, it is stated that it is also of Brahman-consciousness.
सर्वं बुद्धेरेव, न तु चिदाभासस्य अपि ।
Everything belongs to the intellect alone, not even to the cidābhāsa.
बुद्धितादात्म्यादाभासे तत्सर्वं भाति ।
Due to identification with the intellect, all of that appears in the reflection (cidābhāsa).
यथा जलपूर्णे घटे ऋजुवक्रादिस्वरूपे सति, तस्मिन् घटेऽन्येन नीयमाने वा आनीयमाने वा सति, तादृशघटसम्बन्धादेव तत्स्थाकाशाभासस्ताः क्रियाः करोति, न तु स्वतः किञ्चिदपि करोति; तथा कामकर्मात्मकजलपूरितबुद्धिरूपघटः पुण्यपापादिसकलविक्रियाश्रयो भवति ।
Just as when a water-filled pot has straight, curved, or other shapes, or when that pot is carried away or brought back by someone, the reflection of space located therein appears to perform those movements solely due to its connection with such a pot, and does not do anything by itself; similarly, the pot-like intellect, filled with the water of desire and action, is the locus of all modifications such as merit and demerit.
तत्सम्बन्धाच्चिदाभासोऽपि विक्रियाश्रयो भवति ।
And by connection with it, the cidābhāsa also appears as the locus of modifications.
कूटस्थस्तु सर्वविकारशून्यः ।
The kūṭastha, however, is free from all modifications.
यथा घटाकाशो जलपूर्णघटगतसर्वविकाररहितस्तथा कूटस्थोऽप्यसङ्ग इति विद्धि ।
Just as the pot-space is devoid of all modifications occurring in the water-filled pot, know that the kūṭastha is likewise unattached.
अतो जीवत्वप्रयुक्तनिखिलधर्माश्चिदाभासे भवन्ति ।
Therefore, all the characteristics occasioned by jīva-hood reside in the cidābhāsa.
कूटस्थे त्वज्ञानात्प्रतीयन्ते ।
In the kūṭastha, however, they are only perceived due to ignorance.
अतः कूटस्थबुद्धितत्स्थचिदाभाससमुदायो जीव इत्युच्यते ।
Therefore, the composite aggregate of the kūṭastha, the intellect, and the cidābhāsa located therein is designated as the jīva.
183 · अज्ञानप्रतिबिम्बितचैतन्यं जीवः
प्रागुक्तजीवस्वरूपेऽङ्गीक्रियमाणे प्राज्ञस्य हानिरुपजायते ।
If the previously stated definition of the *jīva* is accepted, the invalidation of the *prājña* (the self in deep sleep) will result.
तथा हि - सुषुप्त्यभिमानिनो जीवस्य 1प्राज्ञ इति नाम ।
To explain: the *jīva* that identifies with the deep-sleep state is named *prājña*.
सुषुप्तौ बुद्धेरभावात्तत्स्थचिदाभासोऽपि न सिद्ध्यति ।
Because the intellect (*buddhi*) is absent in deep sleep, the reflection of consciousness (*cidābhāsa*) located in it is also not established.
ततश्च प्राज्ञस्वरूपप्रतिपादकशास्त्रं निर्विषयं भवेत् ।
And consequently, the scriptures expounding the nature of *prājña* would become devoid of a subject-matter.
अतः प्रकारान्तरेण जीव2,3
Therefore, in another manner, the *jīva* [is defined]...
टिप्पणी
1.
जलगतशैत्यं तत्र प्रतिबिम्बितादित्यादीन् यथा न स्पृशति तथान्तःकरणगता विकारा अपि तत्र प्रतिबिम्बितचिदाभासं न कदाचिदपि स्पृशन्ति; किमु वक्तव्यं तदन्तःकरणाधिष्ठानभूतं प्रत्यगात्मानं न स्पृशन्तीत्यत्र ।
Just as the coolness residing in water does not touch the sun and other things reflected in it, so too the modifications belonging to the internal organ never touch even the *cidābhāsa* reflected therein; what then needs to be said about their not touching the inner *ātman* who is the very substratum of that internal organ!
यथा पृथिव्यादिगताः तत्कार्यगताश्च विक्रियाः पृथिव्याद्याधारभूतमाकाशं न स्पृशन्ति; तद्वदेवानात्मभूताज्ञानं तत्कार्याहङ्कारदेहेन्द्रियादिप्रपञ्चधर्माश्च अज्ञानतत्कार्यनिखिलदृश्याधिष्ठानभूतचिद्रूपप्रत्यगात्मानं न स्पृशन्त्येव ।
Just as the modifications residing in earth and other elements and in their effects do not touch space which is their underlying support, so too non-Self *avidyā* and the attributes of the world consisting of its effects such as ego, body, senses, etc., do not at all touch the inner *ātman*, whose nature is pure *cit* and who is the substratum of the entire realm of objects comprising *avidyā* and its effects.
अज्ञानात्तु ते धर्माः कूटस्थं स्पृशन्तीव भ्रान्तिर्भवति ।
However, due to *avidyā*, there arises the delusion as though those attributes touch the immutable (*kūṭastha*).
2.
वस्तुतस्तु सुखदुःखादिसंसारो न बुद्धेरपि सम्भवति ।
In reality, *saṃsāra* consisting of pleasure, pain, etc., is not possible even for the intellect.
तथा चोक्तं गुहाधिकरणभाष्ये (ब्र. सू. १.२.१२) इदं हि कर्तृत्वं भोक्तृत्वं च सत्त्वक्षेत्रज्ञयोरितरेतरस्वभावाविवेककृतं कल्प्यते । परमार्थतस्तु नान्यतरस्यापि सम्भवति; अचेतनत्वात् सत्त्वस्य, अविक्रियत्वाच्च क्षेत्रज्ञस्य । अविद्याप्रत्युपस्थापितस्वभावत्वाच्च सत्त्वस्य सुतरां न सम्भवति । तथा च श्रुतिः - यत्र वान्यदिव स्यात्तत्रान्योऽन्यत् पश्येत् (बृ. ४.३.३१) इत्यादिना स्वप्नदृष्टहस्त्यादिव्यवहारवदविद्याविषय एव कर्तृत्वादिव्यवहारं दर्शयति । यत्र त्वस्य सर्वमात्मैवाभूत् तत् केन कं पश्येत् (बृ. ४.५.१५) इत्यादिना च विवेकिनः कर्तृत्वादिव्यवहाराभावं दर्शयति इति ।
And so it is stated in the Guhādhikaraṇa-bhāṣya (Br. Sū. 1.2.12): 'This agency and experiencership is imagined as caused by non-discrimination of the mutual natures of the intellect (*sattva*) and the individual soul (*kṣetrajña*). In ultimate reality, however, it is impossible for either of them: because the intellect is insentient, and because the *kṣetrajña* is changeless. Moreover, because the very nature of the intellect is fabricated by *avidyā*, [agency/experiencership] is all the more impossible. So also the *śruti*, with where there is duality, as it were, there one sees another (Bṛ. Up. 4.3.31), etc., shows that empirical behaviour like agency belongs strictly to the sphere of *avidyā*, just like transactions involving elephants etc. seen in a dream; and with where, however, everything has become the Ātman alone to him, then whereby and whom should one see? (Bṛ. Up. 4.5.15), etc., it shows the total absence of empirical behaviour such as agency for the discriminating sage.'
3.
यथा चन्द्रस्य स्वतो निर्विकारतया सदैकरूपत्वेऽपि तिथिपक्षाभ्यां चन्द्रस्य कलायामेव वृद्धिक्षयादिकं भवति; यथा वा सदा वृक्षस्यैकरूपत्वेऽपि तत्फलादीनामेव जन्मादिविकारो जायते; तथा स्वयं निर्विकारेऽपि कूटस्थचिन्मात्रे प्रत्यगात्मनि देहादीनामेव जन्मादिषड्विकाररूपपरिणामो जायते ।
Just as waxing and waning occur only in the digit of the moon by the tithis and fortnights though the moon itself is naturally changeless and ever uniform; or just as modifications such as birth take place only in the fruits of a tree though the tree itself is ever uniform; so too, transformation in the form of the sixfold changes like birth occurs only in the body and so on, while the inner ātman, the unchangeable pure Consciousness, is itself changeless.
यदि कूटस्थ एव परिणमेत्, तर्हि स जडः स्यात् ।
If the immutable Self itself were to undergo transformation, then it would be insentient.
परिणामः = विकारः = प्रकृतेरन्यथाभावः ।
Transformation = modification = alteration of the original substance.
तस्मात्कूटस्थस्य विकारो न कथञ्चनोपपद्यते ।
Therefore, modification of the immutable Self is not possible in any way.
स्वरूपनिरूपणं क्रियते ।
Now the determination of essential nature is undertaken.
अज्ञानस्यैकदेशो व्यष्ट्यज्ञानं इति, सम्पूर्णाज्ञानं तु समष्ट्यज्ञानं इति चोच्यते ।
A fraction of avidyā is called individual avidyā (vyaṣṭy-ajñāna), whereas the total avidyā is called collective avidyā (samaṣṭy-ajñāna).
तत्राज्ञानैकदेशप्रतिबिम्बितचिदाभासः, तदज्ञानांशाधिष्ठानभूतकूटस्थचैतन्यं च मिलित्वा जीव इत्युच्यते ।
There, the cidābhāsa reflected in a fraction of avidyā, together with the immutable Consciousness (kūṭastha-caitanya) that is the substratum of that fraction of avidyā, is termed the jīva.
न चैतस्मिन् जीवस्वरूपे प्राज्ञस्याभावः सम्भवति, सुषुप्तावज्ञानस्य सत्त्वात् ।
Nor does Prājña become absent under this definition of the jīva's nature, because avidyā is present in deep sleep.
सुषुप्तौ यः चैतन्यप्रतिबिम्बविशिष्टाज्ञानांशः स बुद्ध्यात्मना परिणमते ।
That fraction of avidyā qualified by the reflection of Consciousness, which exists in deep sleep, transforms into the intellect (buddhi).
तत्र चैतन्यप्रतिबिम्बोऽपि सहैव वर्तते ।
There, the reflection of Consciousness also remains along with it.
अस्यां चिदाभासयुक्तायां बुद्धौ पुण्यापुण्यादिरूपः संसारः प्रतीयते ।
In this intellect endowed with cidābhāsa, transmigratory existence (saṃsāra) in the form of merit, demerit, etc., is experienced.
अनेनाभिप्रायेण बुद्धिरेव शास्त्रेष्वपि क्वचिज्जीवोपाधितया वर्ण्यते ।
With this intention, even in the scriptures, the intellect itself is occasionally described as the limiting adjunct (upādhi) of the jīva.
विचारदृष्ट्या तु जीवस्योपाधिरज्ञानमेव ।
From the viewpoint of inquiry, however, the upādhi of the jīva is avidyā alone.
184 · ईश्वरस्वरूपवर्णनं
मायायां प्रतिबिम्बितचिदाभासः ।1,2
The reflection of Consciousness (cidābhāsa) reflected in māyā [is Īśvara].
टिप्पणी
1.
ईश्वरस्वरूपं तु बहुधा अनेकैः वर्ण्यते ।
The nature of Īśvara, however, is described in various ways by many thinkers.
तथा हि योग-मतानुसारिणः तु एवम् आहुः - चैतन्य-समीपस्थ-प्रकृति-प्रेरकः जीव-विलक्षणः पुरुषः ईश्वरः ।
For instance, the followers of the Yoga school state thus: 'Īśvara is a distinct puruṣa, different from the jīva, who impels prakṛti proximate to consciousness.'
सः च ईश्वरः क्लेश-कर्म-तत्-फल-आदिभिः असंस्पृष्टः जीववत् असङ्गः चिन्मात्रः ।
And that Īśvara is untouched by afflictions, karmas, and their fruits, unattached like the jīva, and is pure consciousness.
जीवस्य अपि क्लेश-आदि-अभावेषु अविवेक-वशात् तत्-सत्त्वं प्रतीयते ।
Even in the case of the jīva, though afflictions etc. are absent in reality, their presence is perceived due to non-discrimination.
अयम् एव जीव-ईश्वरयोः भेद-हेतुः ।
This alone is the ground of distinction between jīva and Īśvara.
न्याय-मतानुसारिणः तु असङ्गस्य ईश्वरस्य नियामकत्व-असम्भवात् योग-मतम् आक्षिप्य ईश्वरस्य ज्ञान-इच्छा-प्रयत्न-आदि-गुणाः नित्याः अतः जीवात् विलक्षणः भिन्नः च ईश्वरः इति आहुः ।
The followers of Nyāya, however, objecting to the Yoga view on the ground that an unattached Īśvara cannot be a controller, say: 'The qualities of Īśvara such as knowledge, desire, and effort are eternal; therefore Īśvara is distinct and fundamentally different from the jīva.'
हिरण्यगर्भ-उपासकाः तु ईश्वर-ज्ञानादीनां नित्यत्वे सोऽकामयत (तै. ब्र. ६) इति-आदि-श्रुति-वाक्यानां सृष्टि-आरम्भ-समये ईश्वर-ज्ञानादीनाम् उत्पत्ति-प्रतिपादकानां विरोधः स्यात् सदा सृष्टि-प्रसङ्गः च स्यात् ।
The worshippers of Hiraṇyagarbha, however, argue: 'If Īśvara's knowledge etc. were eternal, there would be contradiction with Vedic statements such as He desired (Tai. Br. 6) which declare the origination of Īśvara's knowledge etc. at the time of creation's start; and there would also be the absurd contingency of perpetual creation.'
अतः असङ्गतं न्याय-मतम् ।
'Therefore, the Nyāya view is untenable.'
हिरण्यगर्भः एव ईश्वरः ।
'Hiraṇyagarbha alone is Īśvara.'
अस्य लिङ्ग-शरीर-सत्त्वे अपि अविद्या-काम-कर्म-आदि-अभावात् जीव-विलक्षणः सः इति आचक्षते ।
They declare that though he possesses a subtle body, he is distinct from the jīva due to the absence of avidyā, desire, karma, etc.
विराट्-उपासकाः तु विना स्थूल-देहं लिङ्ग-देह-मात्रस्य कुत्रापि अननुभूतत्वात् विराट्-पुरुषः एव ईश्वरः इति आहुः ।
Worshippers of Virāj, however, say that because a subtle body alone is nowhere experienced without a gross body, the cosmic person Virāj alone is Īśvara.
प्रजापति-उपासकाः तु प्रजा-कामाः सन्तः पाणि-पाद-आदि-युक्त-प्राकृत-शरीरवतः ईश्वरत्वे क्रिम्यादेः अपि ईश्वरत्व-प्रसङ्गात् हिरण्यगर्भ-उपासक-मतम् असङ्गतम् तथा विराट्-उपासक-मतम् अपि असङ्गतम् ।
The worshippers of Prajāpati, however, (being desirous of progeny) say: 'If an entity possessing a material body with hands, feet, etc. were Īśvara, even worms etc. would absurdly be Īśvara; therefore the view of Hiraṇyagarbha-worshippers is untenable, and likewise the view of Virāj-worshippers is untenable.'
किन्तु चतुर्मुखः ब्रह्मा एव ईश्वरः इति प्राहुः ।
'Rather, the four-faced Brahmā alone is Īśvara,' they declare.
वैष्णवाः तु विष्णोः नाभि-कमल-उत्पन्नत्वात् चतुर्मुखस्य ब्रह्मणः तत्-कारणीभूतः विष्णुः एव ईश्वरः इति कथयन्ति ।
The Vaiṣṇavas, however, state that since the four-faced Brahmā is born from the navel-lotus of Viṣṇu, Viṣṇu alone, being His cause, is Īśvara.
शैवाः तु शिवस्य पद-अन्वेषणे अशक्तत्वात् विष्णोः शिवः एव ईश्वरः इति वदन्ति ।
The Śaivas, however, declare that because Viṣṇu was incapable of finding Śiva's feet, Śiva alone is Īśvara.
गणपति-उपासकाः तु त्रिपुरासुर-जय-अर्थम् ईश्वरेण अपि उपासितः गणपतिः एव ईश्वरः इति मन्यन्ते ।
The worshippers of Gaṇapati, however, hold that Gaṇapati alone is Īśvara, because even Īśvara (Śiva) worshipped Him to conquer the demon Tripurāsura.
भैरव-मैराल-आदि-उपासकाः तु मारण-उच्चाटन-वशीकरण-स्तम्भन-आदि-सिद्धि-हेतु-भूत-भैरव-आदि-मन्त्रान् तत्-तत्-स्तोत्राणि तत्-हवन-तर्पण-पुरश्चरण-आदि-प्रतिपादक-तन्त्र-ग्रन्थान् च प्रमाणीकृत्य भैरव-आदि-देवताः ईश्वरत्वेन वर्णयन्ति ।
And the worshippers of Bhairava, Mairāla, etc., taking as authoritative the mantras of Bhairava etc. that yield accomplishments such as slaying, driving away, subjugating, and paralyzing, as well as their hymns and Tantric texts prescribing their oblations, libations, and puraścaraṇa, describe deities like Bhairava as Īśvara.
माया-अधिष्ठान-चैतन्यं च इति उभयं मिलित्वा ईश्वरः इति उच्यते ।
The combination of māyā and the substratum-consciousness together is called Īśvara.
अयम् च ईश्वरः मेघ-आकाश-तुल्यः भवति ।
And this Īśvara is comparable to the cloud-conditioned space (meghākāśa).
अयम् एव अन्तर्यामी इति उच्यते ।
He alone is called the inner controller (antaryāmin).
सर्वेषाम् अन्तःस्थः सन् नियन्तृत्वात् = प्रेरकत्वात् अन्तर्यामी ।
Being situated inside all, He is the inner controller (antaryāmin) because He is the regulator, that is, the impeller.
अयम् नित्य-मुक्तः स्व-स्वरूप-आवारक-अज्ञान-अभावात् तस्य ।
He is ever-liberated, because for Him there is absence of ignorance veiling His own true nature.
अतः एव जन्म-मरण-आदि-बन्ध-प्रतीतिः अस्य न अस्ति ततः एव ईश्वरः नित्य-मुक्तः इति उच्यते ।
For this very reason He has no perception of bondage such as birth and death; hence alone is Īśvara called ever-liberated.
किञ्च ईश्वरः सर्वज्ञः तस्य उपाधि-भूत-मायायाः शुद्ध-सत्त्व-गुण-प्रधानत्वात् अस्य सर्वज्ञत्व-सिद्धिः ।
Furthermore, Īśvara is omniscient; His omniscience is established because His limiting adjunct, māyā, has pure sattva as its predominant quality.
स्व-प्रतिबन्धकी-भूत-रजस्-तमसौ अभिभूय स्वयं ताभ्याम् अनभिभूतः यः सत्त्व-गुणः तस्य शुद्ध-सत्त्वम् इति आख्या ।
That sattva quality which, having overpowered rajas and tamas that obstruct it, remains itself unoverpowered by them, is designated as 'pure sattva'.
सत्त्व-गुणात् एव ज्ञानम् उत्पद्यते ।
From the sattva quality alone knowledge is generated.
अतः सत्त्व-गुणः प्रकाश-स्वभावः ।
Therefore, the sattva quality is illuminating by nature.
एवम्-भूत-सत्त्व-गुण-प्रधान-मायायां प्रतिफलित-चैतन्य-आभास-रूप-ईश्वरस्य स्व-विषये विषय-अन्तरे वा न एव आवरणं सम्भवति ।
For Īśvara, who is in the form of the reflection of consciousness in māyā characterized predominantly by such sattva, no veiling is possible at all, whether regarding Himself or regarding any other object.
तस्मात् ईश्वरः नित्य-मुक्तः सर्वज्ञः च भवति ।
Therefore Īśvara is ever-liberated and omniscient.
जीव-ईश्वरयोः अधिष्ठान-भूतं शुद्ध-चैतन्यं बन्ध-मोक्ष-आदि-निखिल-भेद-शून्यं सदा आकाशवत् एक-रस-स्वभावं तयोः उभयोः अपि वर्तते ।
The pure consciousness that is the substratum of both jīva and Īśvara, which is free from all distinctions such as bondage and liberation and is ever of one homogenous essence like space, is present in both of them alike.
बन्ध-मोक्ष-आदिः तु आभास-अंशे एव ।
Bondage, liberation, etc., however, pertain only to the reflection (ābhāsa) portion.
अधिष्ठाने चैतन्ये तु आभासस्य भ्रान्त्या प्रतीयते ।
In the substratum consciousness, however, that of the reflection appears only through delusion.
तस्मात् केवल-आभासे एव बन्ध-मोक्ष-आदि-व्यवहारः ।
Therefore, all empirical discourse of bondage, liberation, etc., applies only to the mere reflection.
इत्थम् अनन्त-मतानि स्व-स्व-मति-विलसितानि परस्पर-विलक्षणानि अन्योन्य-विरुद्धानि च उपलभ्यन्ते ।
In this way, endless doctrines, spun by individual intellects, differing from one another and mutually conflicting, are found.
