Therefore, the definition of pramā does not suffer from over-extension (ativyāpti) to illusory knowledge.
स्मृतिज्ञानमपि प्रमेत्यङ्गीकर्तृमते स्मृतिज्ञानमन्तःकरणस्य वृत्तिरूपं न त्वविद्याया वृत्तिरूपम् ।
In the view of those who accept memory as pramā, memory-cognition is a modification of the internal organ and not a modification of avidyā.
नापि साक्ष्याश्रयम्, अन्तःकरणवृत्तेः प्रमात्राश्रयत्वेन साक्ष्याश्रयत्वाभावात् ।
Nor does it reside in the Witness, because a modification of the internal organ resides in the knower and thus lacks residence in the Witness.
इत्थं केषाञ्चिन्मते स्मृतिज्ञानं अन्तःकरणवृत्तिरूपत्वात् प्रमा भवति ।
Thus, in the opinion of some, memory-cognition is pramā because it is a modification of the internal organ.
केषाञ्चिन्मते तु अविद्यावृत्तिरूपत्वान्न प्रमा ।
In the opinion of others, however, it is not pramā because it is a modification of avidyā.
भ्रान्तिज्ञानं संशयज्ञानं च सर्वमतस्थैरप्यविद्यावृत्तित्वेन साक्ष्याश्रितत्वेन चाभ्युपगम्यते ।
Illusory cognition and doubtful cognition are accepted by adherents of all schools as modifications of avidyā and as residing directly in the Witness.
न विवादोऽस्त्यत्र ।
There is no dispute on this point.
विचार्यमाणे तु स्मृतिज्ञानमप्यविद्यावृत्तिरूपं साक्ष्याश्रयं च; न प्रमा ।
Upon closer examination, however, memory-cognition too is a modification of avidyā and resides in the Witness; it is not pramā.
वेदान्तसम्प्रदायज्ञा अपि प्रमाज्ञानं षोढा विभजन्ति ।
The authorities on the Vedānta tradition also classify valid knowledge into six kinds.
स्मृतेस्तत्रानन्तर्भूतत्वात् न स्मृतिज्ञानं प्रमा ।
Since memory is not included among them, memory-cognition is not pramā.
मधुसूदनस्वामिनोऽपि स्मृतिज्ञानं साक्ष्याश्रयमित्येवावोचन् ।
Svāmī Madhusūdana Sarasvatī also declared that memory-cognition resides solely in the Witness.
212 · षड्विधाः प्रमाः
इदानीं षड्विधप्रमा निर्दिश्यन्ते- (१) प्रत्यक्षप्रमा, (२) अनुमितिप्रमा, (३) उपमितिप्रमा, (४) शाब्दी प्रमा, (५) अर्थापत्तिप्रमा, (६) अभावप्रमा चेति ।
Now, six kinds of valid cognition (pramā) are specified: (1) perceptual valid cognition (pratyakṣa-pramā), (2) inferential valid cognition (anumiti-pramā), (3) comparative valid cognition (upamiti-pramā), (4) verbal valid cognition (śābdī pramā), (5) postulative valid cognition (arthāpatti-pramā), and (6) non-apprehension valid cognition (abhāva-pramā).
पूर्वोक्तानि प्रत्यक्षादिप्रमाणानि क्रमेणैतासां षण्णां प्रमाणां करणानि भवन्ति ।1,2
The aforementioned means of valid knowledge (*pramāṇa*s) beginning with perception are, respectively, the instrumental causes (*karaṇa*s) of these six valid cognitions (*pramā*s).
टिप्पणी
1.
यथार्थानुभवः प्रमेति स्मृतिव्यावृत्तं प्रमालक्षणम् ।
'Valid cognition (*pramā*) is veridical non-recollective experience (*yathārthānubhava*)' is the definition of *pramā* that excludes recollection (*smṛti*).
यथार्थज्ञानं प्रमेति प्रमालक्षणं तु स्मृतिसाधारणमिति विवेकः ।
Whereas the definition 'valid cognition is veridical knowledge (*yathārtha-jñāna*)' is common to recollection too—such is the distinction.
2.
भ्रमरूपानुभवजसंस्कारजनितस्मृतिर्बाधितार्थविषयकत्वादयथार्थज्ञानम् ।
Recollection generated by latent impressions born of an erroneous experience is non-veridical knowledge (*ayathārtha-jñāna*) because its content is a sublated object.
यथार्थानुभवजसंस्कारजनितस्मृतिरबाधितार्थविषयकत्वाद्यथार्थज्ञानं भवति ।
Recollection generated by latent impressions born of a veridical experience is veridical knowledge (*yathārtha-jñāna*) because its content is an unsublated object.
अत एव तादृशस्मृतिज्ञानमन्तःकरणवृत्तिरूपम्, नाविद्यावृत्तिरूपम्; प्रमातारमाश्रितम्, न साक्षिणम् ।
Precisely for this reason, such recollective knowledge is in the form of a mental modification (*antaḥkaraṇa-vṛtti*), not a modification of ignorance (*avidyā-vṛtti*); and it rests upon the empirical knower (*pramātṛ*), not directly upon the witness (*sākṣin*).
तथापि प्राचीना न स्मृतिज्ञानं प्रमेति व्यवहरन्ति ।
Even so, ancient thinkers do not treat recollective knowledge as *pramā* (valid cognition).
तस्माद्द्विविधस्मृतिरप्यप्रमैव ।
Therefore, both forms of recollection are indeed non-valid cognition (*apramā*).
तयोरयथार्थस्मृतिः अयथार्थरूपा अप्रमा यथार्थस्मृतिः यथार्थरूपा अप्रमा इतीयानेव भेदः ।
Between the two, this alone is the difference: non-veridical recollection is non-veridical *apramā*, whereas veridical recollection is veridical *apramā*.
करणलक्षणं - तत्र प्रत्यक्षप्रमायाः करणं प्रत्यक्षप्रमाणं इत्युच्यते ।
The definition of an instrument (*karaṇa*): There, the instrument of perceptual valid cognition is called perceptual means of knowledge (*pratyakṣa-pramāṇa*).
असाधारणकारणं एव करणम् ।
The unique (uncommon) cause alone is the instrument (*karaṇa*).
यत् सकलकार्याणां तुल्यतया कारणं भवति, तत् साधारणकारणम् ।
That which is equally a cause for all effects is a common cause (*sādhāraṇa-kāraṇa*).
कार्यत्वाविच्छन्ननिष्ठकार्यतानिरूपितकारणताशालि यत् तत् साधारणकारणम् ।
That which possesses the causality determined by the effectness inherent in being-an-effect-as-such is a common cause (*sādhāraṇa-kāraṇa*).
धर्माधर्मादिकं सकलकार्याणां कारणत्वात् साधारणकारणम् ।
Merit, demerit (*dharma*, *adharma*), etc., being causes of all effects without exception, are common causes.
सकलकार्याणां कारणभावमनासाद्य कतिपयकार्याणामेव विशिष्य कारणभावं यद्भजते तदसाधारणकारणम् ।
That which, without serving as the cause for all effects, specifically assumes the status of cause for only certain effects, is an uncommon cause (*asādhāraṇa-kāraṇa*).
कार्यत्वातिरिक्तधर्मावच्छिन्ननिष्ठकार्यतानिरूपितकारणताशालि यत् तदसाधारणकारणम् ।
That which possesses causality determined by effectness delimited by an attribute distinct from being-an-effect-as-such is an uncommon cause (*asādhāraṇa-kāraṇa*).
दण्डो हि न सकलकार्याणां कारणं भवति, किन्तु घटादिरूपकार्यविशेषाणामेव कारणं भवति ।
For the potter's stick is not the cause of all effects, but is the cause of specific effects such as pots alone.
तस्माद्दण्डो घटादीनां असाधारणकारणमिति करणमिति चोच्यते ।
Therefore, the stick is called the uncommon cause (*asādhāraṇa-kāraṇa*) and instrument (*karaṇa*) of a pot, etc.
एवमेव प्रत्यक्षप्रमायाः ईश्वरस्तदिच्छादयश्च साधारणकारणानि ।
Just so, with respect to perceptual valid cognition, Īśvara, His will, etc., are common causes (*sādhāraṇa-kāraṇa*s).
यस्मादीश्वरादयः सकलकार्याणि प्रति कारणानि भवन्ति, यस्माच्च न किञ्चिदपि कार्यमीश्वरादिकं विनोत्पद्यते तस्मादीश्वरादयः साधारणकारणानि ।
Because Īśvara and the like are causes with respect to all effects, and because not a single effect is produced without Īśvara, etc., therefore Īśvara and the rest are common causes.
चक्षुरादीनीन्द्रियाणि प्रत्यक्षप्रमां प्रत्यसाधारणकारणानि ।
The sense organs such as the eye are the uncommon causes with respect to perceptual valid cognition.
अतस्तानि प्रत्यक्षप्रमां प्रति करणानि च भवन्ति ।
Hence, they are indeed the instruments (*karaṇa*s) with respect to perceptual valid cognition.
एवञ्च चक्षुरादीनीन्द्रियाणि प्रत्यक्षप्रमाणानीत्युच्यन्ते ।
And thus, sense organs like the eye are designated as perceptual means of knowledge (*pratyakṣa-pramāṇa*s).
213 · प्रमातृप्रमाणप्रमाप्रमेयचैतन्यानि
ननु वेदान्तसिद्धान्ते चक्षुरादीन्द्रियाणां प्रत्यक्षप्रमाकारणत्वं 1न युज्यते ।
Objection: In the Vedānta system, it is not tenable for the sense organs like the eye to be the instrumental cause of perceptual valid cognition (pratyakṣa-pramā).
तथा हि, वेदान्तसिद्धान्ते चत्वारश्चैतन्यभेदाः सन्ति (१) प्रमातृचैतन्यम्, (२) प्रमाणचैतन्यम्, (३) प्रमिति2
To explain: in the Vedānta doctrine, there are four divisions of consciousness: (1) pramātṛ-caitanya (knower-consciousness), (2) pramāṇa-caitanya (instrumental consciousness), (3) pramiti-caitanya…
टिप्पणी
1.
केवलसाधारणकारणं करणमित्युक्ते यत्रासाधारणकारणद्वयं प्राप्तं तत्रेदमेव करणमिति विनिगमकाभावादेकस्य द्वाररूपकारणत्वमन्यस्य व्यापारवदसाधारणकारणत्वरूपकरणत्वं चाभ्युपेयम् ।
If it is defined that 'an extraordinary cause is a karaṇa', then where two extraordinary causes are found, due to the absence of a decisive determinant to specify 'this alone is the karaṇa', one must accept that one is an intermediary cause (dvāra-rūpa-kāraṇa) and the other is the karaṇa in the form of an extraordinary cause possessed of an operation (vyāpāravat-asādhāraṇa-kāraṇa).
यत्तु द्वाररूपकारणं पुरस्कृत्य कार्यं जनयति, तदेवासाधारणकारणरूपं करणं भवति ।
That which produces the effect by employing an intermediary cause, that alone is the karaṇa in the nature of an extraordinary cause.
तद्यथा कपालद्वयं, संयोगद्वारा घटस्योत्पादकत्वात्, घटं प्रति व्यापारवदसाधारणकरणरूपं करणम् ।
For example, the two halves of a pot (kapāla-dvaya), because they produce the pot through the medium of conjunction (saṁyoga), are the karaṇa with respect to the pot, in the form of an extraordinary cause possessed of an operation.
यत्तु व्यापारशून्यं सत् द्वारकारणमनपेक्ष्य साक्षादेव कार्यं जनयति, तत् केवलकारणम्, न तु करणम् ।
However, that which, being devoid of an operation, produces the effect directly without depending on an intermediary cause, is a mere cause (kevala-kāraṇa), not a karaṇa.
यथा कपालद्वयसंयोगः साक्षादेव घटोत्पादकत्वात् केवलकारणम्, न तु करणम् ।
Just as the conjunction of the two pot-halves, being the direct producer of the pot, is a mere cause and not a karaṇa.
व्यापारवदसाधारणकारणं करणमित्यस्य लक्षणस्य प्रत्यक्षानुमानशब्दाख्यप्रमाणेषु सम्भवेऽपि उपमानार्थापत्त्यनुपलब्ध्याख्यप्रमाणेष्वसम्भवादव्याप्तिः ।
Although the definition 'a karaṇa is an extraordinary cause possessed of an operation' is applicable to the pramāṇas called perception, inference, and verbal testimony, there is the defect of under-inclusion (avyāpti) because it does not apply to the pramāṇas known as comparison (upamāna), postulation (arthāpatti), and non-apprehension (anupalabdhi).
उपमित्यादीनां जनने विनैव व्यापारमुपमानादीनां कारणत्वसम्भवात्पूर्वोक्तकरणलक्षणस्य तत्राव्याप्तिः स्यात् ।
Because comparison etc. can be causes in generating analogical cognition (upamiti) etc. without any intermediate operation at all, the previously mentioned definition of karaṇa would suffer from avyāpti in those cases.
अतो व्यापारभिन्नमसाधारणकारणं करणमित्यस्य लक्षणस्य निर्दुष्टत्वात्तदेव सर्वप्रमाणानुगतकरणलक्षणम् ।
Therefore, because the definition 'a karaṇa is an extraordinary cause distinct from an operation (vyāpāra-bhinna-asādhāraṇa-kāraṇam)' is faultless, that alone is the definition of karaṇa conforming to all pramāṇas.
2.
आदिशब्देन ईश्वरस्य ज्ञानम्, ईश्वरस्य प्रयत्नः, कालः, दिक्, अदृष्टम्, प्रागभावः, प्रतिबन्धकाभावश्चेति सप्त गृह्यन्ते ।
By the word 'ādi' (etcetera), seven factors are comprehended: Īśvara's knowledge, Īśvara's volition, time, space, the unseen merit/demerit (adṛṣṭa), prior non-existence (prāgabhāva), and the absence of impediments.
अमी ईश्वरादयो नव सर्वकार्याणां साधारणकारणानि ।
These nine, beginning with Īśvara, are the common causes (sādhāraṇa-kāraṇa) for all effects.
चैतन्यमथवा प्रमाचैतन्यम्, (४) प्रमेयचैतन्यमथवा विषयचैतन्यमिति ।
...[pramiti-]caitanya or pramā-caitanya, (4) prameya-caitanya or viṣaya-caitanya.
वेदान्तमते प्रमा नाम चैतन्यमेव ।
In the view of Advaita Vedānta, valid cognition (*pramā*) is indeed *caitanya* (consciousness) alone.
तच्च चैतन्यं नित्यम्, नेन्द्रियजन्यम्; तस्मान्नेन्द्रियं तत्कारणमिति चेत् ।
If it is objected: 'And that consciousness is eternal and not generated by the sense-organs; therefore the sense-organ cannot be its instrument'
तन्न, चैतन्यस्य प्रमात्वापादिका वृत्तिरपि प्रमेत्युच्यते ।
That objection does not hold; for the *vṛtti* (mental modification) which brings about the condition of valid knowledge in consciousness is also termed *pramā* (by secondary application).
तस्या वृत्तेरिन्द्रियं करणम् ।
The sense organ is the instrumental cause (*karaṇa*) of that *vṛtti*.
(१) प्रमातृचैतन्यं - देहमध्यवृत्त्यन्तःकरणेनावच्छिन्नं चैतन्यं प्रमातृचैतन्यं इत्युच्यते ।
(1) Pramātṛ-caitanya: The consciousness delimited by the internal organ (*antaḥkaraṇa*) situated within the body is called *pramātṛ-caitanya* (the consciousness as the knower).
(२) प्रमाणचैतन्यं - इदमेवान्तःकरणं चक्षुरादीन्द्रियद्वारा बहिर्निर्गत्य घटादिविषयदेशपर्यन्तं दीर्घीभावरूपपरिणामं प्राप्नोति ।
(2) Pramāṇa-caitanya: This very internal organ, issuing out through the doors of the sense-organs such as the eye, undergoes an elongation-modification reaching up to the locus of objects like a pot.
ततो घटादिविषयैः संसृज्य घटादितत्तद्विषयाकारेण च परिणमते ।
Then, having come into contact with objects such as a pot, it transforms into the form of those respective objects.
यथा तडाकोदकं प्रणालीद्वारा बहिर्निर्गत्य कुल्यात्मना परिणामं प्राप्य केदारान् प्रविश्य तत्तच्चतुष्कोणादिरूपकेदाराकारं भवति, तथैवान्तःकरणमपि चक्षुरादीन्द्रियच्छिद्रद्वारा बहिर्निर्गत्य विषयरूपकेदारं प्राप्य विषयाकारं भवति ।
Just as water from a reservoir goes out through an outlet, takes the form of a canal, enters fields, and assumes the four-cornered or other shapes of those fields, so too the internal organ goes out through the apertures of the senses like the eye, reaches the field-like object, and assumes the form of that object.
तत्र देहदेशमारभ्य घटादिविषयदेशपर्यन्तं योऽन्तःकरणस्य दीर्घीभावरूपः परिणामः, स एव वृत्तिज्ञानं इत्युच्यते ।
There, that elongation-modification of the *antaḥkaraṇa* spanning from the bodily region to the region of objects like a pot is called *vṛtti-jñāna*.
वृत्तिज्ञानरूपो योऽन्तःकरणपरिणामः स प्रमाणं इति कथ्यते ।
That modification of the *antaḥkaraṇa* which has the form of modal cognition (*vṛtti-jñāna*) is spoken of as *pramāṇa*.
तेनावच्छिन्नं चैतन्यं प्रमाणचैतन्यं इत्यभिधीयते ।
The consciousness delimited by that modification is termed *pramāṇa-caitanya*.
(३) प्रमितिचैतन्यमथवा प्रमाचैतन्यं - केदारं प्रविश्य यथा जलं केदारसमाकारं भवति, तथा घटादिविषयं प्राप्यान्तःकरणवृत्तिरपि घटादिविषयसमानाकारतां भजते ।
(3) Pramiti-caitanya or Pramā-caitanya: Just as water entering a field takes the shape of the field, so too the mental mode (*antaḥkaraṇa-vṛtti*), reaching an object like a pot, takes on an identical form to that object.
तादृशविषयसमानाकारतयावच्छिन्नचैतन्यं प्रमाचैतन्यं इत्युच्यते ।
The consciousness delimited by such an object-shaped *vṛtti* is called *pramā-caitanya* (or *pramiti-caitanya*).
(४) प्रमेयचैतन्यमथवा विषयचैतन्यं - ज्ञानविषयीभूतघटाद्यवच्छिन्नचैतन्यं विषयचैतन्यम्, प्रमेयचैतन्यं इति चोच्यते ।
(4) Prameya-caitanya or Viṣaya-caitanya: The consciousness delimited by objects such as a pot that have become the content of cognition is called *viṣaya-caitanya* or *prameya-caitanya*.
एताः सर्वा वेदार्थसम्प्रदायविदाचार्यकृतपरिभाषाः ।
All these are technical terminologies established by the Ācāryas well-versed in the tradition of the meaning of the Vedas.
प्रमातृलक्षणम्॥ २१४–२१७ ॥
214 · अवच्छेदवादरीत्या प्रमातृसाक्षिणोः स्वरूपम्; विशेषणलक्षणमुपाधिलक्षणं च
अवच्छेदवादरीत्या अन्तःकरणविशिष्टचैतन्यं प्रमाता ।
According to the doctrine of delimitation (avacchedavāda), Consciousness qualified by the internal organ is the knower (pramātā).
स एव कर्ता भोक्ता च ।
He alone is the agent and the experiencer.
अन्तःकरणोपहितचैतन्यं साक्षी ।
Consciousness conditioned by the internal organ is the witness (sākṣin).
एकमेवान्तःकरणं प्रमातुर्विशेषणत्वेन साक्षिण उपाधित्वेन च भवति ।
The very same internal organ serves as a qualifying attribute (viśeṣaṇa) for the knower and as a limiting condition (upādhi) for the witness (sākṣin).
विशेषणलक्षणं - वस्तुस्वरूपे यस्य प्रवेशः अस्ति, तादृशं व्यावर्तकम्1
The definition of an attribute (viśeṣaṇa) is: that differentiating factor which enters into the essential nature of the thing.
टिप्पणी
1.
प्रवेशः = कार्येण सह सम्बन्धः ।
'Entry' means relation with the effect/action.
वस्तु विशेषणं इत्युच्यते ।
Such an entity is called a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa).
कार्यान्वयित्वे सति व्यावर्तकत्वे सति विद्यमानत्वं विशेषणस्य लक्षणम् ।
The definition of a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa) is: being present while differentiating, as well as entering into connection with the action/effect.
पदार्थान्तरेभ्यो विविच्य वस्तुस्वरूपावेदकं यत् तत् व्यावर्तकं इत्युच्यते ।
That which reveals the entity's nature by distinguishing it from other entities is called a differentiator (vyāvartaka).
इतरेभ्यो भिन्नतया यद्बुध्यते तद्व्यावर्त्यं इत्युच्यते ।
That which is cognised as distinct from others is called the differentiated (vyāvartya).
नीलो घटः इत्यत्र घटस्य नीलवर्णं विशेषणम् ।
In the statement 'The pot is blue', the blue colour is the qualifier of the pot.
यतो नीलवर्णं नीलघटस्वरूपे प्रविष्टं सत् रक्तपीतश्वेतादिवर्णविशिष्टघटेभ्यो व्यावर्त्य पृथगिमं नीलघटं बोधयति, तस्मान्नीलवर्णं व्यावर्तकं विशेषणञ्च ।
Because the blue colour, having entered into the being of the blue pot, makes this blue pot known separately by distinguishing it from pots qualified by red, yellow, white, and other colours, therefore the blue colour is both a differentiator and a qualifier.
घटस्तु परिच्छेद्यः, यतः पीतादिवर्णविशिष्टघटादिभ्यो विविच्यायं नीलघटो बुद्ध्यते ।
The pot, however, is the object delimited, because this blue pot is cognised as distinguished from pots qualified by yellow and other colours.
यस्तु विविच्य बुद्ध्यते पदार्थः, स हि परिच्छेद्यः, व्यावर्त्यः, विशेष्यं इति चोच्यते ।
And that entity which is cognised as distinguished is indeed called the delimited (paricchedya), the differentiated (vyāvartya), and the substantive (viśeṣya).
दण्डी पुरुषः इत्यादावपि दण्डादिकं पुरुषस्य विशेषणम् ।
In examples such as 'The man with a staff', the staff and the like are the qualifiers of the man.
इत्थं प्रमातुरन्तःकरणं विशेषणं भवति, तस्य प्रमातृस्वरूपे प्रवेशात् ।
In this manner, the antaḥkaraṇa is a qualifier of the knower (pramātṛ), because it enters into the very constitution of the knower.
तथा प्रमेयचैतन्याद्व्यावर्त्य प्रमातृस्वरूपस्य बोधकत्वादन्तःकरणं व्यावर्तकं च भवति ।
Likewise, the antaḥkaraṇa is also a differentiator, because it reveals the nature of the knower by distinguishing it from the consciousness underlying the known object (prameya-caitanya).
उपाधिलक्षणं - यस्तु वस्तुस्वरूपे अन्तरेणैव प्रवेशं व्यावर्तको भवति स उपाधिरित्युच्यते ।
Definition of an upādhi: that which differentiates without entering into the nature of the entity is called an upādhi.
कार्यानन्वयित्वे सति व्यावर्तकत्वे सति विद्यमानत्वमुपाधिलक्षणम् ।
The definition of an upādhi is: being present and differentiating, while not entering into the action/effect.
नैयायिकमते कर्णशष्कुल्यवच्छिन्नं नभः श्रोत्रम् इत्युच्यते ।
In the Naiyāyika system it is said: 'Space delimited by the ear-cavity is the organ of hearing (śrotra)'.
तत्र कर्णगोलकं श्रोत्रस्योपाधिर्भवति ।
There, the physical ear-socket is the upādhi of the auditory organ.
कर्णगोलकं श्रोत्रेन्द्रियस्वरूपे प्रवेशमन्तरेणैव बाह्यभूताकाशाद्विविच्य श्रोत्रेन्द्रियं बोधयति ।
The physical ear-socket makes the auditory organ known by distinguishing it from external space, without ever entering into the intrinsic nature of the sense-organ.
तस्मात् कर्णगोलकं व्यावर्तकं भवति ।
Therefore, the ear-socket is a differentiator.
घटाकाशः प्रस्थपरिमितान्नस्यावकाशं ददाति इत्यत्र घट आकाशस्योपाधिरेव ।
In the statement 'The pot-space provides room for a prastha-measure of food', the pot is only an upādhi of space.
प्रस्थपरिमितान्नावाकाशदात्राकाशस्वरूपे प्रवेशं विनैव घटो महाकाशाद्विभज्य घटाकाशं बोधयति ।
Without entering into the nature of the space that provides room for the prastha of food, the pot makes known the pot-space by dividing it from total space (mahākāśa).
घटस्य पृथिवीकार्यत्वेनावकाशप्रदत्वासम्भवादाकाशस्वरूपे प्रवेशो न युज्यते ।
Since the pot is an effect of earth and cannot provide space, its entry into the nature of space is impossible.
तस्माद्घट आकाशस्योपाधिरेव ।
Therefore, the pot is only an upādhi of space.
एवमेवान्तःकरणोपहितचैतन्यं साक्षीत्यत्र साक्षिणोऽन्तःकरणमुपाधिः ।
In the very same way, in the formulation 'Consciousness conditioned by the internal organ is the witness (sākṣin)', the antaḥkaraṇa is an upādhi of the witness.
न ह्यन्तःकरणस्य साक्षिस्वरूपे प्रवेशो भवति ।
For the antaḥkaraṇa does not enter into the intrinsic nature of the witness.
किन्त्वन्तःकरणं प्रमेयचैतन्याद्विविच्य साक्षिणं बोधयति ।
Rather, the antaḥkaraṇa reveals the witness by distinguishing it from the consciousness underlying the known object.
तस्मादेकमेवान्तःकरणं साक्षिण उपाधित्वेन प्रमातुर्विशेषणत्वेन च भवति ।
Therefore, the very same antaḥkaraṇa acts as an upādhi in relation to the witness, and as a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa) in relation to the knower (pramātṛ).
अन्तःकरणोपहितचैतन्यं साक्षी ।
Consciousness conditioned by the antaḥkaraṇa is the witness (sākṣin).
अन्तःकरणविशिष्टचैतन्यं प्रमाता ।
Consciousness qualified by the antaḥkaraṇa is the knower (pramātṛ).
उपाधिना युक्तं उपहितं इति विशेषणेन युक्तं विशिष्टं इति चोच्यते ।
That which is joined with an upādhi is called 'conditioned' (upahita), and that which is joined with a qualifier is called 'qualified' (viśiṣṭa).
तत्रान्तःकरणविशिष्टः प्रमातैव कर्ता, भोक्ता, सुखी, दुखी, संसारी, जीवो भवति ।
Among them, the knower alone, qualified by the antaḥkaraṇa, is the doer, experiencer, happy, unhappy, transmigrating individual soul (jīva).
इत्थं अवच्छेदवादरीत्या प्रमात्रादिलक्षणं निरूपितम् ।
Thus, according to the doctrine of delimitation (avacchedavāda), the definitions of the knower and related entities have been expounded.
215 · आभासवादरीत्या जीवसाक्षिणोः स्वरूपं
आभासवादे आभाससहितान्तःकरणं जीवस्य विशेषणम्, साक्षिण उपाधिश्च भवति ।
In the theory of reflection (ābhāsavāda), the internal organ (antaḥkaraṇa) along with the reflection (ābhāsa) is the qualifying attribute (viśeṣaṇa) of the jīva, and it is the limiting adjunct (upādhi) of the witness-consciousness (sākṣin).
अत एवाभाससहितान्तःकरणविशिष्टचैतन्यं जीवः ।
Therefore, consciousness qualified by the antaḥkaraṇa along with the reflection is the jīva.
आभाससहितान्तःकरणोपहितचैतन्यं साक्षी ।
Consciousness conditioned by the antaḥkaraṇa along with the reflection is the sākṣin.
यद्यपि पक्षद्वयेऽपि विशेषणसहितचैतन्यं जीवः, स एव संसारी च; तथापि विशेष्यभागे चैतन्ये जननमरणादिसंसारो न सम्भवति ।
Although in both views consciousness accompanied by the qualifier is the jīva, and that alone is the transmigrating entity; still, in the substantival part (viśeṣyabhāga), which is consciousness, the worldly transmigratory existence consisting of birth, death, and so forth is not possible.
तस्माद्विशेषणमात्रे संसारः पर्यवस्यति; स एव विशिष्टचैतन्ये प्रतीयते ।
Therefore, saṃsāra culminates in the qualifier alone; and that very saṃsāra is perceived in the qualified consciousness.
(१) क्वचिद्विशेषणगतधर्माणां व्यवहारो विशिष्टे भवति ।
(1) In some cases, the attribution of properties residing in the qualifier occurs with respect to the qualified whole.
(२) क्वचिद्विशेष्यगतधर्माणां व्यवहारो विशिष्टे भवति ।
(2) In some cases, the attribution of properties residing in the substantival element occurs with respect to the qualified whole.
(३) क्वचिद्विशेषणविशेष्योभयगतधर्माणां व्यवहारो विशिष्टे भवति ।
(3) In some cases, the attribution of properties residing in both the qualifier and the substantive occurs with respect to the qualified whole.
तद्यथा - (१) दण्डेन घटाकाशो नश्यति इत्यत्र विशेषणीभूतघट एव दण्डेन नश्यति, न तु विशेष्यभूताकाशः ।
To illustrate—(1) in the statement 'The pot-space is destroyed by a stick', only the pot, which has become the qualifier, is destroyed by the stick, not the space which is the substantive.
तथापि विशिष्टे घटाकाशे नाशः प्रतीतो भवति ।
Even so, destruction is perceived in the qualified entity, the pot-space.
(२) कुण्डली पुरुषः स्वपिति इत्यत्र विशेषणे कुण्डले स्वापो नान्वेति; विशेष्ये पुरुषे तु स्वापः सम्भवति ।
(2) In the statement 'The earring-wearing man sleeps', sleep does not apply to the qualifier, the earring; sleep, however, is possible in the substantive, the man.
तथापि कुण्डलविशिष्टः स्वपिति इति विशिष्टे स्वापव्यवहारो भवति ।
Even so, there is the predication of sleep with respect to the qualified whole, in the form 'The earring-qualified one sleeps'.
(३) आयुधपाणिः पुरुषो योद्धुं याति इत्यत्र विशेषणस्यायुधस्य विशेष्यस्य पुरुषस्य च युद्धाय गमनादुभयोरपि धर्मो विशिष्टे व्यवह्रियते ।
(3) In the statement 'The weapon-handed man goes to fight', because of both the qualifier (the weapon) and the substantive (the man) going to the battle, the property of both is predicated of the qualified whole.
प्रकृते त्ववच्छेदवादेऽन्तःकरणं विशेषणम्, आभासवादे आभाससहितान्तःकरणं विशेषणम्; द्वयोरपि पक्षयोश्चैतन्यं विशेष्यम् ।
In the present context, however, in avacchedavāda the antaḥkaraṇa is the qualifier, whereas in ābhāsavāda the antaḥkaraṇa along with the reflection is the qualifier; in both views, pure consciousness is the substantive.
तस्मिंश्चैतन्ये जन्मादिसंसारो न सम्भवति ।
In that consciousness, saṃsāra beginning with birth is not possible.
किन्तु विशेषणस्यान्तःकरणस्य वा आभाससहितान्तःकरणस्य वा धर्मभूतो यो जन्मादिरूपः संसारः सोऽविवेकिभिर्भ्रान्त्या विशिष्टचैतन्ये व्यवह्रियते ।
Rather, that saṃsāra in the form of birth, etc., which is an attribute of the qualifier—either of the antaḥkaraṇa or of the antaḥkaraṇa along with the reflection—is erroneously attributed by the indiscriminate to the qualified consciousness.
व्यवहारो नाम प्रतीतिः कथनञ्च ।
'Vyavahāra' (attribution / usage) means both cognitive perception and verbal expression.
अनया रीत्या आभासवादावच्छेदवादयोर्भेदोऽवगन्तव्यः ।
In this manner, the distinction between ābhāsavāda and avacchedavāda should be understood.
216 · आभासवादस्य ज्यायस्त्वं
आभासवादेऽन्तःकरणमाभाससहितम्, अवच्छेदवादे तद्रहितं च भवति ।
In the doctrine of reflection (ābhāsavāda), the internal organ is endowed with an *ābhāsa* (reflection), and in the doctrine of limitation (avacchedavāda), it is devoid of that.
द्वयोर्मध्ये आभासवादो ज्यायान् ।
Between the two, the doctrine of *ābhāsa* is superior.
भाष्यकारैराभासवाद एव स्वीकृतः ।
Indeed, the Bhāṣyakāra (Śaṅkara) has accepted the doctrine of *ābhāsa* itself.
अवच्छेदवादे विद्यारण्यमुनयो दोषमप्याहुः ।
Sage Vidyāraṇya has also pointed out a defect in the doctrine of limitation.
तथा हि, आभासरहितान्तःकरणावच्छिन्नचैतन्यस्य प्रमातृत्वाभ्युपगमे घटावच्छिन्नचैतन्यस्यापि प्रमातृत्वं प्रसज्येत ।
To explain: if one accepts that Consciousness delimited by an internal organ that is devoid of *ābhāsa* is the knower (pramātṛ), then Consciousness delimited by a pot would also absurdly become a knower.
यतोऽन्तःकरणवद्घटोऽपि भूतकार्यम्, अन्तःकरणं यथा चैतन्यस्यावच्छेदकमथवा व्यावर्तकं तथा घटोऽपि चैतन्यस्यावच्छेदको व्यावर्तकश्च; तस्मादन्तःकरणविशिष्टचैतन्यमिव घटावच्छिन्नचैतन्यमपि प्रमाता भवेदित्यापत्तिरपरिहार्या ।
Because just like the internal organ, a pot is also a product of the elements; and just as the internal organ is a delimiter or differentiator of Consciousness, so also a pot is a delimiter and differentiator of Consciousness; therefore, the absurd consequence that Consciousness delimited by a pot would also be a knower just like Consciousness qualified by the internal organ, becomes unavoidable.
अन्तःकरणे आभासस्याङ्गीकारे तु नास्य दोषस्यावकाशः ।
However, when the reflection (*ābhāsa*) is accepted in the internal organ, there is no scope for this defect.
तथा हि, अन्तःकरणं पञ्चतन्मात्रसमष्टिसत्त्वगुणकार्यत्वात् स्वच्छम् ।
To explain: the internal organ is clear (transparent/reflective) because it is a product of the collective *sattva-guṇa* of the five subtle elements (tanmātras).
घटादयः पञ्चीकृतपञ्चभूततमोगुणकार्यत्वादस्वच्छाः ।
Pots and other objects, on the other hand, are opaque because they are products of the *tamo-guṇa* of the quintupled five gross elements.
यत् स्वच्छं तत्राभासऽथवा प्रतिबिम्बो जायते ।
Whatever is clear/transparent, in that an *ābhāsa* or reflection is formed.
मलिने पदार्थे नाभासो जायते ।
In a dull/opaque object, no reflection is formed.
दर्पणस्य तत्पिधायककोशस्य च मृत्कार्यत्वाविशेषेऽपि स्वच्छे दर्पणे मुखस्याभासः प्रतीयते ।
Although there is no difference between a mirror and its covering leather/cloth case in both being ultimately material modifications (of earth), the reflection of a face is perceived only in the clear mirror.
अस्वच्छे दर्पणपिधायककोशे न मुखस्याभासः प्रतीयते ।
The reflection of the face is not perceived in the non-reflective mirror-case.
एवमेव सत्त्वगुणकार्यत्वात्स्वच्छेऽन्तःकरणे चैतन्याभासः प्रतीयते ।
In the very same way, because the internal organ is a product of *sattva-guṇa* and thus clear, the reflection of Consciousness (*caitanyābhāsa*) is perceived in it.
तमोगुणकार्यत्वादस्वच्छे शरीरादौ घटादौ च चैतन्याभासो न प्रतीयते ।
And in the body, pots, and so on, which are opaque because they are products of *tamo-guṇa*, the reflection of Consciousness is not perceived.
217
अन्तःकरणगतद्विविधप्रकाश एव प्रमाता; नान्यःइत्थमन्तःकरणे द्विविधः प्रकाशोऽस्ति; एको व्यापकचैतन्यस्य प्रकाशः, अपर आभासरूपचैतन्यस्य प्रकाशः ।
Only that which possesses the twofold light residing in the internal organ is the knower (pramātṛ), not anything else: thus, in the internal organ there is a twofold light — one is the light of the all-pervading Consciousness, and the other is the light of Consciousness as reflected (*ābhāsa*).
शरीरे घटादिषु च व्यापकचैतन्यस्य प्रकाश एक एवास्ति, द्वितीय आभासस्य प्रकाशो नास्ति ।
In the body, pots, etc., there is only one light — that of the all-pervading Consciousness; the second light, that of *ābhāsa*, is not present.
तस्माद्द्विविधप्रकाशसहितान्तःकरणविशिष्टचैतन्यमेव प्रमाता इत्युच्यते, न त्वेकप्रकाशमात्रसहितघटादिविशिष्टचैतन्यं प्रमाता ।
Therefore, only Consciousness qualified by the internal organ endowed with the twofold light is called the knower (pramātṛ), and not Consciousness qualified by a pot, etc., which has only a single light.
येषां मतेऽन्तःकरणे आभासो नास्ति तेषां मते घटादाविवान्तःकरणेऽपि द्वितीय आभासस्य प्रकाशो नास्ति ।
In the view of those who hold that there is no *ābhāsa* in the internal organ, just as in a pot, in the internal organ too the second light of *ābhāsa* is absent.
अपि च य एको व्यापकचैतन्यस्य प्रकाशोऽन्तःकरणेऽस्ति स एव घटादावप्यस्ति ।
Moreover, that single light of all-pervading Consciousness which exists in the internal organ is identically present in pots and the like as well.
तस्मादन्तःकरणविशिष्टचैतन्यस्य प्रमातृत्वाङ्गीकारे, घटविशिष्टस्य शरीरविशिष्टस्य कुड्यविशिष्टस्य च चैतन्यस्य प्रमातृत्वं स्वीकर्तव्यं भवेत् ।
Therefore, if Consciousness qualified merely by the internal organ is accepted as the knower, one would also have to accept knower-hood for Consciousness qualified by a pot, by the physical body, or by a wall.
इत्थं घटशरीराद्यपेक्षयान्तःकरणे ईदृशं वैलक्षण्यमस्ति ।
Thus, the internal organ possesses such a distinction in contrast to pots, bodies, and so on.
अत्र चायं हेतुः - सत्त्वगुणकार्यत्वादन्तःकरणं स्वच्छम्; अत एव तच्चैतन्याभासग्रहणयोग्यं च ।
And here is the reason: being a product of *sattva-guṇa*, the internal organ is clear, and therefore it is capable of capturing the reflection of Consciousness (*caitanyābhāsa*).
इतरपदार्थास्तु तमोगुणकार्यत्वादस्वच्छाः, अत एव ते चैतन्याभासग्रहणायोग्याश्च ।
Other entities, however, being products of *tamo-guṇa*, are opaque, and therefore they are unfit to hold a reflection of Consciousness.
आभासग्रहणयोग्यान्तःकरणविशिष्टचैतन्यमेव प्रमातेत्यभिधीयते; न त्वाभासग्रहणायोग्यघटादिविशिष्टचैतन्यं प्रमाता भवति ।
Only Consciousness qualified by the internal organ (which is capable of holding a reflection) is declared to be the knower; Consciousness qualified by pots and the like (which are incapable of holding a reflection) does not become a knower.
अत एवाभासवादः श्रेयान्, न त्ववच्छेदवादः ।
Therefore, the doctrine of reflection (ābhāsavāda) is superior, and not the doctrine of limitation (avacchedavāda).
टिप्पणी
1.
आभासवादे आभासस्य स्वरूपमधिकतया कल्पनीयं भवति ।
In *ābhāsavāda*, the entity called *ābhāsa* has to be postulated as an additional factor.
अवच्छेदवादे तु न इत्थं यद्यप्याभासवादे गौरवं अवच्छेदवादे लाघवं च, तथापि मन्दजिज्ञासोर्बुद्धावाभासवादः स्फुटमारूढो भवेदित्यनेनाभिप्रायेणाभासवादः स्तूयते ।
In *avacchedavāda*, it is not so; thus, although there is theoretical heaviness (gaurava) in *ābhāsavāda* and parsimony (lāghava) in *avacchedavāda*, nevertheless, with the intention that *ābhāsavāda* may be grasped clearly by an aspirant of moderate intellect, *ābhāsavāda* is praised.
भाष्यकारादीनामप्ययमेवाशयः ।
This alone is the intention of the Bhāṣyakāra and other masters as well.
218 · प्रमात्रादिचतुर्विधचैतन्यस्वरूपं
यथान्तःकरणमाभाससहितमेवास्ते तथा तद्वृत्तिरप्याभाससहितैव जायते ।
Just as the internal organ exists only along with the reflected consciousness (ābhāsa), so too its modification (vṛtti) arises only endowed with the reflection.
आभाससहितवृत्तिविशिष्टचैतन्यं प्रमाणचैतन्यं इत्युच्यते ।
Consciousness qualified by the modification endowed with the reflection is called pramāṇa-caitanya.
घटादिविषयाकारान्तःकरणवृत्त्यारूढं चैतन्यं प्रमेति, यथार्थज्ञानं इति वोच्यते ।
Consciousness mounted upon the mental modification that has taken the form of an object such as a pot is called pramā or accurate knowledge (yathārtha-jñāna).
प्रमायाः साधनमिन्द्रियं प्रमाणं इति कथ्यते ।
The sense organ, which is the instrument of valid knowledge, is called pramāṇa.
अत्रेदं ज्ञेयं - विषयाकारवृत्त्यारूढचैतन्यं प्रमेति कीर्त्यते ।
Here this should be understood: consciousness mounted on the modification shaped as the object is declared to be pramā.
तत्र चैतन्यस्य स्वरूपतो नित्यत्वान्नेन्द्रियजन्यत्वसम्भवः ।
There, because consciousness is essentially eternal, it is impossible for it to be produced by the sense organs.
अतश्च प्रमाचैतन्यं प्रतीन्द्रियस्य यद्यपि साधनत्वं न युज्यत एव तथाप्युपचारेणेन्द्रियस्य प्रमासाधनत्वव्यवहारः ।
And therefore, even though being an instrument towards pramā-consciousness is not strictly logical for a sense organ, its usage as the instrument of pramā is by figurative transference (upacāra).
तथा हि, उपाधिशून्यचैतन्ये प्रमाव्यवहाराभावात् विषयाकारवृत्त्युपहितचैतन्ये एव तद्व्यवहाराच्च, चैतन्ये प्रमाशब्दप्रवृत्तौ विषयाकारवृत्तेरुपाधित्वात्तस्या वृत्तेरिन्द्रियजन्यत्वात्तादृशवृत्त्युपहितप्रमां प्रत्यपीन्द्रियस्य साधनत्वव्यवहारः ।
To explain: because the designation of pramā does not occur with respect to unconditioned consciousness, but only with respect to consciousness conditioned by an object-shaped vṛtti, and because that object-shaped vṛtti serves as the conditioning adjunct (upādhi) in applying the word pramā to consciousness, and because that vṛtti is produced by sense organs, the sense organ is conventionally treated as the instrument even with respect to pramā conditioned by such a vṛtti.
इत्थमेव इन्द्रियं प्रमासाधनं इति व्यवह्रियते ।
In this very manner, the sense organ is conventionally spoken of as the instrument of pramā.
न ह्यन्तःकरणपरिणामाः सर्वेऽपि प्रमात्वेन व्यवह्रियन्ते ।
For not all transformations of the internal organ are designated as pramā.
किन्तु शरीरान्तःस्थमन्तःकरणं विषयरूपघटादिदेशपर्यन्तं दीर्घीभावापत्तिरूपं परिणामं प्राप्नोति, स परिणाम एव प्रमाणं इत्युच्यते ।
Rather, the internal organ situated inside the body undergoes a transformation in the form of elongation reaching up to the locus of the object such as a pot; that transformation itself is called pramāṇa.
विषयैः सह मिलितस्यान्तःकरणस्य विषयसमानाकारो यः परिणामस्तस्य प्रमेति व्यपदेशः ।
The transformation of the internal organ which has united with the object, assuming the identical shape of the object, receives the designation of pramā.
शरीरान्तःस्थितान्तःकरणदेशमारभ्य घटादिविषयदेशपर्यन्तं दीर्घीभूतस्यान्तःकरणस्य परिणामः प्रमारूपतां धत्ते ।
The modification of the internal organ elongated from the location of the mind inside the body up to the location of the object such as a pot assumes the form of pramā.
तस्मात्प्रमायाः प्रमाणरूपान्तःकरणवृत्तेश्च नाधिको भेदोऽस्ति ।
Therefore, there is no significant difference between pramā and the mental modification in the form of pramāṇa.
अनेन क्रमेण बाह्यपदार्थानां प्रत्यक्षज्ञानोत्पत्तिदशायामन्तःकरणवृत्तिर्बहिर्निर्गत्य विषयीभूतघटादिसमानाकारतां धत्ते ।
In this order, at the time of the arising of perceptual knowledge of external objects, the mental modification goes outside and assumes the identical shape of the objectified pot and so on.
शरीरान्तःस्थात्मनः प्रत्यक्षकाले त्वन्तःकरणवृत्तिर्बहिर्निर्गमनं विना शरीरस्यान्तरेवात्माकारतां धत्ते ।
However, at the time of the direct perception of the ātman residing inside the body, the mental modification assumes the form of the ātman right inside the body without issuing outside.
तया आत्माकारया वृत्त्या आत्माश्रितमावरणं निवर्त्यते ।
By that modification having the form of the ātman, the concealing veil resting on the ātman is removed.
आत्मा स्वस्य प्रकाशेन वृत्तौ प्रकाशते ।
The ātman shines in the modification through its own light.
अनेनैव निमित्तेनात्मा वृत्तेर्विषय इत्युच्यते ।
For this reason alone, the ātman is said to be the object of the vṛtti.
वृत्तिस्थचिदाभासरूपफलस्य त्वात्मा न विषयो भवति ।
The ātman, however, does not become the object of the result (phala) consisting of the reflected consciousness (cidābhāsa) present in the vṛtti.
वर्णितेन प्रकारेण साक्षिरूप आत्मा स्वयम्प्रकाशरूपो भातीति सिद्ध्यति ।
In the manner described, it is established that the ātman, as the witness (sākṣin), shines as self-luminous.
ज्ञानस्य कथं प्रत्यक्षतेति तत्त्वदृष्टिप्रश्नः-
'How is knowledge perceptual?' — this is the question raised by Tattvadṛṣṭi:
इन्द्रियसम्बन्धं विना ``अहं ब्रह्म'' इति॥ २१९–२२३ ॥
219 · तत्त्वदृष्टेः शङ्का
ब्रह्मापरोक्षज्ञानेन सकलाविद्यासमूहो नश्यति, न तु परोक्षज्ञानेन इति प्रागभिहितम् ।
It was stated earlier that 'by the direct knowledge of Brahman the entire mass of avidyā is destroyed, not by indirect knowledge.'
अत्रैषा शङ्का भवति इन्द्रियजन्यमेव ज्ञानं प्रत्यक्षमित्युच्यते, ब्रह्मज्ञानं तु नेन्द्रियजन्यमविषयत्वाद्ब्रह्मणः ।
Here this doubt arises: 'Only knowledge produced by sense organs is called perceptual; however, the knowledge of Brahman is not produced by sense organs, because Brahman is not an object.'
यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते अप्राप्य मनसा सह (तै. ब्र. ४.९) इत्यादिश्रुतेः ।
Due to such śruti texts as: 'Whence words return along with the mind, without attaining It' (Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 4.9).
ब्रह्म न ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणां विषयः॥ २२०–२२२ ॥
220 · ब्रह्म न चक्षुषो विषयः
रूपवतः पदार्थस्य अथवा नीलादिवर्णस्यैव ज्ञानं चक्षुषा जन्यते ।
Knowledge is produced by the eye only of an object possessing form, or of colour such as blue.
ब्रह्म तु न तादृशम् ; अतो न ब्रह्म नेत्रेन्द्रियजन्यज्ञानविषयः ।
Brahman, however, is not of such a nature; therefore Brahman is not an object of knowledge produced by the visual sense-organ.
मनुष्याकारेणावतीर्णानां रामकृष्णादीनां मूर्तयो यद्यपि रूपादिमत्यस्तथापि ता मूर्तयो मायिकत्वान्मिथ्या ।
Although the forms of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others who descended in human form possess form and colour, nevertheless those forms are illusory (*mithyā*) because they are products of *māyā*.
अतो न ता मूर्तयो ब्रह्मरूपाः ।
Hence those forms are not identical with Brahman.
यद्यपि पुराणादिषु रामकृष्णादीनां ब्रह्मरूपेण वर्णनमस्ति तथापि तद्वचनं न तदीयशरीरस्य ब्रह्मत्वबुद्ध्या प्रवृत्तं किन्तु तदीयशरीराधिष्ठानचैतन्यस्य ब्रह्मत्वबुद्ध्येति ज्ञेयम् ।
Although there is a description in the Purāṇas and elsewhere of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others as Brahman, nevertheless it should be understood that those statements do not proceed from viewing their physical bodies as Brahman, but rather from viewing the consciousness (*caitanya*) that is the substratum of their bodies as Brahman.
ननु मनुष्यपशुपक्ष्यादिसर्वशरीराणामप्यधिष्ठानं ब्रह्मचैतन्यमेव ।
[Objection]: But Brahman-consciousness alone is the substratum of all bodies of humans, beasts, birds, and so on as well.
अधिष्ठानचैतन्याभिप्रायेण रामकृष्णादीनां ब्रह्मत्वे सर्वशरीराणामपि ब्रह्मचैतन्यस्यैवाधिष्ठानत्वान्मनुष्यपशुपक्ष्यादयोऽपि ब्रह्मरूपा भवेयुः ।
If Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others are Brahman only with reference to the underlying substratum-consciousness, then since Brahman-consciousness alone is the substratum of all bodies, humans, beasts, birds, etc., would also be Brahman.
तथा च पश्वादिसमा एव रामकृष्णादयोऽपि भवेयुः ।
And thus Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others would be just equal to animals and the like.
तस्माद्रामकृष्णादीनां जीवान्तरापेक्षया वैशिष्ट्यसिद्धये तदीयशरीरे एव ब्रह्मबुद्धिरुचिता, न तु तदीयशरीराधिष्ठानचैतन्यदृष्ट्या तेषु ब्रह्मबुद्धिरिति चेत् ।
Therefore, in order to establish the distinction of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others over other *jīvas*, the cognition of Brahman is proper only with regard to their body itself, and not viewing them as Brahman from the standpoint of the substratum-consciousness of their body — if this is contended:
तन्न ।
That is not so.
शरीरं बाधित्वा रामकृष्णादिशरीराणां ब्रह्मत्वविवक्षणे पश्वादिशरीराणामपि बाधपूर्वं ब्रह्मत्वं सिद्ध्येत् ।
If it is intended that the bodies of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others are Brahman by sublating the body, then identity with Brahman would also be established for the bodies of beasts and the like upon sublation.
बाधाभावे तु जीवान्तराणां शरीरवत् करचरणाद्यवयवसहितस्य रूपक्रियादियुक्तस्य रामकृष्णादेः शरीरस्य निरवयवत्वेन रूपक्रियादिशून्येन ब्रह्मणा सहाभेदो न घटेत ।
On the other hand, in the absence of sublation, just like the body of other *jīvas*, the non-difference of the body of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, etc.—which possesses parts such as hands and feet and is endowed with form and action—with Brahman, which is partless and devoid of form and action, cannot be tenable.
तस्मात्सावयवं रूपक्रियादियुक्तं रामकृष्णादेः शरीरं न ब्रह्म ।
Therefore, the body of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, etc., which has parts and is endowed with form and action, is not Brahman.
परन्त्वियान् भेदोऽस्ति - जीवानां शरीरं पुण्यपापाधीनं भूतकार्यं च ।
However, there is this distinction: the body of *jīvas* is dependent on merit and demerit (*puṇya* and *pāpa*) and is a product of the five elements.
किञ्च जीवानां देहाद्यनात्मपदार्थेष्वविद्याबलात् अहम्, मम इत्यध्यासो भवति, स चाध्यास आचार्योपदेशान्निवर्तते ।
Furthermore, in the case of *jīvas*, due to the power of *avidyā*, there occurs superimposition (*adhyāsa*) in non-Self objects such as the body in the form of 'I' and 'mine', and that superimposition ceases through the instruction of the teacher.
रामकृष्णादीनां शरीरं तु न तदीयपुण्यपापजन्यं नापि भौतिकम् ।
The body of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others, however, is neither born of their merit or demerit, nor is it elemental (*bhautika*).
परन्तु सृष्टेः प्राक् यदा प्राणिनां कर्म फलदानोन्मुखं भवति तदा आप्तकामस्यापीश्वरस्य प्राणिनां कर्मानुसारेण अहं जगत्सृजेयम् इति सङ्कल्पो जायते ।
Rather, prior to creation, when the karma of living beings becomes ready to yield its fruit, then even for Īśvara, whose desires are fully accomplished, there arises in accordance with the karma of beings the resolve: 'May I create the world.'
तेन सङ्कल्पेन जगदुत्पत्तिरूपा सृष्टिर्भवति ।
By that resolve, creation in the form of the origination of the world comes into being.
तथैव सृष्टेः परमपि अहं जगत्पालयेयम् इतीश्वरस्य सङ्कल्पो जायते ।
Just so, after creation as well, there arises the resolve of Īśvara: 'May I sustain the world.'
तेन सङ्कल्पेन जगद्रक्ष्यते ।
By that resolve, the world is sustained.
कर्मानुसारेण सुखदुःखादिसम्बन्ध एव पालनं इत्युच्यते ।
Connecting beings with pleasure, pain, and so forth according to their karma is what is called sustenance.
पालनसङ्कल्पमध्ये उपासकानामुपासनफलत्वेन रामकृष्णादिनामसहिता मूर्तयः सर्वेषां प्रतीयन्ताम् इति चेश्वरस्य सङ्कल्पो भवति ।
Within that resolve to sustain, as the fruit of the devotees' worship, there also arises Īśvara's resolve: 'May divine forms endowed with names such as Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others appear to all.'
अनेनेश्वरसङ्कल्पेन नामरूपादिरहिते ईश्वरे रामकृष्णादिनामानि पीताम्बरादिसहितसुन्दरविग्रहाश्चोत्पद्यन्ते ।
By this resolve of Īśvara, names such as Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, etc., and beautiful bodily forms adorned with yellow silks and ornaments appear in Īśvara, who is inherently devoid of name and form.
न ते रामकृष्णादीनां विग्रहास्तदीयकर्माधीनाः ।
Those bodily forms of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others are not dependent on any individual karma of their own.
तैश्च रामकृष्णादिविग्रहैः साधूनां सुखं दुष्टानां दुःखं चोत्पद्यते ।
And through those forms of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others, happiness is generated for the righteous and misery for the wicked.
यच्छरीरं यस्य सुखदुःखादेर्हेतुर्भवति तच्छरीरं तदीयपुण्यपापजन्यमिति न्यायः ।
Such is the maxim: whichever body becomes the cause of someone's happiness or misery, that body is born of their respective merit or demerit.
अनेन न्यायेन रामकृष्णादीनां शरीरं साधूनां सुखहेतुत्वात्साधूनां पुण्यपुञ्जफलम्, असुरादीनां दुष्टानां दुःखहेतुत्वात्तेषां पापफलं च भवति ।
By this reasoning, the body of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others is the fruit of the accumulated merits of the virtuous, since it causes happiness to the virtuous; and it is the fruit of the sins of the wicked, such as the asuras, since it causes misery to them.
एवमवतारपुरुषशरीरस्यापि पुण्यपापाधीनत्वात्तदनधीनत्वोक्तिरसङ्गतेति चेत् ।
If it is objected that since the body of an *avatāra* is thus also dependent on *puṇya* and *pāpa*, the assertion that it is independent of them is invalid;
अत्रेदं तत्त्वं - जीवेन पूर्वशरीरे कृतपुण्यपापयोः फलमुत्तरशरीरे तस्यैव जीवस्य सुखदुःखादिरूपं भवति ।
Here is the exact truth: the fruit of the merit and sin performed by a *jīva* in a prior body manifests in a subsequent body in the form of pleasure, pain, and the like experienced by that very *jīva*.
तस्माच्छरीराभिमानवतो जीवस्य पूर्वजन्मनि स्वेनैव कृतपुण्यपापयोरधीनमुत्तरशरीरमित्युच्यते ।
Therefore, for a *jīva* possessing identification with the body, the subsequent body is said to be dependent upon the merit and sin performed by itself in a previous birth.
रामकृष्णाद्यवतारपुरुषशरीरं तु साध्वसाधुजनसुखदुःखहेतुत्वात्साध्वसाधुजनकृतपुण्यपापाधीनमेव, न तु रामकृष्णादिपुण्यपापाधीनम् ।
However, the body of an *avatāra* such as Rāma and Kṛṣṇa is dependent only upon the merits and sins performed by virtuous and wicked persons, since it is the cause of their pleasure and pain; it is not at all dependent upon merits or sins of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, etc.
अत एव न तेन शरीरेण रामकृष्णादीनां सुखदुःखभोगः ।
For this very reason, there is no experience of pleasure and pain for Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others through that body.
तस्माद्रामकृष्णाद्यवतारपुरुषशरीरं तदीयपुण्यपापाद्यधीनं नेति सिद्धम् ।
Therefore, it is established that the body of an *avatāra* persona such as Rāma and Kṛṣṇa is not dependent upon their own *puṇya*, *pāpa*, etc.
किञ्च रामकृष्णादिशरीरं न पञ्चभूतपरिणामः, किन्तु चैतन्याश्रितमायापरिणामः ।
Furthermore, the body of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, etc., is not a modification of the five elements, but rather a modification of *māyā* seated in Pure Consciousness (*caitanya*).
पञ्चीकृतभूतपरिणामत्वे कृष्णशरीरस्य रज्जुकृतबन्धनाविषयत्वं भागवतादिषु वर्णितमसङ्गतं भवेत् ।
Were it a modification of the quintuplicated elements, the description in the *Bhāgavata* and other scriptures of Kṛṣṇa's body being incapable of being bound by ropes would become untenable.
यद्यपि पञ्चभूतकार्ययोगिशरीरस्यापि बन्धनाविषयत्वं दृश्यते, तथापि योगिशरीरं प्रथमं बन्धनविषयतामापद्यैव पश्चाद्योगमहिम्ना बन्धाद्विमुक्तं भवति ।
Although the body of a yogin, which is also an effect of the five elements, is seen to be beyond binding, nevertheless the yogin's body first falls under binding and only subsequently becomes freed from bondage through the power of yoga.
कृष्णादिशरीरं तु न योगिशरीरवद्योगमहिम्ना बन्धाविषयतां याति; किन्तु स्वभावत एव बन्धाद्यवशम् ।
The body of Kṛṣṇa and others, however, does not attain immunity to binding through the power of yoga like a yogin's body; rather, by its very nature it is not subject to binding and the like.
तस्मान्नावतारपुरुषशरीरं पञ्चभूतपरिणामः ।
Therefore, the body of an *avatāra* is not a modification of the five elements.
भगवत्पादकृतमाण्डूक्योपनिषद्भाष्यस्य टीकायामानन्दगिरिस्वामिभिः रामादिशरीरस्य भूतपरिणामत्वं यदुक्तं तदपि स्थूलदृष्टीनामितरशरीरतुल्यतयैवावतारपुरुषशरीरमपि प्रतीयते इत्यभिप्रायेणेति मन्तव्यम् ।
Whatever statement was made by Svāmin Ānandagiri in the sub-commentary on Bhagavatpāda's *Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad Bhāṣya* asserting that the bodies of Rāma and others are modifications of elements must also be understood as having been made with the intention that to those of gross vision, the *avatāra*'s body merely appears similar to other ordinary bodies.
अत एव भगवत्पादैर्गीताभाष्योपक्रमे स च भगवान् स्वां मायां वशीकृत्याजोऽव्ययोऽपि सन् स्वमायया देहवानिव जात इव च लोकानुग्रहं कुर्वन्निव लक्ष्यते इति जगतः स्थितिं परिपिपालयिषुः स आदिकर्ता विष्णुर्देवक्यां वसुदेवादंशेन कृष्णः किल सम्बभूव इति च कृष्णशरीरं मायाकार्यत्वेन वर्णितम् ।
For this very reason, in the introduction to the *Gītā Bhāṣya*, Bhagavatpāda described Kṛṣṇa's body as a product of *māyā*, stating: And that Lord, keeping His own māyā under control, though unborn and imperishable, appears through His own māyā as if embodied, as if born, and as if bestowing grace upon the world and Desirous of preserving the order of the universe, that primal Creator Viṣṇu was born as Kṛṣṇa from Vasudeva in Devakī through a portion of Himself.
तस्मान्न भूतेभ्योऽवतारपुरुषशरीरमुत्पद्यते ।
Therefore, the body of an *avatāra* is not produced from the elements.
किन्तु तदुपादानकारणं साक्षान्मायैव ।
Rather, its material cause is directly *māyā* itself.
इतरेषां जीवानां देहे अहम् इत्यात्मभ्रान्तिरस्ति ।
Other *jīvas* possess the illusion of Selfhood in the body, thinking 'I am the body'.
रामकृष्णादीनां तु न सा भ्रान्तिरस्ति ।
For Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others, however, that delusion does not exist.
जीवस्योपाधिभूता अविद्या मलिनसत्त्वयुक्ता; रामकृष्णादीनामुपाधिभूता माया तु शुद्धसत्त्वयुता ।
The *avidyā* that serves as the limiting adjunct (*upādhi*) of the *jīva* is endowed with impure *sattva*; the *māyā* that serves as the limiting adjunct of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, etc., however, is endowed with pure *sattva*.
तस्माज्जीवस्याविद्याकार्यभूता भ्रान्तिः, रामकृष्णादेर्मायाकार्यभूतसर्वज्ञत्वं चास्ति ।
Therefore, the *jīva* has delusion which is the product of *avidyā*, while Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others have omniscience which is the product of *māyā*.
जीवस्याज्ञानप्रयुक्तावरणभ्रान्त्योर्निवृत्तये आचार्यमुखान्महावाक्योपदेशजन्यज्ञानमपेक्षितम् ।
For the removal of the veiling (*āvaraṇa*) and delusion caused by ignorance, knowledge generated from the Guru's instruction on the *mahāvākya*s is required for the *jīva*.
रामकृष्णादेरावरणभ्रान्त्योरभावेनोपदेशजन्यज्ञानं नापेक्षितम् ।
For Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others, because of the absence of veiling and delusion, knowledge born of instruction is not required.
तथापि जीवस्यान्तःकरणवृत्तिरूपज्ञानमिवेश्वरस्य मायावृत्तिरूपात्मज्ञानमुपदेशं विनैव जायते ।
Even so, just as the knowledge of a *jīva* is in the form of an *antaḥkaraṇa-vṛtti*, Īśvara's Self-knowledge in the form of a *māyā-vṛtti* arises even without any instruction.
किन्तु न तेन ज्ञानेन प्रयोजनमीश्वराणां सिद्ध्यति ।
However, no novel objective is accomplished for Īśvara through that knowledge.
तथा हि, जीवस्य घटादिज्ञानेनावरणभङ्गो घटादिरूपविषयस्य प्रकाशश्चेति फलं सिद्ध्यति ।
To explain: for the *jīva*, through the knowledge of a pot, etc., the result achieved is twofold: the removal of the veil (*āvaraṇa-bhaṅga*) and the illumination of the object in the form of the pot, etc.
जीवस्य अहं ब्रह्म इति ब्रह्माकारात्मज्ञानोदये तु तादृशज्ञानविषयीभूतस्यात्मन आवरणभङ्गमात्रं ज्ञानेन जन्यते ।
When the *jīva* attains the Self-knowledge taking the form of Brahman as 'I am Brahman', however, only the destruction of the veil covering the *ātman* (which is the object of such knowledge) is produced by that knowledge.
आत्मरूपो विषयस्तु स्वयमेव प्रकाशते ।
The object, which is of the nature of the *ātman*, shines entirely by Itself (as it is self-luminous).
तस्मादात्मज्ञानेन विषयो न प्रकाशते ।
Therefore, an object is not illumined by knowledge of the Ātman.
एवमीश्वरस्य अहं ब्रह्मास्मि इति मायावृत्तिरूपज्ञानस्य विषयभूतः ईश्वरस्यात्मा आवरणरहितस्वयम्प्रकाशस्वरूपोऽस्ति ।
Thus, the Ātman of Īśvara, which is the object of the knowledge in the form of a māyā-vṛtti 'I am Brahman', is of the nature of self-luminous reality free from concealment.
तस्मादावरणभङ्गो वा विषयप्रकाशो वा नेश्वरज्ञानस्य प्रयोजनम् ।
Therefore, neither the destruction of the veil nor the illumination of the object is the purpose of Īśvara's knowledge.
यथा जीवन्मुक्तस्य विदुष आवरणरहितमात्मानं विषयीकुर्वन्ती अहं ब्रह्मास्मि इत्यन्तःकरणवृत्तिरावरणभङ्गादिप्रयोजनशून्या भवति, तथैवेश्वरस्यापि आवरणभङ्गादिप्रयोजनशून्यं मायावृत्तिरूपं अहं ब्रह्मास्मि इति ज्ञानं विनैवोपदेशादिसाधनमुत्पद्यते ।
Just as the mental mode 'I am Brahman' in an enlightened jīvanmukta, taking the unveiled Ātman as its object, is devoid of any purpose such as veil-destruction, in the very same way, in Īśvara also, the knowledge 'I am Brahman' in the form of a māyā-vṛtti, devoid of any purpose such as veil-destruction, arises even without means such as instruction.
इत्थं रामकृष्णादीनां जीवाद्वैशिष्ट्यसत्वेनेश्वरत्वं सिद्ध्यति ।
In this manner, due to their distinction from the jīva, the state of being Īśvara is established for incarnations like Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and others.
तथापि तेषां शरीरं मायाकार्यम् ।
Even so, their physical form is a product of māyā.
अत एव न तद्ब्रह्मरूपम्, किन्तु मिथ्या ।
Hence, it is not of the nature of Brahman, but rather illusory (*mithyā*).
मायाकार्यभूतमवतारपुरुषाणां शरीरं करचरणाद्यवयवोपेतं रूपसहितं चोत्पादितम् ।
The body of the divine incarnations, which is a product of māyā, is created endowed with limbs like hands and feet and possessing visible form.
तस्मात्तेषां शरीरं नेत्रेन्द्रियविषयतामापद्यते ।
Therefore, their body becomes an object of the sense of sight.
तथापि नेत्रेन्द्रियं न ब्रह्म विषयीकरोति ।
Even so, the organ of vision does not make Brahman its object.
221 · ब्रह्म त्वगिन्द्रियस्य न विषयः
त्वगिन्द्रियं तु स्पर्शं तदाश्रयद्रव्यं च विषयीकरोति ।
The tactile organ, however, takes touch and the substance which is its substratum as its object.
ब्रह्म तु न स्पर्शरूपं नापि स्पर्शस्याश्रयः ।
Brahman, however, is neither of the nature of touch, nor is It the locus of touch.
अतो न ब्रह्मणोस्त्वगिन्द्रियविषयत्वम् ।
Therefore, Brahman is not an object of the tactile organ.
222 · ब्रह्म न रसनाघ्राणश्रोत्राणां विषयः
रसनेन्द्रियेण रसज्ञानम्, घ्राणेन्द्रियेण गन्धज्ञानम्, श्रोत्रेन्द्रियेण शब्दज्ञानं च जायते ।
Through the sense of taste arises the knowledge of taste, through the sense of smell arises the knowledge of smell, and through the sense of hearing arises the knowledge of sound.
रसगन्धशब्देभ्यो विलक्षणं ब्रह्म ।
Brahman is distinct from taste, smell, and sound.
तस्मान्न रसनाघ्राणश्रोत्रैर्ब्रह्मणो ज्ञानं जायते ।
Therefore, knowledge of Brahman does not arise through the organs of taste, smell, and hearing.
अशब्दमस्पर्शमरूपमव्ययं तथारसं नित्यमगन्धवच्च यत् (क. १.३.१५) पराञ्चि खानि व्यतृणत्स्वयम्भूस्तस्मात्पराङ्पश्यति नान्तरात्मन् (क. २.१.१) इत्यादिना ब्रह्मण इन्द्रियाविषयत्वं बोध्यते ।
By passages such as 'That which is soundless, touchless, formless, undecaying, likewise tasteless, eternal, and odourless...' (Kaṭha 1.3.15) and 'The Self-existent pierced the senses outwards, therefore one looks outward and not at the inner Self...' (Kaṭha 2.1.1), Brahman's non-objecthood to the senses is taught.
223 · ब्रह्म कर्मेन्द्रियाणामप्यविषयः
कर्मेन्द्रियं न ज्ञानसाधनम्, किन्तु वचनादिक्रियासाधनम् ।
An organ of action is not an instrument of knowledge, but an instrument of activities such as speaking.
तस्मात्कर्मेन्द्रियैर्न कस्यचिदपि ज्ञानं जायते ।
Therefore, knowledge of anything whatsoever does not arise through the organs of action.
इत्थं न केनापीन्द्रियेण ब्रह्मणो ज्ञानं जायते ।
Thus, knowledge of Brahman does not arise through any sense organ at all.
इन्द्रियजन्यमेव ज्ञानं प्रत्यक्षं इत्युच्यते ।
Only knowledge produced by the senses is called perception (pratyakṣa).
तदेवापरोक्षं इति च कीर्त्यते ।
And that alone is designated as immediate (aparokṣa).
तस्माद्ब्रह्मणोऽपरोक्षज्ञानं नैव सम्भवति ।
Therefore, direct knowledge (*aparokṣajñāna*) of Brahman is not possible at all.
शब्देन तु यद्यपि ब्रह्मज्ञानमुत्पद्यते तथापि शाब्दज्ञानस्य परोक्षत्वाच्छब्दजन्यब्रह्मज्ञानं परोक्षं एव भवेत् ।
Even though knowledge of Brahman arises through verbal testimony (*śabda*), nevertheless, because verbal cognition is mediate (*parokṣa*), the knowledge of Brahman born of words would only be mediate.
पूर्वोक्तप्रश्नस्योत्तरम्॥ २२४–२२५ ॥
224
सुखदुःखादेः साक्षिभास्यत्वाद् इन्द्रियसम्बन्धं विना प्रत्यक्षज्ञानं न जायते इति नियमो नास्ति - इन्द्रियसम्बन्धं विना प्रत्यक्षज्ञानं नोदेतीति नियमो नास्ति ।
Because pleasure, pain, and the like are directly illumined by the *sākṣin*, there is no such invariable rule that perceptual knowledge cannot arise without contact with a sense organ — that is, there is no rule that perceptual cognition never arises without sense-organ contact.
सुखदुःखादेर्ज्ञानं न केनापीन्द्रियेण जन्यते, तथापि सुखदुःखादेर्ज्ञानं प्रत्यक्षमेव ।
The cognition of pleasure, pain, and the like is not generated by any sense organ whatsoever; nevertheless, the cognition of pleasure, pain, and so forth is direct perception (*pratyakṣa*) indeed.
तस्मादिन्द्रियसम्बन्धजन्यं ज्ञानमेव प्रत्यक्षज्ञानमिति न नियमः ।
Therefore, there is no such rule that only cognition generated by contact with an organ of sense is perceptual knowledge.
किन्तु यदा विषयेण वृत्तिः सम्बद्धा विषयाकारा भवति तदा प्रत्यक्षज्ञानं जायत इत्युच्यते ।
Rather, when the *vṛtti* (mental modification) is connected with the object and assumes the form of that object, then perceptual knowledge is said to arise.
विषयेण सह वृत्तेः सम्बन्धः1,1,2
The connection of the *vṛtti* with the object...
टिप्पणी
1.
विषयावच्छिन्नचैतन्यस्य वृत्त्यवच्छिन्नचैतन्येनाभेद एव प्रत्यक्षज्ञानलक्षणम् ।
The non-difference of consciousness delimited by the object from consciousness delimited by the mental modification is indeed the definition of perceptual knowledge.
स चाभेदः क्वचिदिन्द्रियद्वारा भवति ।
And that non-difference occurs in some cases through the senses.
क्वचिच्छब्देन भवति ।
In some cases it occurs through verbal testimony.
क्वचिदिन्द्रियादिरूपबाह्यनिमित्तं विनैव शरीरान्तर्जायमानवृत्तिद्वारा भवति ।
In some cases it occurs without any external cause in the form of the sense organs etc., simply through a mental modification arising within the body.
तत्रापि प्रत्यक्षज्ञानमिति व्यपदेशो भवति ।
There also, the designation 'perceptual knowledge' applies.
चैतन्यस्य स्वरूपतो न कोऽपि भेदोऽस्ति ।
In its intrinsic nature, there is no difference whatsoever in Consciousness.
किन्तु विषयवृत्तिरूपोभयोपाधिप्रयुक्तभेदोऽस्ति ।
However, there is a difference conditioned by the two limiting adjuncts in the form of the object and the mental modification.
तयोरुपाध्योर्भिन्नदेशस्थत्वे तादृशोपाधिविशिष्टचैतन्ययोर्भेदव्यवहारो भवति ।
When those two *upādhi*s are situated in different locations, there is the empirical usage of difference between the consciousnesses qualified by such *upādhi*s.
वृत्तेर्विषयाकारताकाले द्वयोरुपाध्योरेकदेशस्थत्वं भवति ।
At the time when the *vṛtti* takes on the form of the object, the two *upādhi*s come to occupy the same location.
तदैकदेशस्थोपाधिसहितविषयचैतन्यवृत्तिचैतन्ययोरभेदो व्यवह्रियते ।
Then, non-difference is spoken of between the object-consciousness and the modification-consciousness, which are accompanied by co-located adjuncts.
एवं विषयचैतन्येन सह वृत्तिचैतन्यस्य जायमानाभेद एव प्रत्यक्षज्ञानं इति, अपरोक्षज्ञानं इति, साक्षात्कार इति चोच्यते ।
Thus, the non-difference that occurs between the *vṛtti*-consciousness and the object-consciousness is called 'perceptual knowledge', 'immediate cognition', and 'direct realization'.
तदिदं प्रत्यक्षज्ञानलक्षणं (१) इन्द्रियजन्यबाह्यघटादिप्रत्यक्षज्ञाने, (२) महावाक्यजन्यब्रह्मप्रत्यक्षज्ञाने, (३) बाह्यनिमित्तं विनान्तरेवोत्पद्यमानसुखदुःखादिप्रत्यक्षज्ञाने, (४) मायावृत्तिरूपेश्वरज्ञाने, (५) अविद्यावृत्तिरूपरज्जुसर्पादिज्ञाने चानुगतम् ।
This definition of perceptual knowledge applies uniformly to: (1) sense-generated perceptual cognition of external pots, etc., (2) direct perception of Brahman generated by the *mahāvākya*s, (3) direct perception of pleasure, pain, etc. arising internally without external causes, (4) Īśvara's knowledge in the form of *māyā-vṛtti*, and (5) the perception of rope-snake etc. in the form of *avidyā-vṛtti*.
क्वचिदिन्द्रियद्वारा भवति, क्वचिच्च शब्देन भवति ।
In some cases it occurs through the senses, and in some cases through verbal testimony.
दशमस्त्वमसि इत्यत्र शब्दाज्जायमानान्तःकरणवृत्तिर्दशमेन स्वात्मना सम्बद्धा दशमाकारा भवति ।
In the statement 'You are the tenth', the *antaḥkaraṇa-vṛtti* generated by the sentence, being connected with one's own self who is the tenth person, takes the form of the tenth.
तस्माच्छब्दजन्यदशमज्ञानमपि प्रत्यक्षमेव ।
Therefore, even the knowledge of the tenth person produced by verbal testimony is indeed perceptual.
तथैव प्रमातरि सुखदुःखाद्युत्पत्तिकालेऽन्तःकरणस्य वृत्तिः सुखाकारा दुःखाकारा च भवति ।
Likewise, at the time of the arising of pleasure, pain, etc. in the cognizer, the modification of the internal organ assumes the form of pleasure and pain.
तया वृत्त्या सह सुखदुःखादेः सम्बन्धो जायते ।
A connection takes place between pleasure, pain, etc. and that mental modification.
तस्मात्सुखदुःखादेर्ज्ञानं प्रत्यक्षं इत्युच्यते ।
Therefore, the cognition of pleasure, pain, etc. is called perceptual.
पूर्वोक्तोत्पन्नसुखदुःखादेर्नाशानन्तरं यदा पुरुषस्य तादृशसुखदुःखादिज्ञानं जायते तदा सुखदुःखाद्याकारा अन्तःकरणवृत्तिरुदेति ।
After the destruction of the aforementioned pleasure, pain, etc., when a person has cognition of such past pleasure, pain, etc., an *antaḥkaraṇa-vṛtti* taking the form of pleasure, pain, etc. arises.
किन्तु तस्या वृत्तेर्नष्टसुखदुःखादिना सम्बन्धो नास्ति ।
However, that *vṛtti* has no contact with the already destroyed pleasure, pain, etc.
अतस्तज्ज्ञानं स्मृतिरूपम्, न प्रत्यक्षरूपम् ।
Therefore, that cognition is of the nature of memory, not perception.
यद्यप्यन्तःकरणधर्माः सुखदुःखादयः साक्षिभास्यास्तथापि सुखाकारदुःखाकारान्तःकरणवृत्तिद्वारैव साक्षी सुखदुःखादीन् प्रकाशयति ।
Although pleasure, pain, etc., which are attributes of the internal organ, are illumined by the witness (*sākṣi-bhāsya*), nevertheless the witness illuminates pleasure, pain, etc. only through the medium of the *antaḥkaraṇa-vṛtti* taking the form of pleasure and pain.
साक्षिभास्यपदार्थमपि साक्षी वृत्तिमपेक्ष्यैव प्रकाशयति ।
The *sākṣin* illuminates even a *sākṣi-bhāsya* object only by depending upon a *vṛtti*.
तथा हि, शुक्तिरजतं साक्षिभास्यमेव ।
For instance, nacre-silver is indeed directly illumined by the witness.
तत्रापि साक्षी अविद्यावृत्तिं अपेक्ष्यैव रजतं प्रकाशयति ।
There too, the *sākṣin* illuminates the silver only by depending upon an *avidyā-vṛtti*.
परन्तु सुख-दुःखादिप्रकाशने अन्तःकरणवृत्तिः साक्षिणः सहायभूता ।
However, in illuminating pleasure, pain, etc., the *antaḥkaraṇa-vṛtti* acts as an auxiliary to the *sākṣin*.
मिथ्यारजतादिप्रकाशने अविद्यावृत्तिः साक्षिणः सहायभूता ।
In illuminating illusory silver etc., the *avidyā-vṛtti* acts as an auxiliary to the *sākṣin*.
इत्थं साक्षिभास्यपदार्थज्ञानेऽपि वृत्तिरावश्यिकी ।
In this manner, a *vṛtti* is necessary even in the cognition of objects directly illumined by the *sākṣin*.
सा वृत्तिर्यत्रेन्द्रियादिबाह्यसाधनाजन्या तत्र तस्या वृत्तेर्विषयः साक्षिभास्य इत्युच्यते ।
Where that *vṛtti* is not produced by external instruments such as the senses, there the object of that *vṛtti* is called *sākṣi-bhāsya* (directly illumined by the witness).
सुखदुःखादिविषयकवृत्तौ बाह्येन्द्रियादिकं न कारणम् ।
In the mental modification whose object is pleasure, pain, etc., external sense organs and the like are not the cause.
अपि तु सुखाद्युत्पत्तिसमये साधनान्तरापेक्षां विनैव सुखाकारा दुःखाकारा
Rather, at the moment of the arising of pleasure etc., without requiring any other instrument, [the modification arises] taking the form of pleasure and taking the form of pain.
1.
अहं दशमः इति दशमस्य स्वस्वरूपापरोक्षज्ञानं दशमस्त्वमसि इति शब्दप्रमाणजन्यम् ।
The direct realization of one's own identity as 'I am the tenth' on the part of the tenth person is generated by the verbal testimony 'You are the tenth'.
नेन्द्रियैर्मनसा वा दशमप्रत्यक्षज्ञानं जायते ।
The direct perceptual cognition of the tenth does not arise through external sense organs or through the mind.
तथा हि, यदि शरीररूपो दशम इन्द्रियवेद्य इत्युच्यते तर्हि नेत्रेन्द्रियमात्रेण वेद्येत ।
To explain: if it is said that the tenth person, being of bodily form, is knowable through the senses, then he should be knowable solely through the eye.
तथा सति निमीलितनयस्यापि दशमस्त्वमसि इति वाक्याद्दशमज्ञानं जायमानमसङ्गतं भवेत् ।
That being the case, the knowledge of the tenth arising from the sentence 'You are the tenth' even in one who has closed his eyes would become untenable.
तस्माद्दशमज्ञानं नेत्रेण न जायते ।
Therefore, the knowledge of the tenth does not arise through the eye.
मनस्तु न साक्षाद्बाह्यार्थग्रहणसमर्थम् ।
The mind, on the other hand, is not capable of directly apprehending external objects on its own.
आन्तरमेव पदार्थं मनः साक्षात् गृह्णीयात् ।
The mind can directly grasp only internal objects.
देवदत्तयज्ञदत्तादिसंज्ञा अपि सूक्ष्मदेहसहितस्थूलदेहे दृश्यन्ते ।
Designations such as Devadatta and Yajñadatta are applied to the physical gross body conjoined with the subtle body.
त्वम्, अहम् इत्यादिव्यवहारोऽपि स्थूलदेहे दृश्यते ।
Conventional usages such as 'you' and 'I' are also applied with reference to the gross body.
स्थूलदेहस्य ज्ञानं मनसा साक्षान्न सम्भवति ।
Direct perception of the gross body through the mind alone is not possible.
तस्माद्दशमज्ञानं शब्दप्रमाणेनैव जायते ।
Therefore, the knowledge of the tenth arises only through the verbal testimony.
तत्र नेत्रं मनश्च सहायतां प्रतिपद्येते ।
In that process, the eye and the mind merely render auxiliary assistance.
2.
सुखदुःखादयो बुद्धेरेव धर्माः, नात्मनः ।
Pleasure, pain, and the like are attributes of the intellect alone, not of the *ātman*.
अत एव ते बुद्धेः सत्त्वे जाग्रत्स्वप्नयोरेव प्रतीयन्ते ।
That is precisely why they are perceived only in the waking and dream states, when the intellect is present.
सुषुप्ते बुद्धेरभावात्सुखदुःखादिप्रतीतिर्नास्ति ।
In deep sleep, due to the absence of the intellect, there is no perception of pleasure, pain, and the like.
तथा चोक्तम् रागेच्छासुखदुःखादि बुद्धौ सत्यां प्रवर्तते । सुषुप्तौ नास्ति तन्नाशे तस्माद्बुद्धेस्तु नात्मनः (उ.सा. पद. १५.१३) इति ।
And so it has been said: 'Attachment, desire, pleasure, pain, and the like manifest when the intellect is present; in deep sleep, upon its cessation, they do not exist; therefore they belong to the intellect, not to the *ātman*' (Upadeśasāhasrī Padya 15.13).
च अन्तःकरणवृत्तिर्जायते ।
And a *vṛtti* (mental modification) of the inner instrument arises.
तस्यां वृत्तावारूढः साक्षी सुखदुःखादीन् प्रकाशयति ।
Reflected in that mental modification, the *sākṣin* (witness-consciousness) illumines pleasure, pain, and the rest.
अतः सुखदुःखादिकं साक्षिभास्यं इत्युच्यते ।
Therefore, pleasure, pain, and the like are said to be directly illumined by the *sākṣin* (*sākṣibhāsya*).
225 · ब्रह्मज्ञानस्य प्रत्यक्षत्वोपपत्तिः तत्त्वदृष्टेर्भेदभ्रमनिवृत्तिश्च
बाह्यघटादिभिः सहान्तःकरणवृत्तेः सम्बन्धो नेत्रादीन्द्रियद्वारा जायत इति घटादयो न साक्षिभास्याः ।
Because the contact of the mental modification (*antaḥkaraṇa-vṛtti*) with external objects like a pot occurs through sense organs such as the eyes, pots and the like are not directly illumined by the witness (*sākṣi-bhāsya*).
अन्तःकरणवृत्तिर्यदा ब्रह्माकारा भवति तदा सा वृत्तिर्न बहिर्गच्छति, किन्तु शरीरस्यान्तरेव वर्तते ।
When the mental modification assumes the form of *Brahman*, that *vṛtti* does not go outside, but remains inside the body itself.
तया वृत्त्या सह ब्रह्मणः सम्बन्धोऽस्ति ।
There is a connection between *Brahman* and that *vṛtti*.
तस्माद्ब्रह्मज्ञानमपि सुखदुःखादिज्ञानमिव प्रत्यक्षरूपं भवति ।
Therefore, the knowledge of *Brahman* also is of the nature of direct perception (*pratyakṣa*), just like the knowledge of pleasure, pain, and the like.
परन्तु सुखाकारदुःखाकारवृत्तिषु बाह्यसाधनापेक्षा नास्ति ।
However, in modifications taking the forms of pleasure and pain, there is no requirement for external means.
तस्मात्सुखदुःखादयः साक्षिभास्याः ।
Therefore, pleasure, pain, and so on are directly illumined by the witness (*sākṣi-bhāsya*).
ब्रह्माकारान्तःकरणवृत्तौ तु गुरुमुखाच्छ्रुतवेदान्तवाक्यस्य श्रोत्रेन्द्रियसम्बन्धरूपबाह्यसाधनमपेक्ष्यते ।
In the mental modification taking the form of *Brahman*, however, an external means is required, consisting of the contact of the auditory sense with the *Vedānta* statement heard from the mouth of the Guru.
तस्माद्ब्रह्म न साक्षिभास्यम् ।
Therefore, *Brahman* is not directly illumined by the witness (*sākṣi-bhāsya*).
इत्थं यत्र विषयेण सह वृत्तिः सम्बद्धा भवति तत्र प्रत्यक्षज्ञानं भवति ।
In this way, wherever the *vṛtti* is connected with the object, direct knowledge (*pratyakṣa-jñāna*) occurs there.
अहं ब्रह्मास्मि इति वृत्तेः विषयेण ब्रह्मणा सह सम्बद्धत्वात् ब्रह्मज्ञानं प्रत्यक्षं भवितुमर्हति ।
Because the modification 'I am *Brahman*' is connected with its object, *Brahman*, the knowledge of *Brahman* is fittingly direct perception (*pratyakṣa*).
यत्र धूमदर्शनेन 1वह्निज्ञानं जायते तत्र धूमज्ञानं प्रत्यक्षम्, वह्निज्ञानं तु न प्रत्यक्षम् ।
Where knowledge of fire arises through the seeing of smoke, there the knowledge of smoke is direct perception, but the knowledge of fire is not direct perception.
चक्षुर्द्वारा निर्गतान्तःकरणवृत्तेर्धूमेन सह सम्बन्धोऽस्ति; अतो धूम2,1
There is a connection of the mental modification, which has issued forth through the eyes, with the smoke; hence smoke...
टिप्पणी
1.
चक्षोः सूर्योऽजायत, आदित्यश्चक्षुर्भूत्वा अक्षिणी प्राविशत् (ऐ. १.२) इत्यादिप्रमाणेन चक्षुषि सूर्याभेदोऽस्ति ।
By authorities such as From the eye the sun was born and The sun, having become the eye, entered the eyes (ऐ. १.२), there is non-difference of the eye with the sun.
अङ्गुल्यादिरूपाल्पावरणेन सूर्यतिरोधाने ब्रह्माण्डान्तर्वर्तिसूर्यस्य प्रकाशो न दृश्यते ।
When the sun is concealed by a tiny obstruction such as a finger, the light of the sun situated within the cosmos is not seen.
आवरणनिवृत्तौ तु चक्षुर्गतान्तःकरणवृत्त्या ब्रह्माण्डान्तर्वर्तिसूर्यस्य प्रकाशो दृश्यते ।
However, upon the removal of the obstruction, the light of the sun situated in the cosmos is perceived through the mental modification proceeding through the eyes.
एवमेव साक्षिरूपे आत्मनि ब्रह्मणोऽभेदोऽस्ति ।
In the very same manner, there is non-difference of *Brahman* in the *ātman* which is of the nature of the witness (*sākṣin*).
तस्यान्तःकरणगताज्ञानांशरूपस्वल्पावरणेनाच्छादने सर्वत्र परिपूर्णं ब्रह्म न प्रत्यक्षतया भासते ।
When it is covered by a slight veil in the form of a portion of ignorance residing in the mind, the all-pervading *Brahman* does not directly shine.
यदा शरीरान्तर्जायमानब्रह्मात्माभेदाकारवृत्त्या पूर्वोक्तावरणस्य भङ्गो जायते, तदा गृहान्तर्गतस्याकाशस्यासङ्गत्वादिज्ञानेन महाकाशस्यासङ्गत्वादिज्ञानोदयवत् सर्वत्र परिपूर्णब्रह्मणः स्वप्रकाशत्वरूपेण भानं भवति ।
When the breaking of the aforementioned veil occurs through the *vṛtti* taking the form of non-difference between *Brahman* and *ātman* arising within the body, then, just as knowing the unattached nature of the space inside a room brings about the knowledge of the unattached nature of the great cosmic space, there occurs the direct illumination of the all-pervading *Brahman* in its nature of self-luminosity.
1.
यस्यान्तःकरणं पूर्वपुण्यपरिपाकवशादत्यन्तं शुद्धमस्ति, यस्य गुरूपदिष्टमहावाक्यरूपशब्दप्रमाणेन सदृढो बोधो जातः, यस्य च तादृशसुदृढबोधोदयानन्तरं संशयादिनिवृत्तये श्रवणादिसाधनान्तरं नापेक्षितं स एवोत्तमाधिकारी ।
He alone is the highest qualified aspirant (*uttamādhikārin*) whose mind is completely purified through the maturation of past merits, who has attained firm knowledge through the verbal testimony of the Mahāvākyas instructed by the Guru, and who, after the rise of such firm knowledge, requires no further means such as *śravaṇa* for the removal of doubts and the like.
यस्य त्वन्तःकरणं नात्यन्तं शुद्धं किन्त्वीषन्मलविक्षेपादिदोषयुक्तम्, स मध्यमाधिकारी; अथवा कनिष्ठाधिकारी ।
However, he whose mind is not completely pure, but rather possessed of slight defects like impurity (*mala*) and distraction (*vikṣepa*), is a middling aspirant (*madhyamādhikārin*) or a lowest aspirant (*kaniṣṭhādhikārin*).
महावाक्यरूपशब्दादपरोक्षज्ञानोदयानन्तरमपि संशयादिनिवृत्तये तेन श्रवणादिकमनुष्ठेयम् ।
Even after the rise of direct knowledge from the word in the form of the Mahāvākya, practices such as *śravaṇa* must be performed by him for the elimination of doubts and the like.
2.
यथा ब्रह्म न साक्षिभास्यं तथा चिदाभाससहितान्तःकरणवृत्तिरूपप्रमातुरप्यगोचरं भवति ।
Just as Brahman is not illuminated by the *sākṣin*, so too it is not an object of the knower (*pramātṛ*) who is of the nature of the mental *vṛtti* imbued with the reflection of consciousness (*cidābhāsa*).
दीपान्तरापेक्षां विना केवलनेत्रस्य यथा दीपो विषयो भवति, तथा ब्रह्म केवलायाः अहं ब्रह्मास्मि इति ब्रह्माकारान्तःकरणवृत्तेर्विषयतां प्रतिपद्यते ।
Just as a lamp becomes an object to the bare eye without requiring another lamp, so too Brahman attains the status of being the object of the bare mental *vṛtti* taking the form of Brahman as 'I am Brahman'.
तस्माद्ब्रह्म न प्रमातृभास्यमपि ।
Therefore, Brahman is not illuminated by the knower (*pramātṛ*) either.
किन्तु स्वप्रकाशं प्रत्यन्यप्रकाशापेक्षारहितसर्वावभासकस्वयम्प्रकाशस्वरूपं ब्रह्म ।
Rather, Brahman is self-luminous by nature, illuminating everything without depending on any other light.
मलेन मलं हन्यात् इति न्यायेन वृत्तिर्ब्रह्मणः आवरणभङ्गं करोति ।
According to the maxim 'one may destroy dirt with dirt', the *vṛtti* effects the destruction of the veil (*āvaraṇa-bhaṅga*) covering Brahman.
सोऽयं वृत्तिप्रयुक्तावरणभङ्ग एव वृत्त्या ब्रह्मणो विषयीकरणमित्युच्यते ।
This very destruction of the veil brought about by the *vṛtti* is called the 'objectification of Brahman by the *vṛtti*'.
न प्रकारान्तरेण वृत्त्या ब्रह्मणो विषयीकरणं सम्भवति ।
In no other way is the objectification of Brahman by the *vṛtti* possible.
साक्षी बाह्यसाधनापेक्षां विनैव अहं ब्रह्मास्मि इति वृत्तिरूपं तत्त्वज्ञानं प्रकाशयति ।
The witness (*sākṣin*) illuminates the knowledge of Truth in the form of the *vṛtti* 'I am Brahman' without requiring any external instruments whatsoever.
अत एव तत्त्वज्ञानं साक्षिभास्यं इत्यभिधीयते ।
For this very reason, knowledge of Truth is said to be 'illuminated by the witness' (*sākṣi-bhāsya*).
ज्ञानं प्रत्यक्षं इत्युच्यते ।
Knowledge is called direct perception (*pratyakṣa*).
लिङ्गज्ञानरूपानुमानप्रमाणजन्यान्तःकरणवृत्तिः शरीरस्यान्तरेव वह्न्याकारं भजते ।
The mental modification generated by the inferential instrument through knowledge of the inferential mark (*liṅga*) takes the form of fire solely within the body.
न हि वृत्तेर्वह्निना सह सम्बन्धोऽस्ति; तस्माद्वह्निज्ञानं न प्रत्यक्षम् ।
For there is no direct contact between the *vṛtti* and the actual fire; therefore the knowledge of fire is not perceptual.
इत्थं यत्र वृत्त्या सह विषयस्य सम्बन्धो भवति तत्र प्रत्यक्षज्ञानं भवति ।
Thus, where there is contact between the *vṛtti* and the object, direct perceptual knowledge occurs.
यत्र वृत्त्या सह विषयस्य सम्बन्धो न भवति तत्र परोक्षज्ञानं भवति ।
Where there is no contact between the *vṛtti* and the object, indirect knowledge (*parokṣa-jñāna*) occurs.
यत्र विषयो देशान्तरस्थो नष्टो भावी वा, तत्रानुमानेन शब्देन वा विषयाकारा वृत्तिः शरीरस्यान्तरेव भवति; तदोत्पद्यमानं ज्ञानं परोक्षं इत्युच्यते ।
Where the object is located in another place, destroyed, or yet to come, the *vṛtti* taking the form of the object arises solely within the body by means of inference or verbal testimony; the knowledge produced at that time is called indirect (*parokṣa*).
इन्द्रियजन्यज्ञानमेव प्रत्यक्षमिति न नियमः ।
There is no invariable rule that direct perceptual knowledge is only knowledge generated by the sense organs.
सुखदुःखादिज्ञानमिन्द्रियजन्यमपि प्रत्यक्षमेव भवति ।
The cognition of pleasure, pain, and the like is also purely perceptual.
दशमपुरुषज्ञानं शब्दजन्यमपि प्रत्यक्षमेव भवति ।
The recognition of the tenth man, though generated by words, is likewise purely direct perception.
अनेन न्यायेन श्रीसद्गुरुमुखाच्छ्रुतमहावाक्यरूपवेदशब्दजन्यब्रह्मज्ञानमपि प्रत्यक्षमेव भवति ।
By this principle, the knowledge of Brahman produced from the Vedic words in the form of the Mahāvākya heard from the mouth of the holy Sadguru is direct perception (*aparokṣa*) alone.
श्रीसद्गुरोरेवंविधमुपदेशं श्रुत्वा बुद्धिमानुत्तमाधिकारी तत्त्वदृष्टिः स्वात्मानं ब्रह्मरूपेण विदित्वा भेदभ्रमं विजहौ ।
Hearing this instruction of the revered Sadguru, the wise and foremost aspirant Tattvadṛṣṭi, realizing his own Self as Brahman, abandoned the delusion of duality.
अहं ब्रह्मास्मि इति वृत्तौ निरावरणं ब्रह्म भाति ।
In the *vṛtti* 'I am Brahman', unveiled Brahman shines forth.
तत्त्वदृष्टिरेवमुवाच ।
Tattvadṛṣṭi spoke thus:
शिष्यःनिरावरणनिर्भासमहं ब्रह्मेति बुद्धवान् । श्रीसद्गुरोः प्रसादेन ह्यखण्डाकारवृत्तितः ॥
'By the grace of the holy Sadguru and through the unbroken, unitary *vṛtti*, I have indeed known myself as Brahman, shining radiant without any veil.'
